title: Rays vs. Yankees Prediction, Odds, Probable Pitchers, Prop Bets for Wednesday, Sept. 23
author: Peter Dewey
body:
The Tampa Bay Rays clinched the AL East in Game 2 of their doubleheader with the New York Yankees on Tuesday, and both teams are locked into their playoff spots heading into Wednesday’s matchup.
Gerrit Cole (3.63 ERA) is on the mound for the Yankees against Tampa Bay lefty Ian Seymour (4.38 ERA), who has worked as both a starter and a reliever this season.
The Yankees are favored at home after splitting yesterday’s doubleheader with a 2-0 win in Game 1 and a 6-1 loss in Game 2. These teams appear to be on a collision course to meet in the ALDS, but the Yankees have to get through the wild card round – and potentially the Boston Red Sox in that round – first.
Meanwhile, the Rays are still playing for the best record in baseball down the stretch of the regular season. They’re just two games back of the Milwaukee Brewers in the win column and have a real shot at a 100-win campaign in 2026.
Can Seymour lead Tampa to an upset win tonight?
Let’s dive into the odds, a player prop to bet and my prediction for this AL East showdown on Sept. 23.

- Cody Bellinger to Hit a Home Run (+553)
In today’s edition of Daily Dinger, I shared why Bellinger is a great bet at home against Seymour and the Rays:
New York Yankees star Cody Bellinger homered in Game 1 of the team’s doubleheader with the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday, and he could have another big game on Wednesday night against left-hander Ian Seymour.
Bellinger is 3-for-5 with a double, a home run and a 2.000 OPS against Seymour in his career, and the star outfielder has been red hot since coming off the injured list earlier in the summer.
Over his last 26 games (25 starts), Bellinger is hitting .305 with five home runs and an .810 OPS. All five of those homers have come in the last 13 games, and the Yankees star is now up to 17 long balls in the 2026 season.
Seymour has struggled to limit home runs, allowing 25 in 127.1 innings of work in 2026. He’s worked as both a reliever and a starter, but the lefty has given up a homer in seven straight outings, allowing 12 homers during that stretch.
Bellinger is an awesome value at +553 in Game 3 of this four-game set.
Rays vs. Yankees Prediction and Pick
The Yankees are actually under .500 (10-11) in Cole’s starts this season, but the former Cy Young award winner has pitched pretty well overall, posting a 3.63 ERA and an expected ERA of 3.84 in his first season since Tommy John surgery.
Cole blanked Tampa Bay across six innings in his first start this season, allowing just two hits in that matchup. He hasn’t been as sharp as of late, seeing his ERA jump half a run in the month of September.
Despite that, I like New York to win this game.
Seymour has some impressive advanced numbers (.3.65 expected ERA, .221 expected BAA), but the Yankees have fared well against southpaws in 2026, ranking eighth in the league in OPs.
In addition to that, Seymour has been shaky over the last two months, posting a 5.11 ERA in his last seven outings. The Rays are 1-6 in those games, and Seymour has allowed at least three runs in six of them.
With the Rays already locking up the division, I’ll take a shot on New York at home, where it is 10 games over .500 this season.
Pick: Yankees Moneyline (-157 at DraftKings)

title: Yankees got their Carlos Rodon answer even as the AL East slipped away
author: Alexander Wilson
body:
Against Tampa Bay, Carlos Rodon gave the Yankees eight scoreless innings with eight strikeouts. That was about as much as a starter can give them against the team that has been keeping them out of first place.
They beat Tampa Bay 2-0 in the first game of Tuesday’s doubleheader. A few hours later, the Rays won 6-1 and clinched the AL East in the Bronx. Both results matter. Rodon’s start showed what this rotation can do in a playoff game; the loss showed why one excellent arm won’t settle the rest of the Yankees’ problems.
There was nothing cheap about those eight innings. Rodon kept Tampa Bay off the board long enough for Cody Bellinger’s two-run homer to stand as the entire margin. David Bednar handled the ninth. For a staff that has spent the year sorting through injuries and changing roles, that is a useful October blueprint.
The Yankees have a real decision behind their ace
Rodon’s 2.67 ERA after the first game is strong enough to make his postseason role a serious conversation. Cam Schlittler has earned the ace label, and Max Fried is still part of the picture. The question is how the Yankees order those starts and what they ask from each pitcher if the Wild Card Series arrives on schedule.
Clarke Schmidt’s return makes that decision more crowded. The rotation questions are already on the table, and Rodon just made his case with the most useful kind of outing: a long one against a division rival.
Rodon also saved the bullpen in the opener. That gets lost when the second game ends with a division celebration in the other clubhouse, but it matters if the Yankees have to play three high-pressure games in five days.
The AL East result still stings
The Yankees are in the postseason. The division title and its first-round bye belong to Tampa Bay, though, and Tuesday made the gap feel obvious. New York scored three runs in two games while its pitchers needed to be close to perfect just to force a split.
Rodon’s outing belongs in any serious October plan. It cannot cover for another quiet night from the lineup. The Yankees got a strong answer from one starter and a reminder that their hitters have less room for silence now.
More about:New York Yankees

title: Yankees Pitcher Responds To Aaron Judge’s ‘Frustrating’ Return To IL After Skipping Rehab
author: Peter Chawaga; Contributor
body:
Aaron Judge's return to the New York Yankees lineup was supposed to provide a major boost heading into the final stretch of the season. Instead, the confounding decision to bypass a rehab assignment to make that return has now become a looming frustration as the Yankees look to push into October without him.
Judge missed roughly three months with a fractured rib before returning to the Yankees without appearing in a minor league game, a decision that he advocated for and the team allowed despite the risks. The hope was that the superstar could immediately provide his usual impact as New York pushed toward the postseason, but he was quickly sidelined again and returned to the injured list.
"In some ways, the Yankees are to blame for Judge's second trip to the IL," Deesha Thosar noted for Fox Sports. "They did, after all, grant Judge's wishes and allow him to skip a rehab assignment after missing three months with a fractured rib."
Now, Judge could potentially miss the remainder of the regular season and even the playoffs, leaving the Yankees without one of the most important pieces of their lineup at the most consequential point of the year.
New York Yankees Manager Aaron Boone Sends 2-Word Message After Brutal Aaron Judge Injury
Given the captain's quick return to the injured list, Yankees manager Aaron Boone was asked whether he second-guessed the decision to skip a rehab assignment that would have allowed him to ease into game action more gradually.
"Not really," Boone responded, per Thosar.
But for a Yankees team built around Judge's presence, the timing makes the setback particularly difficult. His absence changes the complexion of the lineup and leaves New York needing other hitters to absorb the production expected from its biggest star.
New York Yankees' Veteran Pitcher Sends Message On Aaron Judge's Quick IL Return
One Yankees teammate who understands what Judge is experiencing is familiar with the emotional toll of returning from an injury only to be quickly sidelined again.
"It sucks, for him personally, and I've been in that situation, where you're on the IL for a while, you come off and you go back on, it's a frustrating, it's a very frustrating process," Carlos Rodon told Foul Territory on Monday. "Him not being able to be in the lineup I'm sure it's excruciating for him to not be able to play in this moment."
That message captured the difficult reality facing Judge. After spending months working toward his return, he is now unable to contribute at the most important part of the season. And ultimately, the Yankees' decision to allow him to skip a rehab assignment could cost them all a World Series ring.
This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: Yankees’ Aaron Boone Delivers Clear Max Fried Verdict Before Playoffs
author: Keith Watkins
body:
The New York Yankees saw the Tampa Bay Rays claim the AL East crown at Yankee Stadium on Tuesday night. A 6-1 loss in the nightcap of a doubleheader split ended whatever remained of the division chase and confirmed what had felt inevitable for weeks. The Yankees are headed to the Wild Card Series.
The sting of the celebration was real. So was the pragmatism that followed it. With five regular season games remaining and the postseason less than a week away, manager Aaron Boone’s focus has already shifted to October.
His assessment of one pitcher in particular made that clear.
Boone’s Comments on Fried
Max Fried will not pitch again in the regular season. Tuesday’s start against the Rays was his final tuneup before the playoffs.
“I think he looks great,” Boone said. “I thought he was really good tonight. He threw the ball well. His curveball was really, really good tonight. Cutter was there. For the most part, was filling up the strike zone really well.”
Fried’s night unraveled in the seventh when a bunt play went sideways and three runs came in. Before that, he had been efficient and sharp. Boone saw a pitcher who is ready for October, not one who got tagged for four runs.
“He managed contact really well. I thought he was efficient,” Boone said. “He’s in a good place ready to go. Looking forward to seeing him out there in the postseason now.”
Managing the Final Five Games
With the standings locked in, Boone outlined how the Yankees will approach the rest of the week. The priority is keeping players sharp without wearing anyone down.
“Getting guys ready, picking some days for some guys to get off,” Boone said. “We’re the real game. So we’re playing. But I will pick some spots to get some guys down.”
Cody Bellinger and Austin Wells are candidates for rest days. Spencer Jones may get a day to manage. Boone also mentioned experimenting with defensive positions and being selective about when leverage relievers pitch.
The balance is delicate. The games do not matter in the standings. The rhythm and preparation matter for everything that comes after.
Final Word for the Yankees
The division belongs to Tampa Bay. The Yankees know it. They watched the celebration and walked off their own field.
What happens next is the only thing that counts. Fried is ready. Cole and Schlittler are lined up. The rotation has three arms capable of winning a postseason start.
The Wild Card Series begins next week, with a Red Sox series in the Bronx the most likely outcome. Boone’s message on Tuesday was simple. His team is not done. The pitching is in place. Now it is time to prove it matters.

title: ¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026
author: Patrizio Caro
body:
¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge? La lesión por la que recibió una inyección y pone en riesgo su participación en los Playoffs de MLB 2026
El capitán de los Yankees recibió una inyección para tratar su nueva lesión. Te explicamos qué le pasó, cuándo podría regresar y cómo llegan los Yankees a los Playoffs de MLB 2026.
Los New York Yankees podrían comenzar los Playoffs de MLB 2026 sin Aaron Judge. El capitán del equipo sufrió una nueva lesión en la pantorrilla derecha y recibió una inyección de plasma el lunes 21 de septiembre, en un intento por favorecer su recuperación antes del inicio de la postemporada.
El mánager Aaron Boone confirmó este martes que el jardinero presenta una distensión muscular moderada y que la organización está preparando la Serie de Comodines, programada para comenzar el 29 de septiembre, sin contar con él. No obstante, todavía no está descartado oficialmente.
La situación llega en un momento complicado para Judge, quien apenas había regresado de una fractura en una costilla que lo mantuvo fuera de actividad durante más de tres meses. Mientras tanto, los Yankees ya aseguraron su clasificación a los Playoffs, aunque terminaron perdiendo la División Este de la Liga Americana ante los Tampa Bay Rays.
¿Qué le pasó a Aaron Judge y cuál es su nueva lesión?
Aaron Judge sufrió una distensión moderada del músculo sóleo de la pantorrilla derecha el miércoles 16 de septiembre, durante el encuentro de los Yankees contra los Minnesota Twins.
El bateador de 34 años comenzó a sentir molestias desde la primera entrada, pero decidió mantenerse en el partido. Finalmente, tuvo que abandonar el encuentro en el sexto episodio y fue reemplazado por Heliot Ramos.
Al día siguiente, una resonancia magnética confirmó la lesión muscular. El sábado 19 de septiembre, los Yankees colocaron a Judge en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, con efecto retroactivo al jueves 17.
El sóleo es un músculo que se encuentra en la parte posterior de la pierna, debajo de los gemelos. Participa en movimientos fundamentales para un beisbolista, como correr, impulsarse y mantener la estabilidad.
¿Por qué le inyectaron plasma a Aaron Judge y en qué consiste el tratamiento?
La novedad de su recuperación
El lunes 21 de septiembre, durante el día de descanso de los Yankees, Aaron Judge recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas (PPP) en la pantorrilla derecha.
La inyección forma parte del tratamiento médico que está recibiendo Judge para intentar favorecer la recuperación de su lesión muscular. Sin embargo, el procedimiento no garantiza una recuperación acelerada ni determina cuándo podrá regresar a los diamantes.
Tras la aplicación, Judge permanece con actividad física limitada mientras los servicios médicos del equipo evalúan su evolución.
¿Qué otras lesiones ha sufrido Aaron Judge durante la temporada 2026?
La lesión de pantorrilla representa otro episodio en una temporada marcada por los problemas físicos del capitán de los Yankees.
A finales de abril, Judge sufrió una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla del lado derecho, aparentemente durante una jugada defensiva contra los Houston Astros. Aunque continuó jugando varias semanas, las molestias aumentaron y finalmente tuvo que detener su actividad.
El 5 de junio, los Yankees anunciaron el diagnóstico. Judge permaneció fuera de los diamantes durante todo el verano y no regresó hasta el 8 de septiembre, cuando enfrentó a los Colorado Rockies.
Su retorno duró apenas siete encuentros antes de que apareciera la nueva lesión.
Cronología de las lesiones de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Fecha | ¿Qué sucedió? | 
|---|---|
| 26 de abril | Sufrió la lesión que habría originado la fractura en una costilla. | 
| 31 de mayo | Disputó su último partido antes de una ausencia de más de tres meses. | 
| 5 de junio | Los Yankees confirmaron la fractura por estrés. | 
| 8 de septiembre | Regresó a la alineación contra Colorado. | 
| 16 de septiembre | Sufrió una distensión en la pantorrilla contra Minnesota. | 
| 19 de septiembre | Ingresó a la lista de lesionados de 10 días. | 
| 21 de septiembre | Recibió la inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas. | 
| 22 de septiembre | Boone confirmó la gravedad moderada de la distensión y expresó sus dudas sobre su disponibilidad para los Playoffs. | 
¿Qué dijo Aaron Boone sobre la lesión de Aaron Judge?
El mánager de los Yankees actualizó el estado de su capitán este martes 22 de septiembre y reconoció que no espera tenerlo disponible para el comienzo de la postemporada.
Estamos planificando que no forme parte de ella".
Así explicó Boone la postura del equipo ante la próxima Serie de Comodines. Aunque no descartó definitivamente al bateador, los Yankees se preparan para afrontar los primeros encuentros de eliminación directa sin él.
El propio Judge había manifestado el sábado 19 de septiembre su deseo de estar recuperado para los Playoffs, pero reconoció que todavía no tenía respuestas sobre los plazos de su rehabilitación.
¿Cuándo volverá a jugar Aaron Judge con los Yankees?
La primera fecha en la que Judge podría ser activado es el domingo 27 de septiembre, cuando los Yankees disputarán su último encuentro de la temporada regular contra los Baltimore Orioles.
Sin embargo, esa fecha corresponde únicamente al cumplimiento del periodo mínimo de su estancia en la lista de lesionados. No significa que el jugador vaya a estar físicamente preparado para reaparecer.
La organización no ha anunciado una fecha definitiva para su regreso. Su disponibilidad dependerá de la recuperación muscular y de las evaluaciones médicas que se realicen durante los próximos días.
¿Aaron Judge jugará los Playoffs de MLB 2026?
Su participación en la primera ronda se encuentra seriamente comprometida.
La Serie de Comodines comienza el martes 29 de septiembre, solamente ocho días después de que Judge recibiera la inyección de plasma. La cercanía de ambas fechas y la gravedad moderada de la distensión explican por qué los Yankees están preparando su alineación sin el capitán.
Si Nueva York avanza a la Serie Divisional, programada para comenzar el 3 de octubre, Judge dispondría de algunos días adicionales de recuperación. Sin embargo, tampoco está garantizada su participación en esa instancia.
Por ahora, los Yankees mantienen abierta la posibilidad de su regreso durante la postemporada, pero no existe un calendario médico confirmado.
¿Cómo están los Yankees en la temporada 2026 y cuál es su situación rumbo a los Playoffs?
Clasificados a la postemporada
Los Yankees aseguraron su boleto a los Playoffs de MLB 2026 el 14 de septiembre, pero no consiguieron conquistar la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Este martes 22 de septiembre disputaron una doble cartelera contra los Tampa Bay Rays. Primero ganaron 2-0, resultado que les permitió asegurar la ventaja de local para la Serie de Comodines. Sin embargo, en el segundo encuentro cayeron 6-1 y Tampa Bay se proclamó campeón divisional.
Así quedó la División Este de la Liga Americana
Al cierre del martes 22 de septiembre
| Equipo | G | P | 
|---|---|---|
| Rays (Campeón) | 96 | 61 | 
| Yankees | 90 | 67 | 
Los Rays aseguraron el primer sembrado de la Liga Americana, mientras que los Yankees disputarán la Serie de Comodines.
La derrota ante Tampa Bay dejó a los Yankees con cinco partidos pendientes de temporada regular. Ahora deberán concentrarse en llegar a la postemporada con su plantel recuperado y definir cómo cubrirán la ausencia de Judge.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees en la Serie de Comodines de MLB 2026?
Los Boston Red Sox son el rival que actualmente aparece en el posible cruce de primera ronda contra los Yankees.
Boston también aseguró su clasificación a los Playoffs, por lo que ambos equipos podrían protagonizar otra serie de postemporada entre históricos rivales de la División Este.
La Serie de Comodines se disputa al mejor de tres partidos. El ganador avanzará a la Serie Divisional.
Nueva York ya aseguró que será local durante esta ronda, por lo que disputará en el Yankee Stadium todos los partidos que sean necesarios. El enfrentamiento definitivo dependerá de las posiciones al cierre de la temporada regular.
¿Quién reemplazará a Aaron Judge en la alineación de los Yankees?
Heliot Ramos es una de las alternativas que Boone ha utilizado en el jardín derecho. De hecho, fue el encargado de sustituir a Judge cuando abandonó el encuentro del 16 de septiembre contra Minnesota.
El equipo también cuenta con Cody Bellinger y Spencer Jones entre sus opciones para los jardines, mientras continúa evaluando la recuperación de Trent Grisham.
En la ofensiva, los Yankees también disponen de Ben Rice y recuperaron este martes a Jazz Chisholm Jr., quien había permanecido fuera por un esguince en el pulgar derecho.
La conformación definitiva del orden al bate y del roster para la Serie de Comodines dependerá de las decisiones de Boone y de la evolución de los peloteros lesionados.
¿Cuáles son los números de Aaron Judge en la temporada 2026 de MLB?
La prolongada ausencia de Judge ha reducido considerablemente sus estadísticas con respecto a sus temporadas anteriores.
En su regreso del 8 al 16 de septiembre, el capitán de los Yankees conectó cuatro imparables en 23 turnos, incluido un cuadrangular, y produjo tres carreras. También acumuló 13 ponches durante ese periodo.
Estadísticas de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Estadística | Total | 
|---|---|
| Juegos | 66 | 
| Promedio de bateo | .241 | 
| Porcentaje de embasado | .360 | 
| Slugging | .511 | 
| Jonrones | 18 | 
| Carreras impulsadas | 41 | 
Estadísticas hasta su última participación, el 16 de septiembre.
¿Qué sigue para los Yankees antes del inicio de los Playoffs?
Con la División Este ya definida, los Yankees deberán aprovechar los últimos cinco encuentros de la temporada regular para preparar su participación en la Serie de Comodines.
Nueva York terminará su serie contra Tampa Bay y posteriormente recibirá a Baltimore del 25 al 27 de septiembre.
Mientras tanto, Boone deberá definir su rotación abridora, evaluar el regreso de otros jugadores lesionados y decidir qué peloteros integrarán el roster de postemporada.
La primera ronda comenzará el 29 de septiembre, mientras que las Series Divisionales están programadas para iniciar el 3 de octubre.

El lunes 21 de septiembre, durante el día de descanso de los Yankees, Aaron Judge recibió una inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas (PPP) en la pantorrilla derecha.
La inyección forma parte del tratamiento médico que está recibiendo Judge para intentar favorecer la recuperación de su lesión muscular. Sin embargo, el procedimiento no garantiza una recuperación acelerada ni determina cuándo podrá regresar a los diamantes.
Tras la aplicación, Judge permanece con actividad física limitada mientras los servicios médicos del equipo evalúan su evolución.
¿Qué otras lesiones ha sufrido Aaron Judge durante la temporada 2026?
La lesión de pantorrilla representa otro episodio en una temporada marcada por los problemas físicos del capitán de los Yankees.
A finales de abril, Judge sufrió una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla del lado derecho, aparentemente durante una jugada defensiva contra los Houston Astros. Aunque continuó jugando varias semanas, las molestias aumentaron y finalmente tuvo que detener su actividad.
El 5 de junio, los Yankees anunciaron el diagnóstico. Judge permaneció fuera de los diamantes durante todo el verano y no regresó hasta el 8 de septiembre, cuando enfrentó a los Colorado Rockies.
Su retorno duró apenas siete encuentros antes de que apareciera la nueva lesión.
Cronología de las lesiones de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Fecha | ¿Qué sucedió? | 
|---|---|
| 26 de abril | Sufrió la lesión que habría originado la fractura en una costilla. | 
| 31 de mayo | Disputó su último partido antes de una ausencia de más de tres meses. | 
| 5 de junio | Los Yankees confirmaron la fractura por estrés. | 
| 8 de septiembre | Regresó a la alineación contra Colorado. | 
| 16 de septiembre | Sufrió una distensión en la pantorrilla contra Minnesota. | 
| 19 de septiembre | Ingresó a la lista de lesionados de 10 días. | 
| 21 de septiembre | Recibió la inyección de plasma pobre en plaquetas. | 
| 22 de septiembre | Boone confirmó la gravedad moderada de la distensión y expresó sus dudas sobre su disponibilidad para los Playoffs. | 
¿Qué dijo Aaron Boone sobre la lesión de Aaron Judge?
El mánager de los Yankees actualizó el estado de su capitán este martes 22 de septiembre y reconoció que no espera tenerlo disponible para el comienzo de la postemporada.
Estamos planificando que no forme parte de ella".
Así explicó Boone la postura del equipo ante la próxima Serie de Comodines. Aunque no descartó definitivamente al bateador, los Yankees se preparan para afrontar los primeros encuentros de eliminación directa sin él.
El propio Judge había manifestado el sábado 19 de septiembre su deseo de estar recuperado para los Playoffs, pero reconoció que todavía no tenía respuestas sobre los plazos de su rehabilitación.
¿Cuándo volverá a jugar Aaron Judge con los Yankees?
La primera fecha en la que Judge podría ser activado es el domingo 27 de septiembre, cuando los Yankees disputarán su último encuentro de la temporada regular contra los Baltimore Orioles.
Sin embargo, esa fecha corresponde únicamente al cumplimiento del periodo mínimo de su estancia en la lista de lesionados. No significa que el jugador vaya a estar físicamente preparado para reaparecer.
La organización no ha anunciado una fecha definitiva para su regreso. Su disponibilidad dependerá de la recuperación muscular y de las evaluaciones médicas que se realicen durante los próximos días.
¿Aaron Judge jugará los Playoffs de MLB 2026?
Su participación en la primera ronda se encuentra seriamente comprometida.
La Serie de Comodines comienza el martes 29 de septiembre, solamente ocho días después de que Judge recibiera la inyección de plasma. La cercanía de ambas fechas y la gravedad moderada de la distensión explican por qué los Yankees están preparando su alineación sin el capitán.
Si Nueva York avanza a la Serie Divisional, programada para comenzar el 3 de octubre, Judge dispondría de algunos días adicionales de recuperación. Sin embargo, tampoco está garantizada su participación en esa instancia.
Por ahora, los Yankees mantienen abierta la posibilidad de su regreso durante la postemporada, pero no existe un calendario médico confirmado.
¿Cómo están los Yankees en la temporada 2026 y cuál es su situación rumbo a los Playoffs?
Clasificados a la postemporada
Los Yankees aseguraron su boleto a los Playoffs de MLB 2026 el 14 de septiembre, pero no consiguieron conquistar la División Este de la Liga Americana.
Este martes 22 de septiembre disputaron una doble cartelera contra los Tampa Bay Rays. Primero ganaron 2-0, resultado que les permitió asegurar la ventaja de local para la Serie de Comodines. Sin embargo, en el segundo encuentro cayeron 6-1 y Tampa Bay se proclamó campeón divisional.
Así quedó la División Este de la Liga Americana
Al cierre del martes 22 de septiembre
| Equipo | G | P | 
|---|---|---|
| Rays (Campeón) | 96 | 61 | 
| Yankees | 90 | 67 | 
Los Rays aseguraron el primer sembrado de la Liga Americana, mientras que los Yankees disputarán la Serie de Comodines.
La derrota ante Tampa Bay dejó a los Yankees con cinco partidos pendientes de temporada regular. Ahora deberán concentrarse en llegar a la postemporada con su plantel recuperado y definir cómo cubrirán la ausencia de Judge.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees en la Serie de Comodines de MLB 2026?
Los Boston Red Sox son el rival que actualmente aparece en el posible cruce de primera ronda contra los Yankees.
Boston también aseguró su clasificación a los Playoffs, por lo que ambos equipos podrían protagonizar otra serie de postemporada entre históricos rivales de la División Este.
La Serie de Comodines se disputa al mejor de tres partidos. El ganador avanzará a la Serie Divisional.
Nueva York ya aseguró que será local durante esta ronda, por lo que disputará en el Yankee Stadium todos los partidos que sean necesarios. El enfrentamiento definitivo dependerá de las posiciones al cierre de la temporada regular.
¿Quién reemplazará a Aaron Judge en la alineación de los Yankees?
Heliot Ramos es una de las alternativas que Boone ha utilizado en el jardín derecho. De hecho, fue el encargado de sustituir a Judge cuando abandonó el encuentro del 16 de septiembre contra Minnesota.
El equipo también cuenta con Cody Bellinger y Spencer Jones entre sus opciones para los jardines, mientras continúa evaluando la recuperación de Trent Grisham.
En la ofensiva, los Yankees también disponen de Ben Rice y recuperaron este martes a Jazz Chisholm Jr., quien había permanecido fuera por un esguince en el pulgar derecho.
La conformación definitiva del orden al bate y del roster para la Serie de Comodines dependerá de las decisiones de Boone y de la evolución de los peloteros lesionados.
¿Cuáles son los números de Aaron Judge en la temporada 2026 de MLB?
La prolongada ausencia de Judge ha reducido considerablemente sus estadísticas con respecto a sus temporadas anteriores.
En su regreso del 8 al 16 de septiembre, el capitán de los Yankees conectó cuatro imparables en 23 turnos, incluido un cuadrangular, y produjo tres carreras. También acumuló 13 ponches durante ese periodo.
Estadísticas de Aaron Judge en 2026
| Estadística | Total | 
|---|---|
| Juegos | 66 | 
| Promedio de bateo | .241 | 
| Porcentaje de embasado | .360 | 
| Slugging | .511 | 
| Jonrones | 18 | 
| Carreras impulsadas | 41 | 
Estadísticas hasta su última participación, el 16 de septiembre.
¿Qué sigue para los Yankees antes del inicio de los Playoffs?
Con la División Este ya definida, los Yankees deberán aprovechar los últimos cinco encuentros de la temporada regular para preparar su participación en la Serie de Comodines.
Nueva York terminará su serie contra Tampa Bay y posteriormente recibirá a Baltimore del 25 al 27 de septiembre.
Mientras tanto, Boone deberá definir su rotación abridora, evaluar el regreso de otros jugadores lesionados y decidir qué peloteros integrarán el roster de postemporada.
La primera ronda comenzará el 29 de septiembre, mientras que las Series Divisionales están programadas para iniciar el 3 de octubre.

title: What should the Yankees do with Carlos Rodón?
author: Jake Devin
body:
Leading off yesterday's doubleheader, Carlos Rodón pitched like a man who had something to prove. In a way, he does. He may be asked to step aside if the club needs a three-man rotation for a potential Wild Card series next week, widely viewed as the fourth guy sitting outside the Yankees' Big 3 in their rotation, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, and Gerrit Cole. Rodón's also had to answer doubts all year as he's dealt with numerous injuries, starting the season on the IL after offseason elbow surgery and a hamstring injury in spring training, before hitting the IL again with elbow inflammation over the summer. He's been nails through it all, posting a 2.67 ERA in 16 starts, saving his best for last in the form of an eight-inning masterpiece Tuesday afternoon.
Rodón's performance forces some interesting questions for the Yankees, particularly when it comes to their strategy should they face the Red Sox in a best-of-three. How should the Yankees deploy Rodón next week?
First off, you can make a compelling argument that they should just start the man. By any measure, he's been the club's third-best starter this season, behind Schlittler and Fried and ahead of Cole. Cole has been more durable throughout the season, but Rodón's been in better form down the stretch, posting a 1.89 ERA in seven starts since coming off the IL a second time. Why not just roll with the hot hand?
The Yankees seem likely to go with Cole, preferring to defer to both Cole's extensive track record and status over Rodón's superior recent performance, a decision that's both debatable and reasonable. Should that be their move, the strategic implications run deeper.
They could use Rodón in something of a piggyback role, letting him eat multiple innings in support of one of their top starters (perhaps Cole, the team's shakiest starter lately?). They could let him air it out in a one-inning relief role for one series, or even deploy him as a lefty specialist, choosing to bring him in if and when the opposing lineup presents a lane of left-handed hitters.
It's not at all a simple decision, in no small part because there's another plausible idea here: keep him in reserve for a potential ALDS. If the Yankees burn all four of their top starters in some fashion in the ALWC, they'd be forced to start Will Warren in Game 1 of the ALDS should they advance. The difference between Rodón and Warren isn't exactly massive, and Warren has been strong down the stretch as well, but saving Rodón for the ALDS allows the Yankees to ensure that every game is started by one of their top four pitchers.
It's a complicated calculus; every tactical decision you make in one postseason game or series has major strategic consequences on every future game and series. Rodón could be an extra relief weapon in a Wild Card series, he could be held in reserve for a future series, and you could even argue he should just start against Boston. What do you think? What should the Yankees do with Rodón?

Later, Jonathan's entry in our Yankees Birthday series features a fan favorite from a bygone era, Joba Chamberlain, and Josh discusses Aaron Judge's calf injury, and the Yankees' continued reluctance to be forthright whenever Judge gets hurt.

title: Yankees 35-Save Closer Set to Become Free Agent on Nov. 5
author: Jonathan Vankin
body:
The New York Yankees split a doubleheader with the first-place Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday, winning the first game 2-0 behind eight shutout innings from Carlos Rodón and the 35th save of the season by closer David Bednar.
By losing the second game 6-1, however, the Yankees were eliminated from the race for the American League East pennant, and the Rays clinched it. The Yankees are now locked into the AL’s top Wild Card spot, and will most likely face the Boston Red Sox in a best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium starting Sept. 29.
With the regular season winding down, the Yankees’ front office now must decide what to do with Bednar, who played a key role in the Yankees’ run to the postseason but becomes eligible for free agency when the signing period opens on Nov. 5.
Bednar recorded the second-best save total of his career, but the achievement hasn’t yet earned him a contract commitment from Yankees general manager Brian Cashman.
With the bullpen thin on proven arms and October now locked in, letting a closer walk to the open market without so much as an extension conversation raises questions about who closes games for New York after this year.
Bednar Built an Unlikely Path to Closer Duty
David Jeffrey Bednar was born Oct. 10, 1994, in Pittsburgh and grew up nearby in Mars, Pennsylvania. San Diego took the 6-foot-1, 250-pound right-hander in the 35th round of the 2016 draft out of Lafayette College, hardly the pedigree of a future big-league closer.
Bednar debuted with the Padres on Sept. 1, 2019, then landed in Pittsburgh a little more than a year later as part of a three-team trade involving the Mets. He turned that opportunity into back-to-back All-Star nods and a league-leading 39 saves in 2023, becoming the closer in a rebuilding Pirates bullpen.
A rocky 2024 and a brief demotion to Triple-A in 2025 threatened to derail that run, but New York bet on a bounce-back. The Yankees acquired the two-time All-Star reliever on July 31, 2025, sending Pittsburgh minor-league catchers Rafael Flores and Edgleen Pérez and outfielder Brian Sánchez in return. Bednar answered by posting a 2.19 ERA with 10 saves in 22 games down the stretch in 2025.
Yankees Weigh Bednar’s Free Agency Future
Bednar signed a one-year, $9 million contract in January to avoid arbitration, his final season of club control before hitting the open market. He’s made good on it, posting a 2.54 ERA and 35 saves through 62 appearances this season, the second-highest total of his career behind his 39-save 2023 campaign, with 74 strikeouts over 67 1/3 innings.
Bednar carries a 1.83 ERA over his last 30 outings, a run interrupted only by a Sept. 16 blown save at Minnesota in which both runs he allowed were unearned.
Speculation surfaced in June that Bednar could be predicted to lose the closer role to Fernando Cruz, but he held the job through the stretch run regardless.
No extension talks have surfaced publicly. Bleacher Report‘s Joel Reuter called Bednar one of the most reliable closers in baseball and floated a hypothetical three-year, $45 million deal as a “top priority” reunion. MLB Trade Rumors, which included Bednar on its list of 2026-27 MLB free agents, gave him only an honorable mention on its rankings of the winter’s top relievers.
Bednar should be eligible for a qualifying offer, having spent the entire 2026 season with New York and never having received one before. The amount of the MLB qualifying offer is estimated to be set at a projected $23.1 million this offseason, though relievers rarely draw the tag at that price since multiyear closer deals typically land below it.

title: Philadelphia Phillies Reveal Major Don Mattingly Managerial Update
author: TJ French
body:
A lot of news broke on the managerial front in Major League Baseball on Tuesday, September 22, as New York Mets interim manager Andy Green was awarded a three-year extension, and Boston Red Sox executives decided that manager Chad Tracy will also remain in Boston for upcoming seasons.
With those pieces of news, it draws question marks to what the Philadelphia Phillies will do with their interim manager, Don Mattingly, who has brought the team to within striking distance of a playoff berth after carrying the NL’s worst record in late April.
More MLB on Heavy: Struggling Atlanta Braves All-Star Player Still Owed $30+ Million
Phillies to Decide on Don Mattingly’s Future After 2026 Season
Per president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski, the Phillies will decide on interim manager Don Mattingly’s future after the 2026 season.
Here’s what he told reporters, via MLBTR.com:
“[We] have felt it is better to wait until our season is complete,” said Dombrowski.
MLBTR.com’s Anthony Franco then wrote (about the Phillies managerial search):
“That’s not a huge surprise, as the Phillies announced in April that Mattingly was only locked into the job through the end of the season. He’s on a two-year contract with the organization that he signed over the winter to serve as Rob Thomson’s bench coach. Thomson was fired after they limped to a 9-19 start.”
With both the Mets and Red Sox jobs now secured, the Phillies stand out as the most attractive managerial landing spot by far, and the Phillies would be remiss not to at least interview some of the top candidates like Alex Cora.

A lot of news broke on the managerial front in Major League Baseball on Tuesday, September 22, as New York Mets interim manager Andy Green was awarded a three-year extension, and Boston Red Sox executives decided that manager Chad Tracy will also remain in Boston for upcoming seasons.
With those pieces of news, it draws question marks to what the Philadelphia Phillies will do with their interim manager, Don Mattingly, who has brought the team to within striking distance of a playoff berth after carrying the NL’s worst record in late April.

title: What Carlos Rodon gem does for Yankees’ postseason rotation
author: Randy Miller
body:
NEW YORK — The Yankees went into Tuesday's day-night doubleheader hoping to make a last stand with the division title all but lost.
One Rays win in four games this week at Yankee Stadium and the Yankees would be locked into a best-of-three Wild Card Series.
They lasted until Game 2, a 6-1 Rays win that clinched the AL East.
The Yankees' Carlos Rodon-fueled 2-0 win in Game 1 guaranteed they'd be home for the first round. Two more Red Sox wins will ensure a repeat of last October's first-round matchup that the Yankees won in three games.
You remember Game 3, right?
That was Cam Schlittler's real coming out party. That's when the tall rookie right-hander showed everyone how great he can be throwing up eight shutout innings with 12 strikeouts and no walks in a do-or-die game.
That's the Schlittler that the Yankees have seen in almost all of his 2026 starts. He's been so good that he's a lock to win the AL Cy Young and he's getting MVP consideration, too.
As for who starts Game 1 of the Yankees' Wild Card Series next Tuesday, they could go Schlittler on regular rest or Gerrit Cole on extra rest.
It doesn't matter though because none of the Yankees' Wild Card Series starting pitchers will be able to start two games in the next round.
The Wild Card Series starts Sept. 29, and the two American League Division Series begin four days later on Oct. 3. So, unless the Yankees opt to use a starter on short rest — and they won't — their third or fourth starter will get the nod for Game 1 of the ALDS if the Yankees advance.
Another option would be Schlittler in Game 1, Max Fried in Game 2 and Cole in Game 3.
The big lefty could be a long relief option for the Red Sox … or saved for two starts against the Rays.
If the Yankees win their Wild Card Series, the Rays would be up next for a best of five that starts at Tropicana Field.
Rodon manhandled the Rays in Tuesday's opener, eight shutout innings, two singles, eight strikeouts and no walks. After this outing, who better to line up for Game 1 and Game 5 than Rodon if Schlittler isn't rested?
What's next for Rodon?
TBD.
Manager Aaron Boone said the plan is to skip Rodon on Sunday and then figure out what's next.
"Ah, we haven't got that far yet," the skipper said after Tuesday's first game.
That made sense until the Rays clinched.
If the Yankees had been alive in the division race heading into Sunday, Rodon is lined up to pitch game 162.
The Yankees love what they're getting from Rodon, who hasn't allowed more than three runs for 26 consecutive starts (although he did have a three-run, six-inning dud against the Blue Jays in Game 3 of a Division Series last October).
Two injured list stints wiped out more than half of Rodon's season, which is year four of a six-year, $162 million pact - but he's consistently been good to great when he's been pitching and he was as good as he's ever been as a Yankee in Tuesday's opener. He set a tone setting down the stars in the Rays' lineup 1-2-3 in the first inning – Yandy Diaz and Jonathan Aranda by strikeout, Junior Caminero on a lineout – then put up seven more zeroes.
The Rays managed two baserunners in eight innings facing Rodon, both singles. The lefty's last strikeout was special, No. 1,500 over an injury-riddled career that's included three All-Star selections, a no-hitter for the White Sox and 18 wins last year.
"His stuff is really good, especially today with the heater and the profile of that fastball," Boone said. "I think in a lot of ways his fastball is in a better place than it was last year, which was a great season for him. But we've seen over the last couple years him really develop as a pitcher and develop the secondary (pitches).
"When he came to us, his calling card throughout his career was just overpowering fastball/slider combo. The changeup the last couple years has become an excellent pitch for him. So he can pitch now. He can beat you different ways. But I like where his fastball is right now."
The Yankees' starting pitching has been the best in the majors this year, and it's had to with Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton out of the lineup for much of the season. Tuesday's news that Judge is doubtful for the first round — maybe for the entire postseason — only adds to the pressure on the pitching staff.
If the Yankees aren't bounced in the first round, Rodon probably will get at least one and maybe two more shots at the Rays.
"I expect him to play a big role for us hopefully, especially if we go on a deep run in the postseason," Boone said. "I like where he's at right now."

title: Cubs and White Sox are in the hunt for playoff berths: Tracking the magic numbers for Chicago’s baseball teams
author: Chicago Tribune
body:
The marathon that is the Major League Baseball season is down to a September sprint, and the Cubs and White Sox are in the thick of a playoff hunt.
The Cubs will finish in second place in the National League Central for the fourth consecutive season — with the first-place Milwaukee Brewers having clinched their fourth straight division crown.
The White Sox, meanwhile, are in a neck-and-neck battle with the Cleveland Guardians for the American League Central crown. The Sox are trying to complete a remarkable worst-to-first turnaround after losing more than 100 games each of the last three seasons.
Here’s where things stand.
Want the latest baseball news? Subscribe to the Chicago Tribune to read it all — and sign up for our Cubs Insider and White Sox Insider newsletters.
Cubs
Record: 87-70 through Tuesday.
Magic number for a wild-card spot: 1 (combination of Cubs wins and Arizona Diamondbacks losses).
Tuesday’s result: 8-2 loss to the Miami Marlins in 12 innings.
Games remaining: 5.
NL Central standings: The Brewers have clinched the division.
NL wild card: The Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres are tied for the No. 1 spot. The Diamondbacks are four games back after their win on Tuesday. The Cubs own the tiebreaker over all three teams.
Last playoff appearance: 2025 as the No. 4 seed in the NL as the top wild card. The Cubs beat the Padres 2-1 in the wild-card series before losing to the Brewers 3-2 in the division series.
Postseason history: 22 appearances in 150 seasons — eight division titles, four wild-card berths, 17 pennants and three championships (1907, 1908, 2016).
40-40 watch: Pete Crow-Armstrong is trying to become the seventh player in MLB history to reach 40 home runs and 40 stolen bases in a season. He has 45 home runs and 39 stolen bases. The six who accomplished the feat:
- José Canseco, Athletics, 1988: 42 home runs, 40 stolen bases
- Barry Bonds, Giants, 1996: 42-40
- Alex Rodriguez, Mariners, 1998: 42-46
- Alfonso Soriano, Nationals, 2006: 46-41
- Ronald Acuna Jr., Braves, 2023: 41-73
- Shohei Ohtani, Dodgers, 2024: 54-59
White Sox
Record: 81-76 through Tuesday.
Magic number for a wild-card spot: 3 (combination of Sox wins and Houston Astros losses).
Tuesday’s result: 14-11 win over the Kansas City Royals.
Games remaining: 5.
AL Central standings: The White Sox trail the first-place Guardians — who also won Tuesday — by one game. If the Sox and Guardians finish with the same record, the Sox own the tiebreaker and would win the division title.
AL wild card: The Sox hold the No. 3 spot, three games ahead of the Texas Rangers and four games ahead of the Toronto Blue Jays.
Last playoff appearance: 2021 as the AL Central champions and No. 3 seed in the AL. The White Sox lost to the Astros 3-1 in the division series.
Postseason history: 11 appearances in 125 seasons — six division titles, one wild-card berth, six pennants and three championships (1906, 1917, and 2005).
Playoff format
Wild-card round
Sept. 29-Oct. 1, best of three, all at the higher seed
- No. 5 seed at No. 4 seed
- No. 6 seed at No. 3 seed
Nos. 1 and 2 seeds have byes
Division series
Oct. 3-10, best of five, 2-2-1 format
- No. 1 vs. No. 4/5 winner
- No. 2 vs. No. 3/6 winner
League Championship Series
Oct. 11-20, best of seven, 2-3-2 format
World Series
Oct. 23-31, best of seven, 2-3-2 format

title: 5 reasons the Yankees can win without Judge
author: Bryan Hoch
body:
NEW YORK – The news about Aaron Judge’s return to the injured list was still fresh, having been announced less than an hour earlier, and already Cody Bellinger was envisioning how the Yankees could succeed in the postseason without their captain.
Unfortunately for Judge and his club, they’ve had plenty of practice doing exactly that this season. They’ve had no choice.
“Missing Judge, it hurts,” Bellinger said. “We all know he’s the best hitter in the game. For us in here, our mindset is, we’re going to have to find a way. I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself. I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here to go out, win and beat anybody.”
Now they’ll have their chance to prove it.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone said Tuesday that Judge is dealing with a “moderate” strain of his right calf and is not expected to be ready for a potential American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox, which would begin on Sept. 29.
Judge’s availability for subsequent rounds, especially the AL Division Series, is also in doubt. But the Yankees need to get there first. Here are five reasons why the Yankees, lauded as pennant favorites, still can reach the Fall Classic even if Judge doesn’t return:
Dominant starting pitching
Rodón might not even draw a start in a potential Wild Card Series, standing in line behind AL Cy Young Award frontrunner Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and Max Fried. Simply put, the rotation has kept them afloat.
Yankees starters have permitted two earned runs or fewer in 40 of 51 starts since July 28, including one earned run or fewer in 33 of those starts, compiling a 2.50 ERA over that span. Overall, they’ve allowed one run or fewer in 65 games, a single-season franchise record.
“We come to win every game, regardless of who is on the field,” Rodón said. “Obviously it’s tough when you don’t have the best player in the world on the field with you. I’m hopeful that he’ll be back. But … it’s just about winning games for us.”
There’s other thump
This isn’t 2022, when Judge’s 62 home runs set a single-season AL record and served as the unquestioned engine of the offense. Mostly because of the rib injury, Judge was limited to a .241 average, 18 homers and 41 RBIs across 66 games. Ben Rice shouldered much of the load, fulfilling Boone’s spring prediction of 39 homers.

title: Yankees preview postseason blueprint in doubleheader vs. Rays
author: James O'Connell
body:
During a long day of baseball in the Bronx, the Yankees and Rays both took one game apiece in the day-night doubleheader between the top two teams in the American League — and teams that are on a collision course as potential ALDS opponents.
It may have been a sneak peek of what’s to come, from the teams on the field to the chill in the air, and even what to expect from the club known as the Bronx Bombers.
The Yankees have been, to put it kindly, offensively challenged in the absence of Aaron Judge and with their captain likely to miss the Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. That’s not expected to change, as evidenced by their abysmal offensive performance on Tuesday.
The pinstripes scored three runs between the two games and totaled just eight hits. Their first hit in the nightcap didn’t come until the 7th inning.
However, the Yanks did show their strength and it came from their pair of southpaws on the mound. Carlos Rodon tossed eight shutout innings — where he reached 98 mph on his four-seamer and struck out eight batters — and Max Fried, who was superb for most of his outing, added 6.2 innings of four-run ball (three of which came in the seventh).
If the Yankees have an extended stay in October, the games will likely look a lot like they did for most of Tuesday.
Quick and quiet. Because if things start to get loud, chances are they aren’t the ones making the noise.
The Bombers are entering this postseason with pitching at the forefront of their identity, having horses such as Cam Schlittler, Gerrit Cole and the pair of lefties who toed the slab against the Rays.
It’s an elite group to rely on, as the club owned the best ERA in baseball amongst starters with a 3.24. However, here’s a lot riding on each of those guys to be virtually perfect, as, barring a sudden change in offensive firepower, there won’t be many runs to come by.
Since May 31 — the game Judge last played before his rib injury kept him out until Sept. 8 — the Yankees rank 23rd in runs scored, 29th in batting average and 26th in WRC+. It’s not a recipe for success, and they have no choice but to make it work.
Hits like Cody Bellinger’s two-run homer in the day game may have to be enough to get the job done as Aaron Boone’s club showed you on Tuesday how they plan to compete and bring their 28th championship home this season.

title: Rays clinch AL East, celebrate after Yankees secure home field advantage for Wild Card round
author: Gary Phillips
body:
When the Yankees retained a large chunk of their 2025 roster, they didn’t think they’d end up starting the 2026 playoffs in the same position that they did last year.
Alas, the second-place Bombers, burdened by injuries all season, officially missed out on a division title for the second straight season, as Tampa Bay clinched the American League East and a postseason bye with a 6-1 win in the second game of Tuesday’s doubleheader between the two teams. With their significantly richer rivals thwarted — the Yankees’ luxury tax payroll is $228.9 million more than Tampa’s, per Cot’s Contracts — the Rays excitedly shook hands in front of the Bronx faithful before popping bottles and lighting cigars in the visitor’s clubhouse at Yankee Stadium.
“It’s not a good feeling, for sure,” Yankees outfielder Heliot Ramos said after going 1-for-4 with two strikeouts.
“You don’t want anyone to be celebrating at your stadium,” added Max Fried, who allowed four earned runs over 6.2 innings.
It was a sour ending to a long day that began with a 2-0 victory for the Yankees, who are now 90-67 and six games behind the Rays with five games left in the regular season. That afternoon win ensured that the Yankees will have home field advantage in the Wild Card round, which begins on Sept. 29.
The likeliest scenario is that the Yankees will host the Red Sox, just as they did in last year’s Wild Card round.
The Yankees already knew that winning the division was an uphill battle coming into this four-game series against the Rays, as they needed to sweep just to keep that improbable dream alive after losing two games in Arizona over the weekend. And even with their win in Game 1 on Tuesday, the pinstripers only had a 1.8% chance of claiming the AL East, according to FanGraphs.
“You gotta give them credit,” Aaron Boone said of the 96-61 Rays on Tuesday morning. “They’ve won a ton of games this year, games that have probably been up in the air late, and they’ve come out on top. So they’ve had a great year, and they’re always a challenge to play.”
Drew Rasmussen was particularly challenging on Tuesday night, as he out-pitched Fried and didn’t permit a hit until Ramos led off the seventh inning with a double. The right-handed Rasmussen also struck out 11 while allowing one run over 6.2 innings.
With the division race over, the Yankees can now take the remainder of the week to rest key players and experiment before their likely rematch with Boston in the Wild Card round, which they expect to play without the injured Aaron Judge. If they can win that series, they’ll face the Rays again in the ALDS, a possibility that both clubs’ managers acknowledged on Tuesday night.
“This four-game series has been circled on both of our schedules for quite some time, and that’s because of so much respect that you have for the opponent,” Rays skipper Kevin Cash said. “That’s a very talented team, and we know that we could be seeing them here in another 10, 12 games.”
“Hopefully we get another crack at them in the next couple weeks,” Boone chimed in.
While the Yankees beat the Red Sox last October and won this year’s season series against them, the Wild Card round is not how they envisioned beginning the 2026 postseason after they fell short of a division title last year.
In 2025, the Yankees ended the regular season with the same record as the pennant-winning Blue Jays. However, Toronto won the season series tiebreaker between the two teams — and therefore the AL East — earned a bye in the playoffs, and defeated the Yankees in a four-game ALDS.
The Yankees last won the East in 2024. They lost that year’s World Series to the Dodgers.
The Yanks have won their division just three times since 2013, and they haven’t won a championship since 2009. However, they still believe they can end that drought after failing to secure an AL East crown.
“It kind of sucks,” Jazz Chisholm Jr. said of losing the division. “That’s what we work on all season, but it’s not the end goal for us. That end goal is the World Series, so it doesn’t really affect us here.”

title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. makes spotty Yankees return as playoff questions loom
author: Dan Martin; Mark W Sanchez
body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. returned to what looks like a Yankees infield competition with a hit, a walk and a defensive mistake.
The second baseman was activated from the injured list for the nightcap of Tuesday’s doubleheader and got the nod at second base after Anthony Volpe — who has played well at the spot in his absence — started the first game.
		
		
		
				
			Access the Yankees beat like never before		
			
			
Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Chisholm’s most memorable moment, though, was failing to cover first base on a safety squeeze in the 6-1 loss in The Bronx that helped the Rays clinch the division.
With one out and runners on the corners in the seventh inning and Taylor Walls at the plate, manager Aaron Boone said the Yankees were aware that a bunt would be coming “more often than not.”
And sure enough, Walls pushed a bunt toward first base, and Luis García Jr. charged, as he was supposed to, Boone said.
Chisholm started to run over but stopped, believing García would halt his charge and return to the base. Chisholm instead hovered by second base.
“He’s just gotta go [to first base] every time, and he knows that,” Boone said of Chisholm, who acknowledged the mistake.
“Next time, I’ll just keep going through,” said Chisholm, who was sidelined for two weeks after spraining his right thumb Sept. 8 and has returned to a team sorting out its infield with five games to go before the postseason.
Asked before the doubleheader if Volpe would continue to get time at second with Chisholm back, Boone said, “We’ll see.”
Chisholm went 1-for-3 with a single and a walk, while Volpe went 0-for-3 with three strikeouts in the 2-0 doubleheader opener. Entering play, Volpe had hit .286 with a .753 OPS in 10 games with Chisholm on the IL.
The Yankees also have to figure out third base, as Ryan McMahon is a mess on both sides of the ball.
José Caballero got the start there in the opener against Martinez and went 1-for-3 with a pair of stolen bases, with lefty-swinging McMahon in the lineup for the nightcap against Drew Rasmussen. McMahon went 0-for-2 with a strikeout and could not make a difficult play on a Nick Fortes chopper that reached McMahon on an in-between hop and went for an infield single.
Boone said he wanted to get “regular reps” for both Caballero and McMahon, who entered Tuesday just 6-for-40 with an OPS of .402 since returning from a sprained thumb Sept. 1.
Amed Rosario, signed in the offseason with the idea of playing third against lefties, has not produced in those situations this year, and the Yankees have mostly gone with Caballero and McMahon over the last three weeks.
To make room on the roster for Chisholm, Max Schuemann was optioned to the FCL Yankees.
Clarke Schmidt played catch Tuesday after experiencing cramping in his biceps while warming up during Sunday’s game against Arizona.
Boone said the team was awaiting word from doctors regarding the right-hander’s availability, but a source told The Post’s Joel Sherman that Schmidt still felt something in the area.
Another source said an IL stint isn’t out of the question as Schmidt is trying to earn a spot on the postseason roster after missing over a year following Tommy John surgery.
Ryan Weathers threw a bullpen session between games as he works to return from a left forearm strain, and Fernando Cruz (UCL) played catch.
The Yankees haven’t announced their playoff rotation, but Gerrit Cole has started the team’s first postseason game in every season in which he’s been healthy since he joined the organization in 2020.
The right-hander will start Wednesday and was asked by The Post how he would feel if Cam Schlittler got the start in the first game of a wild-card series this season.
“Fine by me,’’ said Cole, who had a similar reaction when there was discussion of having Nestor Cortes open the playoffs in 2022. “What matters is me trying to be my best. Whatever [Boone] thinks is good.”

Giancarlo Stanton jogged in the outfield between games Tuesday. Stanton suffered his third calf strain of the season, and first in his left leg, over four weeks ago, and there remains no guarantee he returns this season… The Yankees have won at least 90 games eight times in the last nine years in which there’s been a full season. … The Yankees lost both ABS challenges early in Game 1 on Tuesday, as Ali Sánchez had a poor challenge catching in the top of the first and Heliot Ramos followed with an even worse challenge at the plate in the bottom of the inning.

title: Kevin Cash speaks out after Rays win first AL East title since 2021
author: Bill Ladson
body:
NEW YORK — A few hours after losing the first game of a day-night doubleheader to the New York Yankees, 2-0, at Yankee Stadium, the Tampa Bay Rays had a game to remember a few hours later. They won the American League East title by beating New York, 6-1, their first crown since 2021.
The Rays started celebrating at 10:11 p.m. after closer Bryan Baker induced George Lombard Jr. to ground out to end the game. Then the champagne started flowing 10 minutes later.
What made the Rays different was that they played all facets of the game well. They didn’t rely just on Junior Caminero or Jonathan Aranda for the long ball; they played small ball. For example, the Rays currently lead the AL in stolen bases (160) and the majors in sacrifice bunts (45).
“(The small ball) was a byproduct of our roster," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "If you look at Cedric Mullins, Chandler Simpson and Wallsy (Taylor Walls), guys with a lot of speed and make a lot of contact, why not put pressure on defenses. It kind of caught like wildfire because they had so much success. They were so good at it that there was confidence that carried out into the season."
The Rays can pitch, too. They are seventh in the league in ERA (3.67) and lead the major leagues with 57 saves. Acquiring right-hander Nick Martinez via free agency was a godsend. He has 15 wins with a 2.94 ERA. However, he is more than just a quality pitcher.
“He is fun to watch. He is an awesome leader for us. What a clubhouse guy. I could give him all the credit for mostly everything that has happened this year,” Walls said about Martinez. "This is my first year knowing him. He is the same guy no matter where you see him. He takes care of everybody. He is positive, always has a smile on his face. He is always doing something that could benefit someone else. If there was one MVP on this team, it would be him.”
Right-hander Drew Rasmussen is the ace of the staff and pitched like one in the division clincher, allowing a run in 6.2 innings and striking out 11. He didn’t allow a hit until the top of the seventh inning, when Heliot Ramos led off with a double.
“It’s the culmination of a lot of things coming together,” Rasmussen told MLB TV. “We had the conversation in February that this group had the opportunity to be special. To see all the hard work the guys have put in offensively, defensively and the mound — I mean, this is what it is all about. I’m happy everyone is enjoying it.”
When the postseason starts, the Rays will be awaiting the winner of the American League Wild Card Series. It’s a possibility they could be facing the Yankees again in October.
“That’s a very talented team and we know we could be seeing them in another 10 to 12 days,” Cash said about the Bronx Bombers.
All quotations obtained firsthand unless otherwise noted.

title: ¿Pierden al Juez? Aaron Judge es duda para los playoffs con los Yankees
author: Emiliano Cárdenas Ramírez
body:
Los New York Yankees podrían comenzar la postemporada sin una de sus principales figuras. Aaron Judge recibió una inyección de plasma rico en plaquetas (PRP) en la pantorrilla derecha, luego de que una resonancia magnética revelara una distensión en la zona.
El manager Aaron Boone reconoció que, en este momento, el equipo trabaja con la idea de que Judge no estará disponible para la serie de comodines, aunque todavía existe una pequeña posibilidad de que pueda recuperarse a tiempo.
Aaron Judge recibió una inyección en la pantorrilla
Antes de la doble cartelera ante los Tampa Bay Rays, Boone informó que Judge recibió la inyección durante el día libre de los Yankees, después de regresar de Arizona.
“Estamos planeando que no forme parte de eso, pero también estamos en esta época del año en la que, con las lesiones, se escucha todo el tiempo que se dan rangos: de dos a cuatro semanas, de cuatro a seis semanas”, explicó Boone.
El manager de Nueva York señaló que, aunque no espera contar con Judge para el inicio de los playoffs, tampoco quiere descartar completamente esa posibilidad.
“El rango existe por una razón y estamos en un punto del año en el que, obviamente, lo forzamos un poco si eso estuviera sobre la mesa, pero eso es dentro de una semana. No lo espero, pero tampoco lo descarto”, agregó.
Aaron Judge volvió a lesionarse tras regresar de una fractura
El toletero se lesionó la pantorrilla durante el encuentro del miércoles pasado frente a los Minnesota Twins. Judge abandonó el partido en la sexta entrada para ser reemplazado por un bateador emergente debido a molestias en la pierna.
En un principio, el movimiento fue considerado como una medida de precaución, pero los síntomas persistieron y posteriormente una resonancia magnética confirmó la distensión, descrita por Boone como “moderada”.
La nueva lesión llega poco después del regreso de Judge a la alineación. El ocho veces All-Star había vuelto el 8 de septiembre después de permanecer fuera durante más de tres meses por una fractura de costilla.
Desde su regreso, Judge bateó para .174, con cuatro hits en 23 turnos, 13 ponches y un extrabase en siete encuentros. En total, durante la temporada registra promedio de .241, 18 cuadrangulares y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos.
Los Yankees, por su parte, podrían enfrentar nuevamente a los Boston Red Sox en la primera ronda de la postemporada. La situación de Judge representa una preocupación importante para Nueva York mientras se acerca el inicio de los playoffs.
“Hemos jugado gran parte del año sin él y, en su mayor parte, hemos hecho un trabajo bastante bueno”, señaló Boone. “Así que los muchachos están acostumbrados. Obviamente siempre quieres a tu mejor jugador en la mezcla, pero entendemos que tenemos un trabajo que hacer y una expectativa de ganar”.
“Creo que esa expectativa no cambia con o sin él. Esperamos entrar a la serie sabiendo que podemos vencer a cualquiera cuando jugamos nuestro juego”, concluyó el manager.

“El rango existe por una razón y estamos en un punto del año en el que, obviamente, lo forzamos un poco si eso estuviera sobre la mesa, pero eso es dentro de una semana. No lo espero, pero tampoco lo descarto”, agregó.
Aaron Judge volvió a lesionarse tras regresar de una fractura
El toletero se lesionó la pantorrilla durante el encuentro del miércoles pasado frente a los Minnesota Twins. Judge abandonó el partido en la sexta entrada para ser reemplazado por un bateador emergente debido a molestias en la pierna.
En un principio, el movimiento fue considerado como una medida de precaución, pero los síntomas persistieron y posteriormente una resonancia magnética confirmó la distensión, descrita por Boone como “moderada”.
La nueva lesión llega poco después del regreso de Judge a la alineación. El ocho veces All-Star había vuelto el 8 de septiembre después de permanecer fuera durante más de tres meses por una fractura de costilla.
Desde su regreso, Judge bateó para .174, con cuatro hits en 23 turnos, 13 ponches y un extrabase en siete encuentros. En total, durante la temporada registra promedio de .241, 18 cuadrangulares y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos.
Los Yankees, por su parte, podrían enfrentar nuevamente a los Boston Red Sox en la primera ronda de la postemporada. La situación de Judge representa una preocupación importante para Nueva York mientras se acerca el inicio de los playoffs.
“Hemos jugado gran parte del año sin él y, en su mayor parte, hemos hecho un trabajo bastante bueno”, señaló Boone. “Así que los muchachos están acostumbrados. Obviamente siempre quieres a tu mejor jugador en la mezcla, pero entendemos que tenemos un trabajo que hacer y una expectativa de ganar”.
“Creo que esa expectativa no cambia con o sin él. Esperamos entrar a la serie sabiendo que podemos vencer a cualquiera cuando jugamos nuestro juego”, concluyó el manager.

title: Yankees Quickly Make Anthony Volpe Change Amid Jazz Chisholm Jr. News
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Tuesday night, the New York Yankees will play the second game of their series with the Tampa Bay Rays.
They won the first (on Tuesday afternoon) by a score of 2-0.
Anthony Volpe (who started at second base) finished with three strikeouts and no hits.
UPDATE: The Yankees lost 6-1 in the second game.
Yankees Made Volpe Change Amid Chisholm Jr. News
Ahead of the second game, the Yankees announced that Jazz Chisholm Jr. has been activated off the injured list.
The Yankees wrote (via X): “Prior to Game 2 of today’s doubleheader, the Yankees made the following roster moves: • Reinstated INF Jazz Chisholm Jr. (#13) from the 10-day injured list. • Optioned INF/OF Max Schuemann to the FCL Yankees.”
The Yankees have also announced their starting lineup.
Underdog MLB wrote: “Yankees Game 2 9/22 B. Rice DH C. Bellinger LF H. Ramos RF L. García Jr. 1B S. Jones CF J. Chisholm Jr. 2B G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C R. McMahon 3B M. Fried SP”
Chisholm Jr. is starting at second base, while Volpe has been removed from the lineup.
Volpe is in the middle of his fourth season with the Yankees.
He is currently batting .248 with 51 hits, two home runs, 26 RBIs, 24 runs and 11 stolen bases in 66 games this year.

title: Rasmussen has 11 strikeouts as Rays clinch AL East with win over Yankees
author: The Associated Press
body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Drew Rasmussen allowed his only hit in the seventh inning and struck out 11 as the Tampa Bay Rays beat the New York Yankees 6-1 on Tuesday in the second game of a day-night doubleheader to clinch their fifth AL East title.
The Rays (96-61) secured home-field advantage throughout the American League playoffs and took their first division crown since 2021, when they won 100 games. Tampa Bay also earned AL East championships in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season along with 2010 and 2008, when the team had its first winning season after entering the league as an expansion franchise in 1998.
Yandy Díaz hit two-run single off reliever John Schreiber in the seventh and had another two-run single in the ninth for his AL-leading 175th hit. Tampa Bay opened a six-game lead over the second-place Yankees (90-67) with five to play.
In the opener, Carlos Rodón allowed three hits in eight sharp innings as New York delayed Tampa Bay's division celebration with a 2-0 victory.
Taylor Walls started the three-run seventh with a bunt single against Max Fried (5-5) when first base was left uncovered. Ryan Vilade hit an RBI groundout in the third after Díaz’s flyball moved runners to second and third.
Rasmussen (16-5) was nine outs from joining Matt Garza as Tampa Bay pitchers with a no-hitter when he gave up a leadoff double to Heliot Ramos on his 97th pitch. Garza held the Detroit Tigers hitless at Tropicana Field on July 26, 2010.
After allowing Ramos’ hit to left field, Rasmussen got the next two outs before walking Jazz Chisholm Jr. on a full count. Kevin Kelly entered and permitted rookie George Lombard Jr.’s RBI single before retiring Austin Wells on a groundout.
Rasmussen threw a career-high 114 pitches, 72 for strikes. He threw first-pitch strikes to 17 of 24 hitters and notched his fourth career double-digit strikeout game.
Rasmussen allowed one hit for the fourth time this year. He also yielded just one hit in six innings against the Yankees on April 12.
Cam Booser and Bryan Baker pitched an inning apiece to finish the three-hitter.
Fried allowed four runs and six hits in 6 2/3 innings.
The Yankees were held to three hits or fewer for the 13th time this year.
Up next
Tampa Bay RHP Ian Seymour (9-7, 4.38 ERA) opposes New York RHP Gerrit Cole (9-9, 3.63) on Wednesday night.
___
See AP’s full MLB coverage here
Larry Fleisher, The Associated Press

title: Yankees activate Jazz Chisholm Jr. for nightcap
author: George Bissell; Jazz Chisholm Jr
body:
Yankees activated 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. from the 10-day injured list.
            
                Chisholm returns to New York’s lineup for the nightcap of Tuesday’s doubleheader against the division-rival Rays following a nearly two-week absence recovering from a right thumb sprain. The dynamic 28-year-old power/speed combo threat has posted 19 homers and 40 steals in 134 games this season. He’s one round-tripper shy of the second 20-homer, 40-steal campaign of his career.

title: The Most Unforgettable Athletes To Ever Host 'SNL'
author: Mycolumbuspower Staff; Davonta Herring
body:
- SNL experiments with putting basketball, football, and other sports stars at the center of comedy.
Jalen Brunson’s victory lap is apparently still going. After leading the New York Knicks to their first NBA championship in 53 years and earning Finals MVP honors, the point guard will trade Madison Square Garden for Studio 8H when he hosts the Season 52 premiere of Saturday Night Live on September 26, 2026. KATSEYE will make its SNL debut as the music guest.
It’ll be Brunson’s first time hosting, and he’ll become the first Knicks player ever to host the show. He’s also the first active NBA player to get the gig since LeBron James opened Season 33 in 2007. Brunson has already been getting increasingly comfortable in the entertainment world — he recently popped up during the Emmys and filmed a guest appearance for Law & Order: SVU — though he joked ahead of SNL that he’s “probably not” prepared for whatever the writers are about to throw at him.
That uncertainty is part of what makes athletes on SNL so interesting. We normally see them in tightly controlled press conferences, commercials or postgame interviews, but sketch comedy requires them to loosen up, laugh at themselves and occasionally look completely ridiculous on live television. Since quarterback Fran Tarkenton became the first pro athlete to host in 1977, everyone from NBA legends and Super Bowl champions to tennis stars, Olympians and baseball players has stepped onto the SNL stage. Brunson will soon get his turn. Until then, here are some of the most memorable athletes who have hosted Saturday Night Live.
Michael Jordan (1991)
Fresh off his first NBA championship, Jordan hosted the Season 17 premiere on September 28, 1991, with Public Enemy serving as musical guest. His appearance in the Chicago-centric “Bill Swerski’s Super Fans” was practically inevitable, but his wonderfully straight-faced session with Al Franken’s Stuart Smalley in “Daily Affirmation” remains one of the best examples of SNL figuring out exactly how to use a superstar athlete.
Peyton Manning (2007)
Manning arrived at SNL only weeks after winning Super Bowl XLI and immediately proved he was willing to go all-in on the joke. His infamous United Way digital short flipped his wholesome quarterback image on its head by depicting him as an absolutely terrible influence on a group of children, and the sketch has remained tied to Manning’s comedy résumé ever since.
O.J. Simpson (1978)
Decades before the murder trial that would completely reshape his public image, Simpson hosted SNL on February 25, 1978, with Ashford & Simpson as musical guests. The episode included Simpson delivering his monologue as a Conehead and spoofing the famous Hertz commercials that had helped make him one of the most recognizable athlete endorsers in America.
Bill Russell (1979)
Russell became one of the earliest sports legends to host SNL when he took over Studio 8H on November 3, 1979, with Chicago as the musical guest. The NBA icon appeared throughout an episode that included “Sports Hotline,” “The Black Shadow,” and a Barry White-themed sketch, making Russell one of the show’s earliest experiments with putting a basketball superstar at the center of a comedy show.
Travis Kelce (2023)
Kelce was already known as one of the NFL’s biggest personalities before hosting in March 2023, but SNL gave him a chance to show that his charisma could translate outside of football. His episode leaned into everything from his reputation as an overly enthusiastic bro to the inherent comedy of seeing a 6-foot-5 NFL right end dropped into increasingly bizarre situations, helping kickstart an even bigger run for him in mainstream entertainment.
Charles Barkley (1993, 2010, 2012 & 2018)
Nobody on this list embraced SNL quite like Charles Barkley. Sir Charles has hosted four times, beginning with the 1993 season premiere alongside Nirvana and returning in 2010, 2012 and 2018, long after his playing career ended. His willingness to make fun of himself — and the same unfiltered personality that eventually made him a television star — made him unusually well suited for the format.
Derek Jeter (2001)
Yankees captain Derek Jeter hosted on December 1, 2001, at the height of his New York celebrity, with Shakira and Bubba Sparxxx appearing as music guests. Naturally, SNL went heavy on baseball, most memorably putting Jeter in drag as one of the “Baseball Wives” sitting in the Yankee Stadium stands alongside Rachel Dratch, Amy Poehler, Maya Rudolph and Ana Gasteyer.
Chris Evert (1989)
Tennis legend Chris Evert became one of the relatively few women athletes to host the show when she took the stage on November 11, 1989. Her episode immediately poked fun at her famously composed demeanor, opening with a sketch imagining Evert completely losing it after a Wimbledon defeat before she used her monologue to compare the pressure of live television to playing professional tennis.
Ronda Rousey (2016)
Rousey hosted in January 2016, only a few months after Holly Holm handed her the first loss of her MMA career. She addressed that defeat during her monologue before jumping into sketches including “Bland Man,” “Teacher’s Trial,” and a bit alongside Cecily Strong and musical guest Selena Gomez. The appearance came at an interesting moment in Rousey’s career, as she was beginning to move more heavily into movies, television and eventually professional wrestling.
Deion Sanders (1995)
There may never have been a host better suited to the phrase “Prime Time.” Sanders hosted in February 1995 while still famously balancing careers in the NFL and Major League Baseball, and SNL naturally leaned into his outsized personality with sketches about the baseball strike and the ESPYs. He even performed his own songs, “Must Be The Money” and “It’s On,” during the episode while Bon Jovi handled the official musical guest duties.
LeBron James (2007)
Just a few months after leading Cleveland to his first NBA Finals, a 22-year-old LeBron James hosted the Season 33 premiere on September 29, 2007. Kanye West was the musical guest, while James showed a playful side of himself in sketches that included Kristen Wiig’s increasingly absurd Penelope character and jokes about what his family was supposedly doing while he was busy hosting the show.
Wayne Gretzky (1989)
“The Great One” became the first hockey player to host SNL when he appeared on May 13, 1989, alongside musical guest Fine Young Cannibals. The writers unsurprisingly built plenty of material around hockey — including “Stanley Cup Loss” and “Wakiki Hockey” — while Gretzky also stepped into one of that era’s signature recurring sketches, “Wayne’s World.”
