title: Schlittler lanzando y Goldschmidt bateando dan a los Yankees la serie en Seattle - AGP Noticias
author: AGP Noticias
body:
Seattle, Washington.- Cam Schlittler lanzó un juego sin permitir carreras hasta la séptima entrada y Paul Goldschmidt conectó un jonrón de tres carreras, lo que permitió a los Yankees de Nueva York vencer a los Marineros de Seattle por 5-3 el miércoles.
Ben Rice también conectó un jonrón y un doble productor para los Yankees, que terminaron con un récord de 5-1 en su gira por la Costa Oeste al inicio de la temporada. Jugarán su primer partido en casa el viernes contra los Miami Marlins.
Schlittler (2-0) permitió dos hits en 6 1/3 entradas y retiró a sus últimos 16 bateadores, extendiendo su inicio de temporada sin permitir carreras. Ponchó a siete y no otorgó bases por bolas en 79 lanzamientos, 58 de ellos strikes.
El lanzador derecho de 25 años dejó a los Giants sin carreras durante 5 1/3 entradas el viernes pasado. Solo ha permitido tres hits esta temporada, mientras que ha ponchado a 15 bateadores. Tanto él como su compañero Max Fried no han permitido carreras en sus dos aperturas esta temporada.
Brendan Donovan abrió la parte baja de la primera entrada con un doble, pero fue el único jugador que llegó a segunda base contra Schlittler.
David Bednar necesitó 40 lanzamientos para conseguir los cuatro outs y lograr su tercer salvamento.
Nueva York tomó la delantera en la primera entrada con un doble productor de Rice, y Goldschmidt conectó un jonrón contra el abridor George Kirby (1-1) en la sexta entrada, su primer jonrón de la temporada. Fue el primer jonrón de Goldschmidt contra un lanzador diestro desde el 6 de junio.
Rice añadió un jonrón solitario en la novena entrada, su primer jonrón del año.
Cal Raleigh impulsó dos carreras para Seattle con un sencillo de bate roto ante Bednar con dos outs en la octava entrada, reduciendo la desventaja a 4-2. Dominic Canzone conectó un sencillo productor de carrera en la novena entrada.
Desde el partido del lunes por la noche, los lanzadores abridores de los Yankees no han permitido ninguna carrera en 16 entradas consecutivas.
A continuación
El lanzador derecho de los Yankees, Will Warren (0-0), abrirá el viernes contra el lanzador derecho de los Marlins, Eury Pérez (0-0).
El lanzador derecho de los Mariners, Bryan Woo (0-0), recibirá la pelota el viernes por la noche como visitante contra el lanzador zurdo de los Angels de Los Ángeles, Reid Detmers (0-0).
Información: AP.

title: Cam Schlittler laments what he couldn't do for Yankees with AL East hopes slipping away
author: Bob Nightengale
body:
Cam Schlittler laments what he couldn't do for Yankees with AL East hopes slipping away
PHOENIX — It was more than an hour since New York Yankees ace Cam Schlittler threw a pitch Saturday evening, and he was still upset with himself.
He had another strong performance in the Yankees’ 5-3 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks, one that just about every starter in baseball would take − but they’re not Schlittler.
They’re not demanding perfection.
They’re not having one of the greatest seasons in baseball history.
So, when you give up just three hits and one earned run in six innings, it’s not good enough.
Not when you’re cruising to the Cy Young award with a 14-6 record and 1.94 ERA, yielding no more than one earned run in 22 of 32 starts, the best mark in Yankees history.
The 24-year-old has looked like Bob Gibson on the road, yielding an insane 1.16 ERA, the third-lowest in MLB history in a pitcher’s first 17 road starts. The only pitchers with a lower road ERA are Gibson in 1968 and Claude Hendrix in 1914.
Still, Schlittler didn’t care about any of that. All he knows is that the Yankees lost on Pavin Smith’s pinch-hit, two-run homer in the ninth inning, and he blamed himself.
He was livid that he couldn’t field a bunt in the fifth inning by Tim Tawa, and paid the price by giving up a two-run triple to Jordan Lawlar, with both runs unearned, coughing up a 2-1 lead. And after the Yankees took a 3-2 lead in the top of the sixth, he ran into control problems, throwing eight consecutive balls, and gave the lead right back, 3-3.
His night was over after six innings.

title: Yankees' Aaron Boone Makes Statement on Spencer Jones Decision
author: Cole Sullivan
body:
The New York Yankees fell in heartbreaking fashion on Saturday night against the Los Angeles Dodgers, losing on a walk-off two-run shot from Pavin Smith.
New York is now 89-65 on the season and still sits firmly in the top Wild Card spot but trails the Tampa Bay Rays by five games for the AL East division.
Currently, the biggest concern for the Yankees stems from injuries, as Aaron Judge, Giancarlo Stanton, and Jazz Chisholm Jr. are all sidelined. Even rookie slugger Spencer Jones seems to be dealing with some type of foot injury.
Aaron Boone Makes Statement on Jones’ Decision
Fortunately, Jones’ injury does not seem serious as he said pregame it was “no big deal.”
In fact, Boone said that he was available off the bench during Saturday night’s game and ultimately explained why he didn’t use him as a pinch-hitter.
After a reporter asked Boone if Jones was available or if he was trying to stay away from him because of the injury, Boone made it clear that he would’ve gone to him if the right spot emerged.
“He was available, like I would’ve… if a spot came up to hit or we needed to do something I would’ve gone to him,” Boone said.
Aaron Boone speaks to the media following the Yankees 5-3 loss tonight in Arizona. pic.twitter.com/aeBBxybvHN
— YES Network (@YESNetwork) September 20, 2026
Looking at the Yankees
New York will play the Diamondbacks one more time on Sunday and then, after a day off Monday, will begin a massive four-game set with the Rays. If they can sweep the series, they could get back into the race over the final three games of the regular season.
On Tuesday, the two teams will play a doubleheader and then wrap it up across Wednesday and Thursday, with the Yankees likely throwing their top four guys in Max Fried, Carlos Rodon, Gerrit Cole, and Cam Schlittler.

title: Pavin Smith's pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees
author: Field Level Media
body:
Pavin Smith's pinch-hit, walk-off homer lifts D-backs over Yankees
(Photo credit: Arianna Grainey)
Pinch-hitter Pavin Smith hit a two-run walk-off homer with one out in the ninth and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat the New York Yankees 5-3 Saturday in Phoenix on a night the franchise celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series victory.
Ildemaro Vargas walked to lead off the ninth off Michael Fulmer (0-1), reaching base after he appealed the 3-2 pitch that originally was called a strike. After a strikeout, Smith hit a 389-foot homer to right center for the D-backs' 46th comeback win of the season
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells hit bases-empty homers for the Yankees, who had won four of five and eight of 10. Wells and Jose Caballero had two hits apiece.
Nolan Arenado had two hits and Jordan Lawlar added a two-run triple for the D-backs, who had lost three in a row and five of six.
The Yankees (89-65), who have clinched a playoff berth, fell five games behind Tampa Bay (94-60) in the AL East and remained 5 1/2 games ahead of Boston (84-71) for the top AL wild card spot. The Yankees and Rays play a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader Tuesday.
The D-backs (81-74) gained a game on Philadelphia (85-70) for the third spot in the National League wild-card race but are still four games back with seven games to play.
Yankees starter and American League Cy Young candidate Cam Schlittler gave up three hits and three runs (one earned) in six innings, leaving when his pitch count reached 98. His season high is 106.
Schlittler struck out three and walked six while lowering his ERA to an American League-leading 1.94. He has given up one earned run or fewer in each of his last eight starts.
Arizona starter Brandon Pfaadt gave up four singles and one run in 4 1/3 innings, leaving after the Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth. Ben Rice hit a sacrifice fly off Justin Martinez to break a scoreless tie. Pfaadt struck out three and walked one.
The D-backs broke up Schlittler's no-hitter with a two-run fifth. Both runs scored after Schlittler's one-out fielding error.
Arenado had Arizona's first hit, a line single to left field with one out, before Tim Tawa pushed a bunt toward the mound. Schlittler could not field the ball cleanly and both runners were safe.
Lawlar lined a two-out triple to left-center on a 99 mph fastball for a 2-1 lead.
Ramos and Wells homered in the sixth to put the Yankees in front 3-2.
The D-backs tied it in the sixth when Ketel Marte and Gabriel Moreno drew four-pitch walks and Geraldo Perdomo beat out a two-strike bunt single to load the bases. Corbin Carroll hit a sacrifice fly before Schlittler struck out Arenado and Tawa with runners on second and third.
--Field Level Media

title: Yankees let lead slip away in walk-off loss to Diamondbacks | Fingerlakes1.com
author: Facebook Com; Fingerlakes1; Kyle Evans
body:
The New York Yankees suffered a tough loss on Saturday night, falling to the Arizona Diamondbacks 5-3 on Pavin Smith’s two-run walk-off home run in the ninth inning.
The loss came after the Yankees twice held a lead earlier in the game. New York broke through in the fifth inning when Austin Wells, Anthony Volpe and José Caballero opened the frame with consecutive singles to load the bases. Ben Rice followed with a sacrifice fly that brought home Wells and put the Yankees ahead 1-0.
Arizona answered in the bottom half of the inning, taking a 2-1 lead on Jordan Lawler’s two-run triple. Both runs were unearned against Yankees starter Cam Schlittler, who committed a fielding error on a sacrifice bunt during the inning.
New York responded quickly in the sixth. Heliot Ramos tied the game with a solo home run before Wells put the Yankees back in front with his 13th home run of the season. Both home runs came against Arizona reliever Kevin Ginkel.
Schlittler ran into trouble again in the bottom of the sixth after issuing two walks and allowing a single to load the bases with nobody out. Corbin Carroll tied the game with a sacrifice fly, but Schlittler struck out the next two batters to escape further damage.
Schlittler completed six innings, allowing three runs on three hits with three walks and six strikeouts over 98 pitches. Only one of the three runs was earned, and his season earned-run average dropped to 1.94.
Neither team scored again until the ninth, when Smith ended the game with his two-run homer off Michael Fulmer.
The Yankees will finish the series Sunday at 4:10 p.m. Will Warren will face Corbin Burnes.

title: Yankees Star Cody Bellinger Makes Honest Statement After Diamondbacks Loss
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Saturday, the New York Yankees played the second game of their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
The Yankees lost by a score of 5-3.
Cody Bellinger finished with no hits in four at-bats.
Yankees Star Cody Bellinger Makes Honest Statement
After the game, Bellinger met with the media (via YES Network).
He gave several honest answers.
Reporter: “Offense kind of quiet tonight. Just what caused you guys to be shut down, especially early on?”
Bellinger: “Pfaadt did a pretty good job today. I think he pitched well. We had a few chances early on. Balls ended up in some gloves. And just a tough one today.”
Reporter: “How big a deal was winning the division? Teams have won from the wild card.”
Bellinger: “Obviously the goal is win the division, rest your guys, get those extra off days. And that’s always goal number one. Ultimately World Series champions have come out of the wild card. So keep on fighting for the division and just keep on rolling.”
Reporter: “Considering you guys have been without Aaron for a lot of the year, Giancarlo for almost the entire year, is there still some proudness of where you guys are at generally speaking?”
Bellinger: “Yeah. Something I love in here. There’s no excuses. Everyone in here show up to win. Got a few more games left and we just gotta keep on rolling.”

The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East with an 89-65 record in 154 games.
They have one more game with the Diamondbacks (on Sunday).
On Tuesday, the Yankees will return home to host the Tampa Bay Rays in the Bronx.

title: Yankees lose to Diamondbacks in walk-off fashion
author: Joshua Diemert
body:
One would figure that with Cam Schlittler going on Saturday night, this would be the game for the Yankees to win if they had any hope for a last-ditch AL East comeback, but something about Arizona wore down the likely Cy Young Award winner tonight. The Snakes were pesky, annoying, and other terms my editors won’t let me use while in the batter’s box tonight, finally breaking through on a Pavin Smith walk-off home run, to win it, 5-3.
Right off the top, I need to be grumpy about something. Nobody likes West Coast games and nobody likes the fact that every time the Yankees are on the West Coast, they play more night games than day games. This goes double for West Coast Yankee fans, because the beautiful thing about cheering for an East Coast team is they start playing when you get off work, or when you’re just finishing your Saturday morning coffee, the game takes three hours and you have the evening to yourself. That doesn’t happen on these trips.
Now, the Diamondbacks were celebrating the only World Series title in history, 25 years ago this season. I get it, you want to have a special event, the team isn’t very good so the end of the season starts to drag a little bit, you want a little spice. I even respect the cheek of waiting until the Yankees are in town. What I don’t respect is being completely incapable of running a functioning ceremony. The Yankees have Old Timer’s Day every year, they designate a special start time and at that time, the festivities have concluded and we can get down to the reason we’re all here, to watch a baseball game, which I don’t think is an unreasonable expectation at a baseball stadium with a baseball team in town.
The Diamondbacks started their pregame ceremonies at 4:30pm local time, with a scheduled 5:10pm first pitch. They absolutely blew past that in a way that, in my opinion, was both unprofessional and downright insulting. The four clocks I have ready access to in my apartment agreed: Brandon Pfaadt didn’t throw his first offering to Ben Rice until 5:42pm. This was an absolute joke of a start to the series’ second game. That all this happened in a city I’m predisposed to dislike already was…whatever the anti-cherry on top. I also firmly don’t like the existence of Phoenix as a city in general so I was always going to be ticked off watching this one.
I said in the gamethread that we had maybe begun to develop outsized expectations for Cam Schlittler. He’s been SO good, for long enough, that we needed to remember the other team all drives nice cars and lives in nice houses too. While Cam did get through 4.1 innings without allowing a hit, the Diamondbacks pushed a pair of runs across in the fifth. Nolan Arenado reached with a one-out single, before Tim Tawa attempted to give himself up with a sac bunt. Schlittler couldn’t corral what should have been an out though, an error that put two men on, and #9 hitter Jordan Lawlar made him pay:
Funny enough, because Schlittler was charged with that error, both of the runs were unearned, and he still hasn’t allowed more than a single earned run in eight starts now. The Yankees would tie the game the next inning, but all those extra pitches taxed his right arm, and I think had a major impact on what would happen in the sixth.
Speaking of tying the game, Heliot Ramos was brought to New York because of his opposite field power. He stunk in his first taste of East Coast baseball, but has looked much more representative in his last 20 games, and flexed that oppo pop within moments of Schlittler getting back in the dugout:
Corbin Carroll ran down a sinking Anthony Volpe liner for the second out, a very nice play that loomed larger when Austin Wells stepped to the plate:
Wells is getting hot at the right time, with three home runs in his last five games and he’s actually been a league average hitter since August 1! The nice thing about being a good defensive catcher is if you can just not embarrass yourself at the plate, you’re a major asset for your team.
The good vibes only lasted until Cam got back on the mound though. I think the error and the triple shook him up a little, and we’ve seen this happen before. Schlittler’s a high-energy guy, when that energy is less than positive I do think he gets a little in his own head and starts to overthrow. He walked the first two batters of the inning on eight total pitches, completely uncompetitive at-bats that are just so out of whack with what he’s done so far this season.
A soft Geraldo Perdomo bunt loaded the bases, and Cam did seem to lock in at that point. Corbin Carroll did bring in the third Snakes run of the game — and the only earned for Cam — but the ace got both Arenado and Tawa to whiff to end the threat. It was a weird one for Schlittler tonight, but 6.0 IP and one earned run is what the line reads.
The bullpen wasn’t exactly dynamite in Cam’s stead; the Diamondbacks have the third-lowest strikeout rate in baseball and their ability to grind out at-bats showed, even if the Yankees got through eight innings keeping the game tied at three. This was a long, miserable game, and wasn’t helped by the fact the Yankees couldn’t really find the nine-run spark that they showed on Friday.
If nothing else, I got to re-hate Michael Fulmer, and all those feelings from 2016 sprung forth anew. He walked the leadoff batter to open the ninth, and gave up the walk-off dinger to Pavin Smith:
The division race is functionally over with the Rays’ win earlier today, as they restored their five-game lead. Get yourself set for the Wild Card, lock up home-field advantage for that series, and don’t get yourselves hurt. The Yankes finish this series tomorrow with Will Warren on the hill. First pitch is supposedly at 4:10pm Eastern, but we’ll see.

title: Cam Schlittler Gets Great Sign For Entering AL MVP Race
author: Joey Haverford
body:
Second year pitcher Cam Schlittler is the strong American League Cy Young candidate, but he may have a chance at another award. The New York Yankees ace continues to add to the great body of work and saw his ERA dropping below 2.00 in recent weeks. Schlittler has an outside chance at the AL MVP Award since he's arguably the best player in the entire MLB right now.ESPN's Bradford Doolittle uses an advanced stats model, and it recently saw Schlittler moving up in the rankings via his AXE rating:
"Front-runner: Yordan Alvarez, Astros (146.9 AXE). Next: 2, Cam Schlittler, New York Yankees (143.0).
Schlitter has an uphill battle, but if I'd included pitchers in the MVP tables earlier, he would have been a fixture all season. Now he's earning a little buzz both in articles speculating on awards consideration and the betting markets. I don't think he'll win, but for a 2026 starting pitching to get so prominently mentioned, that tells you all you need to know about how dynamic he has been."
Doolittle confirmed that he expects Houston Astros slugger Alvarez to win the award since it's extremely difficult for pitchers to take home MVP. However, he made sure to note that Schlittler making this race at all shows he's having a historically great season for the contending Yankees roster.
How Cam Schlittler Can Win The MVP
Alvarez remains the strong favorite to win the AL MVP, but his Astros are still battling to make the playoffs. Houston is currently tied for first place in the American League West with the Texas Rangers both having 77-77 records. Voters could punish Alvarez for team success if the Astros miss the playoffs and finish with a record under .500. Schlittler must hope for some luck of Houston failing and finishing his season strong with the Yankees having the second-best American League record. An important start against the Tampa Bay Rays could see Schlittler having a "statement performance" if it helps the Yankees have a chance at the AL East title. Hitters getting the advantage in MVP voting requires Schlittler to finish perfectly to have a viable shot.
Current Betting Odds Hurt Cam Schlittler
Doolittle's model is fully based off advanced stats, and fan discussions do little to help Schlittler's case with baseball media. Current betting odds on various sports gambling sites see Schlittler still distantly behind Alvarez and Junior Caminero. Bet MGM has the following odds for viable American League MVP candidates, as of September 19, 2026;
Alvarez: -2000
Caminero: +1100
Schlittler: +6000
Unfortunately for the Yankees and Schlittler, the odds show that it may be too late for him to make up ground in the narratives. Alvarez has been considered the favorite since he started putting up strong slugging numbers early in the season. Schlittler should take pride in likely winning the Cy Young Award and even creating enough momentum to get any MVP consideration as a pitcher in 2026. The postseason will see Schlittler hoping to lead a rotation with Gerrit Cole and Max Fried to the World Series.

Doolittle confirmed that he expects Houston Astros slugger Alvarez to win the award since it's extremely difficult for pitchers to take home MVP. However, he made sure to note that Schlittler making this race at all shows he's having a historically great season for the contending Yankees roster.
How Cam Schlittler Can Win The MVP
Alvarez remains the strong favorite to win the AL MVP, but his Astros are still battling to make the playoffs. Houston is currently tied for first place in the American League West with the Texas Rangers both having 77-77 records. Voters could punish Alvarez for team success if the Astros miss the playoffs and finish with a record under .500. Schlittler must hope for some luck of Houston failing and finishing his season strong with the Yankees having the second-best American League record. An important start against the Tampa Bay Rays could see Schlittler having a "statement performance" if it helps the Yankees have a chance at the AL East title. Hitters getting the advantage in MVP voting requires Schlittler to finish perfectly to have a viable shot.
Current Betting Odds Hurt Cam Schlittler
Doolittle's model is fully based off advanced stats, and fan discussions do little to help Schlittler's case with baseball media. Current betting odds on various sports gambling sites see Schlittler still distantly behind Alvarez and Junior Caminero. Bet MGM has the following odds for viable American League MVP candidates, as of September 19, 2026;
Alvarez: -2000
Caminero: +1100
Schlittler: +6000
Unfortunately for the Yankees and Schlittler, the odds show that it may be too late for him to make up ground in the narratives. Alvarez has been considered the favorite since he started putting up strong slugging numbers early in the season. Schlittler should take pride in likely winning the Cy Young Award and even creating enough momentum to get any MVP consideration as a pitcher in 2026. The postseason will see Schlittler hoping to lead a rotation with Gerrit Cole and Max Fried to the World Series.

title: No, not as painful as '01 -- but this walk-off loss could prove costly to Yanks
author: Bryan Hoch
body:
ARIZONA – This one won’t hurt for the next 25 years, but it might sting for the next eight games.
On an evening when the D-backs turned back the clock to honor a World Series celebration that took place on this same diamond, it became the setting for another Yankees walk-off defeat – this one courtesy of Pavin Smith’s pinch-hit homer, sealing a 5-3 loss on Saturday at Chase Field.
Michael Fulmer took the loss, dropping the Yankees (89-65) five games behind the Rays (94-60) in the American League East with eight left to play, dimming their chances of avoiding a best-of-three AL Wild Card Series.
“We’ve got to go on a good run,” Cam Schlittler said. “It’s going to be tough. I think we’ve had opportunities all season to put ourselves ahead, and we haven’t done a great job of that. There’s still a chance, but we’ve got to play our [butts] off a little bit.”
Even with Saturday’s loss, the Yankees have won eight of 11, yet they have been unable to make up ground. The Rays walked off the Red Sox at Tropicana Field earlier Saturday, Tampa Bay’s seventh win in eight contests.
“They’re playing tremendous baseball. It’s tough to climb up in the standings if they keep winning,” Cody Bellinger said. “It’s mathematically pretty tough, but we’ve got to keep on rolling.”
The Yankees are scheduled to host the Rays for a four-game series that begins on Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
“We sweep, and then it gets interesting,” manager Aaron Boone said. “But you can’t sweep before [Sunday’s] game.”
The sight of Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling draped in purple and gold as they hoisted the championship trophy atop the infield – just as they did that November evening in 2001 – offered a gut punch for Yankees fans who can clearly picture Luis Gonzalez’s hit sailing over a drawn-in infield.
For the next generation, another was delivered later. The frontrunner to win the American League Cy Young Award, Schlittler was dominant early, holding Arizona hitless until Nolan Arenado’s fifth-inning single.
Tim Tawa followed with a bunt back to the mound that Schlittler couldn’t handle cleanly, the ball falling out of his right hand. Four pitches later, Jordan Lawlar laced a two-run triple to the gap in left-center field, giving Arizona its first lead of the game.
Because of Schlittler’s error, both runs were unearned – though that offered no consolation to the right-hander.
“I’ll take the blame for that,” Schlittler said. “I made an error there and let up two runs. That’s baseball, but that one is on me.”
Heliot Ramos and Austin Wells homered in the sixth, but an uncharacteristic loss of command allowed the D-backs to tie the score.
Schlittler threw eight consecutive pitches out of the zone, then Geraldo Perdomo loaded the bases with a bunt single that third baseman Ryan McMahon fielded but couldn’t make a play on.
Corbin Carroll jumped on a high fastball to lift a sac fly off Schlittler, who struck out the next two batters to wrap his outing.
Schlittler finished the evening with a 1.94 ERA, allowing three runs (one earned) and three hits over six innings, walking three and striking out six.
“I felt like I made an adjustment after the second inning,” Schlittler said. “I was missing a couple arm-side. I made a good adjustment and lost the zone there [in the sixth]. Ultimately, it cost me.”
Though Schlittler was dissatisfied with his performance, Boone said he thought the right-hander “threw the ball great.”
“To get us through that sixth, it was a good job there,” Boone said.
Schlittler’s final start of the regular season is lined up to come during the series against Tampa Bay in the Bronx, carrying some statistical weight.
Schlittler has also allowed one earned run or none in 24 starts this season, joining Sandy Koufax (25 in 1963, 24 in 1966) and Bob Gibson (24 in 1968) as the only pitchers in the Live Ball Era with at least 24 starts of one earned run or none in a season (excluding openers).
Yet all the Yankees care about is making those four games mean something in the AL East race.
“Obviously, the goal is to win the division, rest your guys and get those off-days,” Bellinger said. “That’s always goal number one. Ultimately, World Series champions have come out of the Wild Card. We’ll keep on fighting.”

title: MLB: José Caballero e Iván Herrera brillan con el bate y destacan con sus equipos
body:
Los Grandes Ligas panameños Iván Herrera y José Caballero tuvieron una impresionante jornada a la ofensiva con los Cardenales de San Luis y Yankees de Nueva York respectivamente, en los choques de la MLB disputados el sábado 19 de septiembre.
José Caballero se luce en Arizona - MLB
El "Chema" de 30 años se fue de 2-2 con 1 pasaporte en la derrota de los Yankees de Nueva York 5-3 frente a los Arizona Diamondbacks en el Chase Field.
"Cabby" ahora deja su promedio en .238 con 14 cuadrangulares, 51 empujadas, 49 anotadas y 32 bases robadas.

WELCOME TO THE EVENING SHADE, A SANCTUARY OF SANITY AFTER A LONG HARD DAY OF FIGHTING FASCISM.
YOU WILL FIND in the DIARIES a LOT of POLITICS (Or NOT As the CASE MAY BE) AND EVEN MORE CRITTERS. THE PERSON who MAKES the FIRST COMMENT WILL GET TWO CRITTERS. EVERY PERSON WHO COMMENTS WILL GET A CRITTER (OR LYNX TO A CRITTER)
The good news is that I found a trove of 50+ comics this morning. The bad news is that it took me a long time to get them set aside. I’m going to have to just categorize them and put them in a Google Doc for the other diarists to use what I don’t.
I’m way behind schedule.
News
The Guardian
A federal immigration officer wanted on assault charges for shooting and wounding a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis was arrested there on Wednesday, eight months after a confrontation that became a flashpoint over Donald Trump’s deportation sweeps.
Christian Castro, an Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent, was taken into custody by agents of the Minnesota bureau of criminal apprehension in Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin county jail on his outstanding arrest warrant, the agency said.
Castro had been released on bond from federal custody earlier this month, after an initial appearance in a district court in McAllen, Texas, on charges of lying to investigators about the circumstances of the 14 January shooting.
Under an agreement with Minnesota law enforcement, Castro voluntarily drove to Minneapolis from Texas to turn himself in to state authorities at his attorney’s office but ended up being arrested minutes before he was due to arrive, the lawyer, Daniel Gerdts, told Reuters.
Minnesota’s Moriarty and Ellison are pushing back against the assertion in the last paragraph that Castro had an agreement. Mary Moriarty said that Castro didn’t get to set the time and place of his arrest. That’s a weird flex that Castro and his lawyer were trying to pull.
This isn’t one of the killers (that I know of) in the Twin Cities last winter. Not for lack of trying. He shot into a residence and his bullet lodged in the bedroom wall where a child was. Then Castro and his partner lied about the incident until video emerged. The US Attorney then dropped all charges against the victims and Castro fled to Texas, into the warm, loving embrace of Greg Abbott, who wouldn’t willingly give up his boy-toy.
===
Nifty gave us an upbeat story of a similar ilk (but before Chicago’s own occupation) in the comments of yesterday’s GNR. Note that these crimes occurred before Chicago’s Midway Blitz.
Chicago Sun Times
It simply didn’t matter whether Luis Uribe’s victims were sex workers.
That’s what a prosecutor told jurors this week when he asked for a guilty verdict against the U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer who used his gun and badge to commit violent sexual assaults.
It’s possible for a sex worker to be raped, Assistant U.S. Attorney Richard Rothblatt reminded the jury. For them to be robbed. “Sex workers,” he said, “can be credible.”
The jury agreed Thursday, siding with four women over a federal law enforcement officer whose lawyer called the victims “liars” and “hustlers.” The panel concluded that Uribe, 45, sexually assaulted the women in Chicago’s suburbs in 2022, convicting him of a series of crimes that could put him in prison for the rest of his life.
They also rejected Uribe’s claim that he’d been set up by a Chinese prostitution ring because he wouldn’t help them circumvent U.S. immigration law — an explanation Uribe delivered from the witness stand amid testimony in which he was accused of telling a “rape joke.” ✂️
It’s a disturbing story. It reinforces that there needs to be reform of ICE and CBP.

Since we’ve shifted to Chicago, Kat Abughazaleh has a book about organizing that drops as a free download on Monday. You can get a hard (spiral bound) copy for a $50 or more donation. Or as I call it, less than the price of a tank of gas.
Here’s the link to the download. Here’s the link to the donation page for the PAC for those that want a hard copy ($50 or more donation).
===
Michigan Advance
The family of a woman who died after she could not get an abortion in Texas is suing doctors and state officials including Attorney General Ken Paxton. It is the first lawsuit over a death linked to an abortion ban.
“It’s horrible that she’s gone and she was taken from us this way. It’s horrible that she’s not here anymore,” said LaTanya Walker, Tierra Walker’s aunt and the lead plaintiff in the case, in a press conference Wednesday. She added: “I want justice for her. I want it to not happen to anyone else. It needs to stop.”
The case, filed Tuesday in state court by a malpractice firm and the abortion rights group Amplify Legal, argues that Texas’ abortion bans violate both the state and U.S. Constitution. This case is also the first to directly sue Paxton, who has taken a leading role in enforcing Texas’ ban. Paxton is locked in a tight race for the U.S. Senate.
“Tierra Walker is dead and those responsible must be held accountable,” the suit reads. “At every turn, Texas’s political and medical establishments not only failed but actively harmed Ms. Walker.”
Walker is one of the numerous women whose deaths have been linked to abortion bans. Other deaths have occurred in North Carolina and Georgia, states with bans less restrictive than Texas’. Texas’ near-total abortion ban provides exceptions only if staying pregnant puts someone “at risk of death or poses a serious risk of substantial impairment of a major bodily function.” In 2025 — after Walker’s death — the state passed a law meant to clarify what constitutes a risk of death. But the penalties for violating the state’s ban remain onerous, and many doctors have said it is not obvious what care they can provide or how sick a patient must be before they can intervene. ✂️

Hat tip to Girasol for the heads up on this next item.
Boise State Public Radio
Parent company McClatchy Media laid off 10 journalists and three editors at the Idaho Statesman on Thursday.
Michael Lycklama, chair of the Idaho News Guild, the union representing most Statesman reporters, said that’s 60% of the newsroom.
Lycklama was a sports reporter for the paper for 12 years. He said he got an email Thursday morning notifying him of an HR meeting 30 minutes later.
“That was all the notice that I got, and got a nonsensical explanation that didn’t explain any reasons why they’re doing the things that they’re doing,” he said.
McClatchy laid off staff in newsrooms across the country. An exact count is unknown, but Poynter reports at least 90 journalists have been affected across 13 papers.
The New York Times reports McClatchy told employees subscriber revenue had fallen 41%. A layoff notice McClatchy sent to union leadership and shared with Boise State Public Radio listed shifting subscriber interests and changes in the ways people engage with news as the reason for its restructuring. The company said it is focusing resources on journalism, subscriber value and what serves local communities. ✂️
===
Virginia Mercury
Gov. Abigail Spanberger on Friday unveiled a package of legislative proposals to rein in the data center industry in Virginia, with goals to tighten environmental regulations, increase cost allocation for the industry, and make the proposal process more transparent by barring non-disclosure agreements between localities and data center developers.
The plan does not include a moratorium on data center development while the details of the plan are refined, a step several environmental and advocacy groups and citizens have demanded in recent weeks.
Dubbed the “Data Center Accountability Framework,” Spanberger’s plan outlines five pillars as key priorities: transparency, environmental protections, lowering energy costs, promoting clean energy, and focusing on local workers.
“The Framework is a thorough plan to end data center secrecy, protect our environment, lower energy costs for families, bolster our clean energy economy, and make sure Virginia workers have the protections and assurances they deserve,” Spanberger said in a press conference to announce the plan at the Virginia State Capitol.
Spanberger also signed Executive Order 22, which will kick-start her plans for clamping down on the industry ahead of the next legislative session that will begin in January 2027. ✂️
===
===
Alaska Beacon
On the day that his campaign announced it had accepted hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations from employees of a California-based artificial intelligence company, Democratic governor candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said that if elected, he will seek to temporarily ban new computing data centers in Alaska.
As Americans grow frustrated with artificial intelligence software and concerned about the side effects of data centers, they have become a major issue in this year’s midterm elections. Alaska’s gubernatorial race is no exception, particularly since the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority announced plans for a development that could include data centers in Southcentral Alaska.
All four candidates — Republicans Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson and the Democratic Kreiss-Tomkins — have staked out different policy positions before Alaskans vote this fall.
Data centers need reliable connections to the internet, cheap electricity and a cooling method. Currently, the North Slope is the most promising location for all three.
One $500 million proposal on the North Slope intends to burn local natural gas for power and use the natural cold air of the Arctic.
Another shipping-container-sized plan involves a gas-powered data center processing Bitcoin. ✂️

Today is…*
*Attributions to WineRev refer to his entries in his History Corner diary. I didn’t use his material today, but I do often enough that he has a perpetual attribution in my Shades.
Birthdays
William Sellers (1824-1905) – American engineer and inventor (US standard screw thread), born in Upper Darby, Pennsylvania.
[if he hadn’t been born, we wouldn’t be screwed]
Karen Aabye (1904 -1982) – Danish journalist, author (Min bedstemor er jomfru (My Grandmother is a Virgin)), and WWII resistance fighter, born in Copenhagen, Denmark.
Danish writer. In the late 1930s, she worked as a journalist in Paris and London before she gained popularity with a number of historical novels in which strong-willed women were her main characters. Her works also include travel books and a collection of essays. ✂️ [Wikipedia]
Leon Jaworski (1905-1982) – American Watergate scandal special prosecutor, born in Waco, Texas.
Sir William Golding was a British novelist, poet, and playwright best known for his debut novel “Lord of the Flies”, published in 1954. Throughout his career, he wrote 12 fiction novels, three non-fiction works, and various collections.
Golding is most notable for winning the 1983 Nobel Prize in Literature, and was knighted only five years later for his contributions to literature in 1988. He was also a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.
Golding attended Brasenose College, Oxford, as a science major before transferring to English for his final two years. After graduating in 1934, his book of poems was published by Macmillan & Co. He later became a schoolmaster teaching various subjects and served in the Royal Navy during World War II.
In 2008, Golding was ranked third on The Times’ list of 50 greatest British writers since 1945.
Frances Farmer (1913-1970) – American actress (Son of Fury, Flowing Gold, Among the Living), born in Seattle, Washington.
Jay Ward (1920-1989) – Cartoonist and illustrator who created The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends.
(1:56)
Adam West [William West Anderson] (1928-2017) – American actor (Batman, Last Precinct), born in Walla Walla, Washington
(0:49)
After being discharged from the army, in part due to his homosexuality, and then pursuing training as an actor, Brian Epstein joined his family’s retail business, running their North End Music Store (known as NEMS). He expanded the inventory from pianos and radios to include records, while also writing a column in ‘Mersey Beat’ a local music magazine.
After a customer request for an early recording that the Beatles made backing Tony Sheridan in Germany, Epstein went to see the group perform. He immediately saw their potential and with no experience in the business, became their manager. He polished their image and secured a proper record contract. The success he had with the Beatles enabled him to expand his roster of clients to include other Liverpudlian acts: Gerry and the Pacemakers, Cilla Black, and Billy J. Kramer and The Dakotas.
Bra Willie [Keorapetse Kgositsile](1938-2018) – South African poet (When the Clouds Clear; My Name Is Afrika; Point of Departure), and political activist, born in Johannesburg, South Africa
“Mama” Cass gained fame as part of the 1960s folk-pop vocal quartet the Mamas & the Papas. The group was together from 1965 until 1968, before personal issues tore them apart. They released 4 albums and had 6 Top-Ten singles, including “California Dreamin’” and “Monday, Monday”.
“Dream A Little Dream of Me” recorded by the group, was released as a single giving Elliot top billing, and launching her solo career. Elliot would go on to released 4 studio albums and a live set, with her biggest hit being “Make Your Own Kind of Music”. A final group album was recorded in 1971 – mostly with individual parts overdubbed – to complete contract obligations.
After some ups and downs, and health and substance issues, Elliot settled into a nightclub and theater routine that was proving successful and fulfilling. After a two-week run at London’s Palladium, she died in her sleep of a heart attack at 32.
She was inducted in to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1998, and received a star on the Hollywood walk of Fame in 2022.
(Lawrence) “Lol” Creme (1947-Still Living) – English rock vocalist, songwriter, keyboardist, guitarist (10cc – “I’m Not On Love”, “The Things We Do for Love; Godley & Creme – “Cry”), and music video director, born in Prestwich, Lancashire, England
Daniel Lanois (1951-Still Living) – Canadian record producer (Brian Eno; U2; Peter Gabriel; Bob Dylan), and singer-songwriter, born in Hull, Quebec

WELCOME TO THE EVENING SHADE, A SANCTUARY OF SANITY AFTER A LONG HARD DAY OF FIGHTING FASCISM.
YOU WILL FIND in the DIARIES a LOT of POLITICS (Or NOT As the CASE MAY BE) AND EVEN MORE CRITTERS. THE PERSON who MAKES the FIRST COMMENT WILL GET TWO CRITTERS. EVERY PERSON WHO COMMENTS WILL GET A CRITTER (OR LYNX TO A CRITTER)
The good news is that I found a trove of 50+ comics this morning. The bad news is that it took me a long time to get them set aside. I’m going to have to just categorize them and put them in a Google Doc for the other diarists to use what I don’t.
I’m way behind schedule.
News
The Guardian
A federal immigration officer wanted on assault charges for shooting and wounding a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis was arrested there on Wednesday, eight months after a confrontation that became a flashpoint over Donald Trump’s deportation sweeps.
Christian Castro, an Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent, was taken into custody by agents of the Minnesota bureau of criminal apprehension in Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin county jail on his outstanding arrest warrant, the agency said.
Castro had been released on bond from federal custody earlier this month, after an initial appearance in a district court in McAllen, Texas, on charges of lying to investigators about the circumstances of the 14 January shooting.
Under an agreement with Minnesota law enforcement, Castro voluntarily drove to Minneapolis from Texas to turn himself in to state authorities at his attorney’s office but ended up being arrested minutes before he was due to arrive, the lawyer, Daniel Gerdts, told Reuters.
Minnesota’s Moriarty and Ellison are pushing back against the assertion in the last paragraph that Castro had an agreement. Mary Moriarty said that Castro didn’t get to set the time and place of his arrest. That’s a weird flex that Castro and his lawyer were trying to pull.
This isn’t one of the killers (that I know of) in the Twin Cities last winter. Not for lack of trying. He shot into a residence and his bullet lodged in the bedroom wall where a child was. Then Castro and his partner lied about the incident until video emerged. The US Attorney then dropped all charges against the victims and Castro fled to Texas, into the warm, loving embrace of Greg Abbott, who wouldn’t willingly give up his boy-toy.
===
Nifty gave us an upbeat story of a similar ilk (but before Chicago’s own occupation) in the comments of yesterday’s GNR. Note that these crimes occurred before Chicago’s Midway Blitz.
Chicago Sun Times
It simply didn’t matter whether Luis Uribe’s victims were sex workers.
That’s what a prosecutor told jurors this week when he asked for a guilty verdict against the U.S. Customs and Border Protection officer who used his gun and badge to commit violent sexual assaults.
It’s possible for a sex worker to be raped, Assistant U.S. Attorney Richard Rothblatt reminded the jury. For them to be robbed. “Sex workers,” he said, “can be credible.”
The jury agreed Thursday, siding with four women over a federal law enforcement officer whose lawyer called the victims “liars” and “hustlers.” The panel concluded that Uribe, 45, sexually assaulted the women in Chicago’s suburbs in 2022, convicting him of a series of crimes that could put him in prison for the rest of his life.
They also rejected Uribe’s claim that he’d been set up by a Chinese prostitution ring because he wouldn’t help them circumvent U.S. immigration law — an explanation Uribe delivered from the witness stand amid testimony in which he was accused of telling a “rape joke.” ✂️
It’s a disturbing story. It reinforces that there needs to be reform of ICE and CBP.

===

Michigan Advance
The family of a woman who died after she could not get an abortion in Texas is suing doctors and state officials including Attorney General Ken Paxton. It is the first lawsuit over a death linked to an abortion ban.
“It’s horrible that she’s gone and she was taken from us this way. It’s horrible that she’s not here anymore,” said LaTanya Walker, Tierra Walker’s aunt and the lead plaintiff in the case, in a press conference Wednesday. She added: “I want justice for her. I want it to not happen to anyone else. It needs to stop.”
The case, filed Tuesday in state court by a malpractice firm and the abortion rights group Amplify Legal, argues that Texas’ abortion bans violate both the state and U.S. Constitution. This case is also the first to directly sue Paxton, who has taken a leading role in enforcing Texas’ ban. Paxton is locked in a tight race for the U.S. Senate.
“Tierra Walker is dead and those responsible must be held accountable,” the suit reads. “At every turn, Texas’s political and medical establishments not only failed but actively harmed Ms. Walker.”
Walker is one of the numerous women whose deaths have been linked to abortion bans. Other deaths have occurred in North Carolina and Georgia, states with bans less restrictive than Texas’. Texas’ near-total abortion ban provides exceptions only if staying pregnant puts someone “at risk of death or poses a serious risk of substantial impairment of a major bodily function.” In 2025 — after Walker’s death — the state passed a law meant to clarify what constitutes a risk of death. But the penalties for violating the state’s ban remain onerous, and many doctors have said it is not obvious what care they can provide or how sick a patient must be before they can intervene. ✂️

Parent company McClatchy Media laid off 10 journalists and three editors at the Idaho Statesman on Thursday.
Michael Lycklama, chair of the Idaho News Guild, the union representing most Statesman reporters, said that’s 60% of the newsroom.
Lycklama was a sports reporter for the paper for 12 years. He said he got an email Thursday morning notifying him of an HR meeting 30 minutes later.
“That was all the notice that I got, and got a nonsensical explanation that didn’t explain any reasons why they’re doing the things that they’re doing,” he said.
McClatchy laid off staff in newsrooms across the country. An exact count is unknown, but Poynter reports at least 90 journalists have been affected across 13 papers.
The New York Times reports McClatchy told employees subscriber revenue had fallen 41%. Gov. Alaska’s gubernatorial race is no exception, particularly since the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority announced plans for a development that could include data centers in Southcentral Alaska.
All four candidates — Republicans Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson and the Democratic Kreiss-Tomkins — have staked out different policy positions before Alaskans vote this fall.
Data centers need reliable connections to the internet, cheap electricity and a cooling method. Currently, the North Slope is the most promising location for all three.
One $500 million proposal on the North Slope intends to burn local natural gas for power and use the natural cold air of the Arctic.
Another shipping-container-sized plan involves a gas-powered data center processing Bitcoin. ✂️

On the day that his campaign announced it had accepted hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations from employees of a California-based artificial intelligence company, Democratic governor candidate Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins said that if elected, he will seek to temporarily ban new computing data centers in Alaska.
As Americans grow frustrated with artificial intelligence software and concerned about the side effects of data centers, they have become a major issue in this year’s midterm elections. Alaska’s gubernatorial race is no exception, particularly since the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority announced plans for a development that could include data centers in Southcentral Alaska.
All four candidates — Republicans Dave Bronson, Treg Taylor and Bernadette Wilson and the Democratic Kreiss-Tomkins — have staked out different policy positions before Alaskans vote this fall.
Data centers need reliable connections to the internet, cheap electricity and a cooling method. Currently, the North Slope is the most promising location for all three.
One $500 million proposal on the North Slope intends to burn local natural gas for power and use the natural cold air of the Arctic.
Another shipping-container-sized plan involves a gas-powered data center processing Bitcoin. ✂️

Birthdays
William Sellers (1824-1905) – American engineer and inventor (US standard screw thread), born in Upper Darby, Pennsylvania.
[if he hadn’t been born, we wouldn’t be screwed]
Karen Aabye (1904 -1982) – Danish journalist, author (Min bedstemor er jomfru (My Grandmother is a Virgin)), and WWII resistance fighter, born in Copenhagen, Denmark.
Danish writer. In the late 1930s, she worked as a journalist in Paris and London before she gained popularity with a number of historical novels in which strong-willed women were her main characters. Her works also include travel books and a collection of essays. ✂️ [Wikipedia]
Leon Jaworski (1905-1982) – American Watergate scandal special prosecutor, born in Waco, Texas.
Sir William Golding was a British novelist, poet, and playwright best known for his debut novel “Lord of the Flies”, published in 1954. Throughout his career, he wrote 12 fiction novels, three non-fiction works, and various collections.
Golding is most notable for winning the 1983 Nobel Prize in Literature, and was knighted only five years later for his contributions to literature in 1988. He was also a fellow of the Royal Society of Literature.
Golding attended Brasenose College, Oxford, as a science major before transferring to English for his final two years. After graduating in 1934, his book of poems was published by Macmillan & Co. He later became a schoolmaster teaching various subjects and served in the Royal Navy during World War II.
In 2008, Golding was ranked third on The Times’ list of 50 greatest British writers since 1945.
Frances Farmer (1913-1970) – American actress (Son of Fury, Flowing Gold, Among the Living), born in Seattle, Washington.
Jay Ward (1920-1989) – Cartoonist and illustrator who created The Adventures of Rocky and Bullwinkle and Friends.
(1:56)
Adam West [William West Anderson] (1928-2017) – American actor (Batman, Last Precinct), born in Walla Walla, Washington
(0:49)
After being discharged from the army, in part due to his homosexuality, and then pursuing training as an actor, Brian Epstein joined his family’s retail business, running their North End Music Store (known as NEMS). He expanded the inventory from pianos and radios to include records, while also writing a column in ‘Mersey Beat’ a local music magazine.
After a customer request for an early recording that the Beatles made backing Tony Sheridan in Germany, Epstein went to see the group perform. He immediately saw their potential and with no experience in the business, became their manager. He polished their image and secured a proper record contract. The success he had with the Beatles enabled him to expand his roster of clients to include other Liverpudlian acts: Gerry and the Pacemakers, Cilla Black, and Billy J. Kramer and The Dakotas.
Bra Willie [Keorapetse Kgositsile](1938-2018) – South African poet (When the Clouds Clear; My Name Is Afrika; Point of Departure), and political activist, born in Johannesburg, South Africa

In 1796, President George Washington’s farewell address was published. In it, America’s first chief executive advised, “Observe good faith and justice toward all nations. Cultivate peace and harmony with all.”
In 1881, the 20th president of the United States, James A. Garfield, died 2 1/2 months after being shot by Charles Guiteau; he was succeeded by Vice President Chester A. Arthur.
In 1893 New Zealand becomes the first country to grant all women the right to vote.
(6:57)
In 1955, President Juan Peron of Argentina was ousted after a revolt by the army and navy.
In 1957, the United States conducted its first contained underground nuclear test, code-named “Rainier,” in the Nevada desert.
In 1985, the Mexico City area was struck by a devastating earthquake that killed at least 9,500 people.
In 1988, Olympic diver Greg Louganis suffered a concussion after striking his head on the diving board during the preliminary round of the 3-meter springboard diving competition at the Seoul Summer Games; Louganis would recover from the injury and win a gold medal in the event the following day.
In 1995, The New York Times and The Washington Post published the manifesto of Unabomber Ted Kaczynski (kah-ZIHN’-skee), which proved instrumental in identifying and capturing him.
[with AI, the Unibomber is being proven right. I’m not endorsing his actions, but the reasoning was sound]
In 2004, Hu Jintao (hoo jin-tow) became the undisputed leader of China with the departure of former President Jiang Zemin (jahng zuh-MEEN’) from his top military post.
In 2008, struggling to stave off financial catastrophe, the Bush administration laid out a radical bailout plan calling for a takeover of a half-trillion dollars or more in worthless mortgages and other bad debt held by tottering institutions. Relieved investors sent stocks soaring on Wall Street and around the globe.
In 2011, Mariano Rivera of the New York Yankees recorded his 602nd save, making him baseball’s all-time leader in the category.
In 2022, Great Britain and the world said a final goodbye to Queen Elizabeth II at a state funeral that drew presidents and kings, princes and prime ministers — and crowds who thronged the streets of London.

National Days
Yar harrr! Ahoy there ye lily livered blaggards! Talk Like a Pirate Day means it’s time for pillaging and the imbibing of rum!
Pirates have been all the rage in recent years, and out of that particular fascination came an insane and completely pirate-oriented idea: that there should be a day dedicated to keeping the piratical language alive and, more importantly, the tradition of all things related to pirates.
So Talk Like a Pirate Day was invented. And now it’s time to celebrate with all of the pirate talk that can be mustered in one day!
=
Software Freedom Day is all about giving people the keys to their own digital world. It celebrates software that anyone can use, share, or change—no locked doors, no hidden rules.
On this day, folks from all walks of life come together to talk about how tech can stay fair and open. It’s not just for programmers; it’s for parents, students, workers—anyone who’s ever clicked a mouse or tapped a screen.
In friendly gatherings around the world, people trade stories, try out new tools, and help each other understand what “free software” really means. Some discover apps that can replace expensive programs.
Others get inspired to join global projects where their ideas actually matter. Everyone walks away knowing more and feeling more in control.
That’s the real magic—turning complex code into something simple, helpful, and truly shared.
=
As National Dance Day approaches, dance studios and activewear brands typically roll out exciting promotions. In 2026, expect special class rates from local studios like Arthur Murray Dance Centers and Fred Astaire Dance Studios, encouraging new sign-ups. Retailers such as Capezio and Bloch often offer discounts on dancewear and shoes. Fitness apps like Steezy Studio may feature free trial periods or reduced subscription costs for their online classes. Even entertainment venues might host special dance nights or themed events. We will update this page with confirmed live deals as September 19 approaches.

Dive into Gotham’s world through classic comics, blockbuster films, and thrilling animated series. Join the global celebration by dressing up, re-reading your favorite stories, and sharing your love for the Dark Knight.

title: MLB playoff picture: Updated standings, postseason matchups and teams still alive
author: Jake Elman
body:
Those following the Major League Baseball postseason picture will see and hear the term “earn” frequently mentioned within the coming days, which isn’t exactly the word that comes to mind upon looking at the standings.
Outside of the 60-game 2020 season, we’ve never seen a losing team make the playoffs. Depending on how the next eight days play out, there could be four American League teams that finish with 81 or fewer wins yet qualify for the playoffs.
The easiest way to keep tabs on how close teams are to clinching is by looking at magic numbers. The formula to calculate a magic number is as follows, per MLB.com:
- Games remaining +1 - (Losses by second place team - losses by first place team)
American League standings and playoff picture
For all intents and purposes, the Red Sox have clinched a playoff berth; they entered Saturday with their magic number sitting at two, and they’re so far ahead in the Wild Card standings that they’re all but locked into a first-round matchup with the Yankees. It’d be the fourth time in less than a decade these two have met in the playoffs, and the Red Sox look to avenge last year’s Wild Card Series loss.
The AL Central and AL West are, shall we say, messy. Houston holds the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas and is only two games back of Cleveland for the AL’s No. 2 seed. Meanwhile, the White Sox have a one-game lead over the Rangers for the final Wild Card berth, and we could realistically see three of those teams make the postseason with a losing record.
| Team | Record | Games back | 
|---|---|---|
| Tampa Bay Rays | 93-60 | -- | 
| Cleveland Guardians | 79-75 | 14.5 | 
| Houston Astros | 77-77 | 16.5 | 
| New York Yankees | 89-64 (WC) | 4 | 
| Boston Red Sox | 84-70 (WC) | 9.5 | 
| Chicago White Sox | 78-76 (WC) | 15.5 | 
| Texas Rangers | 77-77 (OUT) | 16.5 | 
| Toronto Blue Jays | 76-78 (OUT) | 16.5 | 
| Baltimore Orioles | 75-79 (OUT) | 18.5 | 
If the regular season ended today, here's a look at what the AL Wild Card round matchups would look like.
- Bye: (1) Tampa Bay Rays
- Bye: (2) Cleveland Guardians
- (3) Houston Astros vs. (6) Chicago White Sox
- (4) New York Yankees vs. (5) Boston Red Sox
National League standings and playoff picture
The only thing that’s changed in the National League is how crowded the Wild Card race has become. Barring a collapse over the season’s final week, we’re all but assured of the Cubs, Phillies, and Padres being the three Wild Card teams. That’s been the case for most of September, as has the Braves being the No. 3 seed and NL East champions.
How the seeding will work, though, is where things get interesting. The Cubs, Phillies, and Padres all began Saturday at 85-69, and they’d be seeded in that order; No. 4 Chicago would host No. 5 Philadelphia, and No. 6 San Diego would play at Atlanta.
Unfortunately for the Phillies, they close the regular season with a six-game homestand against the Brewers and Rays. Both teams are still fighting for the top seeds in their respective leagues, so don’t expect them to go lightly on Don Mattingly’s club.
| Team | Record | Games back | 
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee Brewers | 93-60 | -- | 
| Los Angeles Dodgers | 79-75 | 2.0 | 
| Atlanta Braves | 77-77 | 6.0 | 
| Chicago Cubs | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 | 
| Philadelphia Phillies | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 | 
| San Diego Padres | 85-69 (WC) | 11.0 | 
| Arizona Diamondbacks | 80-74 (OUT) | 16.0 | 
If the regular season ended today, here’s a look at what the NL Wild Card round matchups would look like.
- Bye: (1) Milwaukee Brewers
- Bye: (2) Los Angeles Dodgers
- (3) Atlanta Braves vs. (6) San Diego Padres
- (4) Chicago Cubs vs. (5) Philadelphia Phillies
MLB magic numbers: Which AL teams are closest to clinching a playoff spot?
| Team | Magic number | Elimination number | 
|---|---|---|
| Tampa Bay Rays | CLINCHED | -- | 
| Cleveland Guardians | 7 | -- | 
| Houston Astros | 8 | -- | 
| New York Yankees | CLINCHED | -- | 
| Boston Red Sox | 2 | -- | 
| Chicago White Sox | 7 | 8 | 
| Texas Rangers |  | 8 | 
| Toronto Blue Jays |  | 6 | 
| Baltimore Orioles |  | 6 | 
| Detroit Tigers |  | 3 | 
| Seattle Mariners |  | 4 | 
| Minnesota Twins |  | 3 | 
| Kansas City Royals | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| Athletics | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| Los Angeles Angels | -- | ELIMINATED | 
As we said, half of the AL playoff picture has essentially already been determined. Only three games separate the White Sox and Orioles, who are still mathematically alive despite entering Saturday with a 75-79 record. Let’s also not forget about the 76-78 Blue Jays, who are only two games back of the White Sox.
We recently referenced the 2008 Yankees, who missed the playoffs at 89-73 and watched the Dodgers win the NL West with 84 wins. If we created a portal and grabbed that Yankees team, they’d be the AL’s No. 4 seed if the playoffs began tomorrow, and it wouldn’t be close. Great job, all.
But hey, we objectively love chaos, so we’re in the minority in loving the AL playoff picture.
MLB magic numbers: Which NL teams are closest to clinching a playoff spot?
There’s not much else to say about the National League playoff picture. The teams that haven’t officially locked up a playoff berth should do so within the coming days, and the Diamondbacks’ tragic number dropped to four following Friday night’s loss to the Yankees.
| Team | Magic number | Elimination number | 
|---|---|---|
| Milwaukee Brewers | CLINCHED | -- | 
| Los Angeles Dodgers | CLINCHED | -- | 
| Atlanta Braves | CLINCHED | -- | 
| Chicago Cubs | 3 | -- | 
| Philadelphia Phillies | 4 | -- | 
| San Diego Padres | 4 | -- | 
| Arizona Diamondbacks | -- | 4 | 
| Pittsburgh Pirates | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| Miami Marlins | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| St. Louis Cardinals | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| Washington Nationals | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| Cincinnati Reds | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| New York Mets | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| San Francisco Giants | -- | ELIMINATED | 
| Colorado Rockies | -- | ELIMINATED | 
It’s hard not to feel bad for the Rockies. Despite not blowing up their roster at the trade deadline, they're 13-31 since Aug. 1, and they haven't had a winning streak longer than four games all year. Warren Schaeffer’s club is two losses away from its fourth consecutive 100-loss season, and they’ve been outscored by nearly 200 runs.
But considering they went 43-119 last year, this technically means they’ve made significant progress. Yikes.

title: New York Yankees 9- 2 Diamondbacks: Resultados y crónica - UNANIMO Deportes
author: Unanimo Deportes
body:
Los New York Yankees respondieron con autoridad en su primer partido sin Aaron Judge y derrotaron 9-2 a los Arizona Diamondbacks este viernes en Chase Field. Nueva York fabricó cinco carreras en la primera entrada, Ben Rice y George Lombard Jr. conectaron cuadrangulares y Gerrit Cole lanzó seis entradas de calidad para llevarse una victoria que también tuvo un significado histórico para el derecho.
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Aaron Judge vuelve a la lista de lesionados de los Yankees!
LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
La jornada comenzó con una noticia importante para los Yankees: Judge fue colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha. Sin su principal figura ofensiva, Nueva York necesitó encontrar producción desde el primer turno y la respuesta llegó inmediatamente frente al abridor de Arizona, Eduardo Rodríguez.
Los primeros cinco bateadores de los Yankees lograron embasarse. Ben Rice recibió una base por bolas y posteriormente Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor para abrir la pizarra. Después llegaron más oportunidades para la ofensiva neoyorquina, hasta que George Lombard Jr. conectó un sencillo de dos carreras que llevó el marcador a 5-0 antes de que terminara el primer episodio. Rodríguez necesitó 45 lanzamientos para conseguir los tres outs de la entrada, la mayor cantidad de su carrera en un primer inning.
Arizona intentó reaccionar en el segundo capítulo. Corbin Carroll conectó un cuadrangular de dos carreras para acercar a los Diamondbacks a 5-2 y darle algo de vida al público de Chase Field. Sin embargo, Cole logró contener la ofensiva local y evitó que la reacción se transformara en una amenaza mayor.
La respuesta de los Yankees llegó en la tercera entrada. Ben Rice volvió a aparecer y conectó un cuadrangular solitario, su número 39 de la temporada, para recuperar la diferencia de cuatro carreras y colocar el encuentro 6-2. El batazo también completó una noche ofensiva sobresaliente para Rice, quien terminó con dos imparables, dos bases por bolas, dos carreras y dos carreras impulsadas.
Mientras la ofensiva seguía produciendo, Cole encontró estabilidad desde la lomita. Después del cuadrangular de Carroll, el derecho no permitió otra carrera y completó seis entradas con cuatro hits, dos carreras limpias, ninguna base por bolas y seis ponches. Venía de dos aperturas en las que había permitido siete jonrones combinados, por lo que su actuación en Phoenix representó una recuperación importante en su temporada.
Lombard Jr. volvió a aparecer en la sexta entrada. El campocorto conectó su tercer jonrón de la temporada, esta vez solitario, para ampliar la ventaja de Nueva York a 7-2. El joven infielder terminó la noche con dos imparables y tres carreras impulsadas, convirtiéndose en otra de las figuras ofensivas del triunfo visitante.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
Los Yankees agregaron dos carreras más en la séptima entrada para terminar de sentenciar el encuentro. La ofensiva visitante terminó con ocho hits y nueve carreras, mientras que Arizona consiguió siete imparables, pero no volvió a pisar el plato después del segundo inning.
Para Cole, la victoria tuvo un valor especial. El derecho llegó a 162 triunfos en su carrera, superando a Mike Moore y convirtiéndose en el lanzador con más victorias entre los jugadores que fueron seleccionados con el primer pick global del Draft. Cole fue elegido por los Pittsburgh Pirates con la primera selección en 2011.
La derrota, en cambio, complicó todavía más el panorama de Arizona en la recta final de la temporada. Los Diamondbacks llegaron al encuentro buscando mantenerse en la pelea por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, pero la caída ante Nueva York significó su tercera derrota consecutiva. Al término de la jornada quedaron cinco juegos por detrás del último puesto de Wild Card, con ocho encuentros restantes.
Los Yankees, ya clasificados a los playoffs, mejoraron a 89-64 y se colocaron a cuatro juegos de los Tampa Bay Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con nueve partidos por disputar. Nueva York además consiguió su octava victoria en sus últimos 10 encuentros.
El triunfo llegó, además, en una noche en la que los Yankees tuvieron que afrontar la ausencia de Judge. Rice y Lombard Jr. aportaron los batazos largos, mientras que Cole respondió desde el montículo para que Nueva York tomara el primer partido de la serie en Arizona con una victoria contundente de 9-2.

Carroll back, on the track, at the wall.
See ya.

title: Aaron Judge confía en que podrá volver en los playoffs
author: FOX Deportes
body:
Redacción FOX Deportes
Aaron Judge confía en que podrá volver en los playoffs
El jardinero y cañonero de los Yankees fue colocado en la lista de lesionados
Después de ser enviado a la lista de lesionados por diez días debido a una distensión en el músculo sóleo derecho, Aaron Judge expresó su deseo de regresar para los playoffs.
“Me gustaría estar de vuelta para la postemporada; ese es definitivamente el plan”, declaró el capitán de los Yankees. El jardinero confirmó que mantendrá sus rutinas de tiro y entrenamiento físico “para volver de inmediato en cuanto estemos listos” y afrontar el cierre del campeonato.
Respecto a la gravedad de la lesión, el estelar bateador admitió que la localización de la molestia ha dificultado su movilidad en el terreno. “He lidiado con distensiones antes y he jugado así, pero esto fue en un lugar diferente que lo hizo un poco más difícil”, explicó Judge, añadiendo que el sóleo “es más crucial para correr y batear”. Sobre su tiempo de baja, reconoció que no tiene certeza: “El cuerpo médico no me ha dicho el grado aún y no tengo respuestas sobre plazos”.
Los Yankees colocaron a Aaron Judge en la lista de lesionados
El equipo neoyorquino se quedará sin su máxima estrella en la parte final de la temporada
Por su parte, el mánager Aaron Boone adoptó una postura pragmática y evitó ofrecer un diagnóstico médico o una fecha estimada para el retorno de su figura. “No importa qué grado sea, nos quedan nueve partidos”, afirmó el estratega ante los medios de comunicación. “Vamos a trabajar para tenerlo de regreso o no; eso es lo que vamos a hacer y ya veremos qué sucede”, enfatizó sobre las posibilidades de volver a contar con el jugador en el roster.
La fecha más cercana para la reactivación de Judge es el 29 de septiembre frente a los Orioles, día en que también inicia la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana. El vigente Jugador Más Valioso busca reincorporarse a tiempo para los playoffs tras una campaña afectada por los problemas físicos, en la que registra un promedio de .241 con 18 cuadrangulares y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos disputados esta temporada.
LO MÁS VISTO

title: Yankees at Diamondbacks. Cam Schlittler dominating in early innings
author: Nick Piecoro; José M Romero
body:
Yankees at Diamondbacks. Cam Schlittler dominating in early innings
The Yankees broke through with the first run of the game in the top of the fifth inning, while the Diamondbacks are still looking for their first hit off Yankees right-hander Cam Schlittler.
The Diamondbacks trail the Yankees, 1-0, after 4½ innings as play continued at Chase Field on Saturday, Sept. 19.
The Yankees loaded the bases on three singles in the fifth off right-hander Brandon Pfaadt, prompting manager Torey Lovullo to make an aggressive move to his bullpen. Right-hander Justin Martinez entered and recorded two fly-ball outs, the first of which, by Ben Rice, was deep enough to score the first run of the night.
The Diamondbacks are trying to keep their slim playoff hopes alive with a win. Meanwhile, the San Diego Padres, whom the Diamondbacks are hoping to catch, were losing to the Marlins at Petco Park.
The game started about a half-hour late after a lengthy pregame ceremony honoring the Diamondbacks’ 2001 World Series team.
With former radio voice Greg Schulte hosting the ceremony, the Diamondbacks introduced players, coaches and staff from the ‘01 team. Randy Johnson was the last one announced. While everyone else entered the field from beyond the right-field fence, Johnson came out of the home bullpen in left field, a call back to his relief appearance in Game 7 of the World Series.
One of the memorable moments of the pregame ceremony was when trumpeter Dr. Jesse McGuire, performing the national anthem as he did at the World Series in 2001, hit a sour note on his instrument. Then the trumpet gave out completely, and McGuire acted quickly by grabbing the microphone and singing the rest of the Star-Spangled Banner.
Afterward, he received a hug from Diamondbacks manager Torey Lovullo as the crowd cheered.
—Nick Piercoro and Jose M. Romero
With his team teetering on the brink of elimination, Lovullo’s job status is again a topic of discussion. Lovullo understands. For him, it’s nothing new.
“It seems to be a very important part of the conversation for a lot of people,” Lovullo said on Saturday, Sept. 19, a day after his team lost for the third consecutive day to drop five games out of a playoff spot with eight games remaining.
“For me, it’s real, I understand it, but it’s the realities of this game. You’ve got to win. That’s what it comes down to. Have we won enough? You know, I want to win every game that we play.”
Lovullo, in his 10th season as Diamondbacks manager, has worked as a “lame-duck” manager in four of the past six seasons. He seemed to reference that history, as well as the fact that he had to “fight for everything” during his playing career.
But he said that, for now, at least, he remains focused on doing what he can to help his players and coaches finish out the season.
“When it’s time to worry about it or think about it, whether that’s sooner than later, I will,” he said. “I’ve got to do my job. If I'm worried about different things that I can’t control, then I'm not doing my job for that group in there. I’m doing fine. I’m doing fine. Because I've lived in this space for a long time. I understand the playbook. I understand the realities of this game.”
Last year, Lovullo went into the final weekend of the year with similar questions surrounding him. He found out a day after the season ended that he would be coming back for another year.
The situation is believed to be similar to then: Lovullo has strong support from the baseball operations department and general manager Mike Hazen, but how he is viewed by ownership is less certain.
Lovullo has two postseason appearances — 2017 and 2023 — during his managerial tenure, but he also has presided over multiple late-season collapses. If this year's team continues to stumble, it would mark a third consecutive year the Diamondbacks fell short in September.
Hazen is working under the five-year extension he signed in September 2023. His deal runs through 2028.
The Diamondbacks entered Saturday, Sept. 19, facing long odds at a postseason berth. FanGraphs put their chances at claiming a wild-card spot at about 5%.
—Nick Piecoro
Justin Martinez leaves impression on manager
Members of the 2001 Diamondbacks World Series team milled about in front of the home dugout at Chase Field on Friday, Sept. 18, catching up, taking photos and conducting interviews.
Justin Martinez walked among them, asking each one he approached to sign a baseball. The Diamondbacks reliever later put the ball in a case he had with him in the team clubhouse.
Lovullo said Martinez seeking autographs of veterans is a throwback to a previous generation of players.
“I love it,” Lovullo said. “There was probably seven fistfights between those teammates, firstfights don’t happen anymore. It’s just a different level of camaraderie. But players care about the same thing, and that’s to win the world championship.
“So ‘J-Mart’ was probably just getting a feel for the common denominator based on what drove that team, and that’s a brotherhood that you can’t replace.”
Lovullo added that he's happy that the current team has players that are fans of baseball on that level.
“That he gets to touch their emotions makes it even better. That’s vintage J-Mart," Lovullo said.
— José M. Romero
Yankees at Diamondbacks, 5:10 p.m., Cox, Ch. 34
Diamondbacks RHP Brandon Pfaadt (7-3, 3.77) vs. Yankees RHP Cam Schlittler (14-6, 1.95).
At Chase Field: Pfaadt gave up six runs in 6⅔ innings against the Rangers in his most recent start. All six runs came in the fifth inning, in which Pfaadt was ruled to have missed the bag while covering first, opening the door for the final four runs of the inning to score. … Pfaadt has had a strong past few months overall, but his past five starts have been rough. He has posted a 5.74 ERA in 31⅓ innings in that stretch. … He has faced the Yankees only once in his career, giving up six runs (five earned) in 4⅓ innings in a game in 2023. … Schlittler looks like the favorite to win the American League Cy Young Award. He has the lowest ERA and WHIP and has logged 184⅔. … He has never faced the Diamondbacks. … Schlittler averages 98 mph with his four-seam fastball. He primarily throws that, his sinker and cutter, only occasionally sprinkling in curveballs and a rare slider.
Coming up
Sunday, Sept. 20: At Chase Field, 1:10 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Corbin Burnes (0-0, 5.87) vs. Yankees RHP Will Warren (10-6, 3.89).
Monday, Sept. 21: Off.
Tuesday, Sept. 22: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Michael Soroka (8-5, 3.45) vs. Rockies LHP Kyle Freeland (4-10, 6.38).
Wednesday, Sept. 23: At Colorado, 5:40 p.m., Diamondbacks RHP Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00) vs. Rockies RHP Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09).
