title: Aaron Judge Injured, Latest Updates on Yankees Star's Timeline to Return Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
author: Andrew Peters
body:
Aaron Judge Injured, Latest Updates on Yankees Star's Timeline to Return Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
Just over a week after he returned from a rib injury that kept him out for most of the season, Aaron Judge is heading back to the injured list.
Judge is being placed on the 10-day IL with a calf strain, the New York Yankees announced Friday.
TOP NEWS
Mets 1B Has Memory Loss After Collision
Mets player calls out own fans
Ichiro Throws CRAZY Shutout 🔱
Judge left Wednesday's game against the Minnesota Twins in the sixth inning because of right lower leg tightness. He said after the game that he felt something during the first inning and eventually decided he should come out.
Judge went 0-for-2 with a pair of strikeouts before he exited the game. Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for him.
Judge suffered a rib injury in late May and missed more than three months of action, finally making his return last Tuesday against the Colorado Rockies. Since returning, he's gone 4-for-21 with a home run and three RBI, clearly still working his way back to 100 percent.
After his return, the three-time AL MVP addressed having to get back into shape while simultaneously helping the Yankees fight for ideal playoff seeding.
"I get paid to do this, so I gotta go do it," Judge told reporters. "That's the end of it. I get paid to go out there and give my best to the New York Yankees and these fans. So, you get paid to win games so you gotta keep going out there and winning games."
Luckily for Judge, New York managed to stay afloat during his absence. The Yankees are sitting in second place in the AL East and secured a spot in the postseason earlier this week.
The Bronx Bombers are six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox and should be able to secure the top wild-card spot.
Even though New York has guaranteed a spot in the playoffs, Judge's injury is worrisome. The Yankees may have managed when he was gone, but making a World Series push without their star would be a different story.
With Judge heading back to the injured list, the Yankees will hope their star slugger can return to the lineup sooner rather than later as New York battles for playoff position in the AL East.

title: Aaron Judge to hit IL due to calf strain, can't return until Yankees' final game of regular season
author: Jack Baer
body:
New York Yankees star Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list due to a right calf strain, the club announced Friday.
Assuming the roster move is backdated to Thursday, the day after Judge's last on-field appearance, the three-time AL MVP won't be eligible to return until Sept. 27, the day of the Yankees' final game of the regular season. Of course, it's unclear if he will be ready to play by then.
Per Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News, the Yankees plan to call up outfielder Max Schuemann from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre as the corresponding move for Judge.
Judge came off the IL only 10 days earlier after missing three months due to a stress fracture in his ribs. He has played in seven games since then, going 4-for-23 with 1 homer and 13 strikeouts.
This injury popped up on Wednesday, when Judge left a game due to what he described as stiffness in his lower right leg. Per MLB.com, Judge didn't point to any one play causing the issue. Rather, he described it as the kind of issue that arises after a long layoff like his IL stint:
"I feel like you deal with this every spring training. You know, usually at the start of the season once you start ramping up again, things pop up, and that's where we've been," Judge said. "Thankfully, this whole time coming back, nothing's really nagged us. So hopefully it's just one little thing and then we're back out there soon."
Unfortunately, the injury appears to not be one little thing.
Judge has won AL MVP in three of the past four seasons, but this year has not gone according to plan. He got off to a slow start by his standards, slashing only .248/.375/.533 until the Yankees placed him on the IL in early June. Those struggles were partially due to the rib injury, which he reportedly tried to play through for six weeks.
Judge didn't return to the lineup until Sept. 8, and now he's going back on the shelf. Going forward, he represents an enormous unknown for the Yankees, who sit second in the AL East at 88-64. They are currently on pace for a second straight wild-card series clash with the Boston Red Sox.
At best, Judge could return right before the playoffs. At worst, he might have already played his final game of 2026.
Not counting his cup of coffee in 2016 or the COVID-shortened 2020 season, Judge has never played in fewer than the 66 games he's seen in 2026 or posted an OPS+ lower than this year's 140 (which is still very good). That adds up to a career-worst season for Judge at 34 years old.

title: What Aaron Boone and Jack Curry Said About Oswaldo Cabrera Should Have Reds Fans Intrigued
author: Greg Kuffner; Unknown
body:
The Cincinnati Reds claimed infielder and outfielder Oswaldo Cabrera off waivers from the New York Yankees on Friday, adding a versatile player who clearly made an impression on the people around him, as well as the fans.
The reaction from those who knew Cabrera in New York said plenty about the person Cincinnati is getting.
Jack Curry of the YES Network shared a strong endorsement of Cabrera after the move was announced.
“Oswaldo Cabrera, who is as kind and as gracious as any baseball player I’ve covered, is headed to the Reds. Best of luck to a versatile player and a gem of a human being.”
That is high praise from someone who has spent decades covering baseball. Curry’s comments were similar to the comments made by Yankees manager Aaron Boone.
“I’m blessed to have a lot of guys on this team that you just admire and respect and love doing the job with on a daily basis," Boone told the New York Daily News. "Oswaldo’s right there at the top of that list... The good thing is, Oswaldo’s come back from a very difficult injury and had a really good year down at Triple-A. He’s playing really well, so hopefully this is just one of those things. I’m confident that Oswaldo will go on to have a very good career, and hopefully it’s still with us.”
Boone’s hope of keeping Cabrera in the organization ultimately did not happen. Instead, the Reds will give him his next opportunity.
Cabrera Has Played Well in the Minors This Season
Cabrera has hit .232/.292/.343 across 304 career major league games. After missing most of 2025 with an injury, he appeared in just three major league games this season.
His production at Triple-A this season gives Reds fans something to be optimistic about. Cabrera hit .288/.345/.444 with 19 home runs in 122 games, putting together the kind of season Boone referenced while discussing his recovery.
Cabrera has played six different positions at Triple-A this season, appearing in 55 games at third base, 39 at shortstop, 12 at second base, 10 in left field, eight in right field and six at first base.
His ability to play both the infield and outfield gives the Reds options. He will still have to turn that Triple-A production into results at the major league level, but he arrives with strong support from people who watched him work every day.
Greg Kuffner a contributor to Reds On SI. He graduated from the University of Cincinnati and worked for the Sports Information Department during his time as a student. He follows all things Reds year round, including the minor league system.

title: Yankees' Aaron Judge Dilemma Features a Problem No One is Discussing
author: Matthew Schmidt
body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge returned from a rib stress fracture on Sept. 8, and it took him all of seven games to get injured again.
Judge left Wednesday's loss to the Minnesota Twins as a result of what he and the team are calling a "lower leg injury," which almost surely means a calf issue.
There have been no definitive updates on his status since, and it's looking more and more like Judge will not play against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night.
The playoffs start on Sept. 29, which obviously creates a nightmare scenario for the Yankees. Even if Judge is healthy enough to play.
Why? Because at this point, the three-time AL MVP pretty much has to serve as a designated hitter. Unless Judge has a minor bruise in his calf, it seems highly unlikely that he will be able to play right field if he returns.
Why is that a big deal? Because it completely messes up New York's lineup.
The Yankees acquired Luis Garcia Jr. back at the MLB trade deadline with the expectation that he would be the first baseman. Ben Rice would then serve as DH, as Giancarlo Stanton's status was up in the air then, and now, it looks like Stanton is done for the year.
When Judge is in right field, that isn't an issue. Garcia plays first, Rice goes to DH and all three of those big boppers are in the lineup.
But with Judge potentially having to spend all of his time at designated hitter, that means Garcia would almost certainly get the boot.
You're not platooning Rice and Garcia at first. They're both lefties, and you always want Rice's bat in the lineup no matter what. What the Yankees could have done was platoon Garcia and Paul Goldschmidt at first base given how much Goldschmidt mashes lefties, but if Judge is DHing, that isn't possible.
If Judge is healthy enough to hit, he'll obviously be in the lineup. Running the bases could be another story (just ask Giancarlo), but the more you limit Judge's movement, the better.
That the Yankees have been so mum on Judge's status is concerning. If there weren't a major problem here, they surely would have already said something.
And after all of the experience fans have had with the medical stuff and how New York handles injuries, they know by now that when there is silence, there is reason to worry.
Hopefully, Judge's malady is no big deal and he can head back out to right field within the next week. But Yankees fans need to prepare for other scenarios, and even if Judge does return, that could mean their lineup still wouldn't be all it could be,

title: Carlos Rodón has earned a Yankees playoff start over Gerrit Cole
author: Jake Elman
body:
History and common sense (we know, two things that don’t always share space in a conversation) typically dictate that a $162 million pitcher doesn’t make a playoff roster for one of two reasons: injuries or disaster.
Luckily for the New York Yankees, that’s not the problem with veteran lefty Carlos Rodón. The three-time All-Star is healthy after multiple elbow problems, and he’s recorded a 2.95 ERA and 1.6 bWAR over 11 starts. Depending on how confident you feel about Gerrit Cole, we’d argue that Rodón is the Yankees’ third-best starter behind AL Cy Young favorite Cam Schlittler and the always-reliable Max Fried.
Yet all signs point to Cole, and not Rodón, starting a potential Game 3 in the Wild Card Series. In fact, some who cover the Yankees have even listed the latter as someone who could be on the roster bubble, at least for the first round.
The New York Yankees must turn to Carlos Rodón rather than Gerrit Cole in the playoffs
We addressed the Cole vs. Rodón debate earlier this week, so we don’t want to make things too repetitive. The bottom line is that Cole has allowed far more home runs at Yankee Stadium than on the road, and the Yankees would host all three games (if needed) in the Wild Card Series. Theoretically, that’d set Rodón up to possibly pitch Game 1 of the ALDS, which would either be against the No. 1 Rays or whoever earns the No. 2 seed; as of Friday afternoon, that honor would go to the AL Central-leading White Sox.
Let’s take a quick look at how Cole and Rodón fare in several key departments:
| Stat | Carlos Rodón | Gerrit Cole | 
|---|---|---|
| Batters faced | 315 | 475 | 
| Batting average against | .178 | .241 | 
| Walk rate | 12.1 percent | 4.2 percent | 
| Strikeout rate | 26.3 percent | 24.6 percent | 
| Home runs allowed | Seven | 20 | 
| Doubles | 12 | 21 | 
| Triples | Zero | Two | 
| Hit batsmen | 2 | 2 | 
The knock against Rodón, though, is his career-worst 12.1 percent walk rate, which is significantly above his lifetime 9.0 average. He hasn't exceeded a 9.0 percent walk rate over a full season since a 10.8 mark in 2018. Assuming that the Yankees don’t overtake the Rays in the AL East, they’d host the Red Sox in the first round.
But here's the good news: The Red Sox have drawn 491 walks, well below the league average of 516. So you’d think that Rodón has the leg up on Cole, right? Interestingly, the Red Sox have only hit 158 home runs, which is tied for seventh-worst in baseball. Much of their offense comes from doubles — their 272 two-baggers are one off the Royals for the MLB lead — and the occasional bruise; the Red Sox’s 93 hit-by-pitches are tied with the Angels for the league lead.
Call us boring, but we’d much rather have the guy who works around walks instead of the 36-year-old with a penchant for giving up home runs. Naturally, that means we should prepare for Cole to throw seven shutout innings during his first playoff start, but what do we know?

author: SNY Newsdesk
body:
With Clarke Schmidt being activated off the 60-day IL as he returns from Tommy John surgery, the Yankees are creating room on the 40-man roster by designating utility player Oswaldo Cabrera for assignment.
Cabrera was then claimed by the Cincinnati Reds, ending his time with the Yankee organization after five seasons in The Bronx.
Cabrera played just three games for the Yanks this season as he spent the majority of the year with Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes Barre, where he was hitting .288/.345/.444 in 122 games while getting starts at all four infield positions and both corner outfield spots.
The 27-year-old appeared in 304 games at the big league level, posting a .232/.292/.343 slash line for a .635 OPS. In 15 postseason games, Cabrera tallied three hits in 34 at-bats with a .420 OPS.
As for Schmidt, he has been out since July 3 of last season, when he was diagnosed with a torn UCL that required Tommy John surgery that also included an internal brace procedure.
Schmidt had a 3.32 ERA (3.95 FIP) and 1.09 WHIP in 14 starts last season before going down with his injury.
In another notable move on Wednesday, hard-throwing pitching prospect Carlos Lagrange was activated off the IL in Triple-A.
Lagrange, who had been dealing with a right shoulder sprain, last pitched on June 28.

title: Former Detroit Tigers All-Star Quietly Thriving With Current Team
author: Ben Stinar
body:
On Friday night, the Detroit Tigers will visit the Chicago White Sox at Rate Field for the first of a three-game series.
The Tigers are coming off a series where they won two out of three games over the Toronto Blue Jays in Canada.
Former Detroit Tigers All-Star Quietly Thriving
With less than two weeks left in the 2026 season, it’s worth noting that a former Tigers star is off to a strong start with his new team.
Michael Fulmer signed with the New York Yankees earlier this year.
MLB.com wrote (on August 26): “New York Yankees signed free agent RHP Michael Fulmer.”
So far, he has gone 0-0 with a 2.57 ERA in his first eight games with the Yankees.
Considering they got Fulmer for nothing, he has been a very promising addition to the team’s bullpen.
Looking At Fulmer
Fulmer was picked in the 1st round of the 2011 MLB Draft by the Tigers.
He won the 2016 American League Rookie of The Year Award (and was then a 2017 MLB All-Star).
Following six years pitching for the Tigers, Fulmer went on to also have stints with the Minnesota Twins, Chicago Cubs, Boston Red Sox and Los Angeles Angels (before the Yankees).
Over 276 career games, Fulmer (who is 33) has gone 37-50 with a 3.91 ERA.
Looking At The Tigers Right Now
The Tigers are the third-place team in the American League Central with a 72-81 record in 153 games.
They have won seven out of their last ten games.

title: ¿Cómo responderán los jóvenes de Yankees en los playoffs?
author: Patrick Donnelly
body:
Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre.
Jugador, Número de Partidos de Playoffs de por vida
Cody Bellinger, 76
Aaron Judge, 65
Paul Goldschmidt, 29
Trent Grisham, 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells, 21
Anthony Volpe, 21
Amed Rosario, 11
Ryan McMahon, 10
Ben Rice, 6
José Caballero, 3
Pero faltan algunos nombres en esa lista: El campocorto George Lombard Jr., el jardinero Spencer Jones, el primera base dominicano Luis García Jr. y el jardinero puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos. Ninguno de esos cuatro nunca ha jugado en la postemporada, ya sea con los Yankees o, como es el caso de García y Ramos, con sus equipos anteriores.
Ahora, es posible que algunos de los jugadores veteranos lesionados -- Grisham y Chisholm, específicamente -- puedan regresar a la alineación y enviar a algunos de esos nuevos rostros a la banca o fuera del roster de postemporada por completo. Pero es seguro decir que los Yankees van a contar con al menos algunos novatos en los playoffs el próximo mes, en su búsqueda de ganar su primera Serie Mundial desde el 2009.
Boone ha expresado que sus jóvenes y los recién llegados a los playoffs tienen otra ventaja sobre los jugadores en otros mercados.
"Jugar para los Yankees, jugar en Nueva York”, dijo, "tiene una manera de prepararte para la postemporada”.
Éste ha sido un año de transición en las Grandes Ligas. Consulta la primera ronda del Draft del 2023 si quieres pruebas. No menos de 19 de las 37 selecciones de primera ronda y de compensación han debutado en las Mayores, y muchos de ellos ya son jugadores clave en sus equipos.
"Los jugadores están llegando a las Grandes Ligas a un ritmo muy rápido ahora y a temprana edad”, manifestó el piloto de los Tigers, A.J. Hinch, quien ha dado la bienvenida a la tercera selección Max Clark y al favorito para Novato del Año de la Liga Americana, Kevin McGonigle, a Detroit este año. "No creo que se sientan tan impresionados por los grandes pasos que están dando”.
Para los Yankees, ese grupo incluye a Lombard, quien se ha aclimatado bien desde que fue subido a principios de agosto. Y Jones fue elogiado recientemente nada menos que por Aaron Judge, quien dijo que el jardinero novato "realmente ha evolucionado cada vez que ha sido subido, mejorando un poco más en cada ocasión”.
Por supuesto, habrá contratiempos en el camino. El miércoles, Jones se fue de 6-0 con cinco ponches y cometió un error cuando dejó caer un batazo en el jardín central. Y Lombard no pudo atrapar un roletazo del boricua Victor Caratini en la 13ª entrada que fue considerado un sencillo mientras los Mellizos vencían a los Yankees.
Pero cualquiera que siga el béisbol sabe que los días malos y las malas jugadas son parte del ciclo de crecimiento de un jugador de Grandes Ligas. La clave es aprender de ellos para poder limitarlos en el futuro. Y todo ello -- lo bueno, lo malo y lo ocasionalmente feo -- ayuda a preparar a un joven jugador para su primera vez jugando en el béisbol de octubre.
El mundo está a punto de descubrir lo preparados que están los Yankees jóvenes. Pero Jones ofreció un poco de tranquilidad el lunes mientras disfrutaba de la celebración en el vestuario después de la victoria en Target Field que aseguró otra clasificación de Nueva York para los playoffs.
"Creo que para nosotros, jugamos mejor cuando la multitud se vuelve más ruidosa", dijo. "Estoy bien emocionado por lo que está por venir”.

title: Yankees Announce Starting Pitchers for Diamondbacks Series: Gerrit Cole Must Get Back on Track
author: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
body:
If there's one reason to think the New York Yankees have a minuscule chance of overcoming a five-game deficit in the American League East, it's the probable pitchers every series. Aaron Boone's Bombers can feature one of his many frontline starters on a given night, and in this series against the Arizona Diamondbacks, two of his four best pitchers take the mound.
On paper, you see the first two starters and think the advantage should go to the Yankees, but one issue in particular has hampered their former Cy Young winner. If this team is going to make any noise in the postseason, he'll have to work on it, and it starts with this series.
Friday, Sept. 18 (9:40 p.m. ET): Gerrit Cole (NYY) vs. Eduardo Rodriguez (ARI)
Eduardo Rodriguez has proven to be a playoff-caliber pitcher, and his 2.62 ERA in 178.1 IP is frontline stuff. He is the type of high-level arm they'll see in the postseason. Rodriguez typically pitches to contact, holding opposing batters to an 87.3 MPH average exit velocity and a 33% hard-hit rate. This can be one of those games where the Yankees hit ground balls against him for 7+ innings.
Cole, meanwhile, has been snakebit by the long ball, and it isn't so wild to say that the advantage could go to Rodriguez in this one if Cole pitches the way he has. It's been a concerning turn of events ever since that game against the San Diego Padres. For now, the advantage goes to Rodriguez, who'll want to harken back to his Boston days and shut down the Yankees.
Saturday, Sept. 19 (8:10 p.m. ET): Cam Schlittler (NYY) vs. Brandon Pfadt (ARI)
Pfaadt, though, isn't a slouch by any means, and if the Yankees are going to be without Aaron Judge — which usually means the offense will be listless — what can be said about Rodriguez applies to Pfaadt here.
The 27-year-old Arizona starter has a 68th-percentile groundball rate and holds hitters to a 35.5% hard-hit rate. It could be another instance of the Yankees hitting a ton of ground balls. Most competent offenses should be able to hold their own, but it's hard to trust the Yankees 1-through-9 these days. They might need a great pitching performance by Schlittler and win one of those 2-0 or 3-0 games here.
Pfaadt has one of the best walk rates in baseball. His 5.7% BB% is in the 91st percentile, so he'll force them to make contact, and that can be a recipe for disaster for a team that can't put together runs.
Sunday, Sept. 20 (4:10 p.m. ET): Will Warren (NYY) vs. Corbin Burnes (ARI)
Corbin Burnes has pitched all of 7.2 innings this season. He's coming back from Tommy John surgery, which he had last June. It feels like a quick recovery, and he'll likely be on a pitch limit. That said, the sooner the Yankees can get him back in the game, the better.
Every Warren start can't be a high-scoring affair because he can be brilliant or a disaster, so hopefully they get a brilliant Warren here while also chasing Burnes out of the game quickly. If he's out by the third, they can ground down that bullpen.
Warren is coming off a solid outing against the Twins earlier this week, where he allowed five hits, two runs (zero earned), two walks, and racked up six strikeouts in 5.2 innings.
The advantage should go to the Yankees if Warren gives them length, but again, as with any game, it will come down to whether they can score.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

For now, the advantage goes to Rodriguez, who'll want to harken back to his Boston days and shut down the Yankees.
Saturday, Sept. 19 (8:10 p.m. ET): Cam Schlittler (NYY) vs. Brandon Pfadt (ARI)
Pfaadt, though, isn't a slouch by any means, and if the Yankees are going to be without Aaron Judge — which usually means the offense will be listless — what can be said about Rodriguez applies to Pfaadt here.
The 27-year-old Arizona starter has a 68th-percentile groundball rate and holds hitters to a 35.5% hard-hit rate. It could be another instance of the Yankees hitting a ton of ground balls. Most competent offenses should be able to hold their own, but it's hard to trust the Yankees 1-through-9 these days. They might need a great pitching performance by Schlittler and win one of those 2-0 or 3-0 games here.
Pfaadt has one of the best walk rates in baseball. His 5.7% BB% is in the 91st percentile, so he'll force them to make contact, and that can be a recipe for disaster for a team that can't put together runs.
Sunday, Sept. 20 (4:10 p.m. ET): Will Warren (NYY) vs. Corbin Burnes (ARI)
Corbin Burnes has pitched all of 7.2 innings this season. He's coming back from Tommy John surgery, which he had last June. It feels like a quick recovery, and he'll likely be on a pitch limit. That said, the sooner the Yankees can get him back in the game, the better.
Every Warren start can't be a high-scoring affair because he can be brilliant or a disaster, so hopefully they get a brilliant Warren here while also chasing Burnes out of the game quickly. If he's out by the third, they can ground down that bullpen.
Warren is coming off a solid outing against the Twins earlier this week, where he allowed five hits, two runs (zero earned), two walks, and racked up six strikeouts in 5.2 innings.
The advantage should go to the Yankees if Warren gives them length, but again, as with any game, it will come down to whether they can score.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

title: Pete Rose llegó a 100 hits por vigésimo segundo año consecutivo; Alex Rodríguez completa el 40-40
source: El Nacional — La voz de todos
author: Agencia AP
body:
En esta fecha
Pete Rose llegó a 100 hits por vigésimo segundo año consecutivo; Alex Rodríguez completa el 40-40
Albert Pujols estableció récord de carreras impulsadas para un novato de la Liga Nacional; Mariano Rivera impuso una marca de las Grandes Ligas con su salvamento número 602
1968 — Denny McLain ganó su partido número 31, la mayor cantidad en la Liga Americana desde los 31 de Lefty Grove en 1931. Los Detroit Tigers vencieron a los New York Yankees 6-2, mientras que Mickey Mantle conectó su jonrón número 535 y penúltimo de su carrera.
1972 — César Tovar, de Minnesota, completó el ciclo con un jonrón de dos carreras que le dio la victoria a los Twins en la parte baja de la novena entrada, otorgándoles un triunfo de 5-3 sobre los Texas Rangers.
1973 — Frank Robinson conectó su primer jonrón en el Estadio Arlington, como miembro de los California Angels. Fue el trigésimo segundo estadio de las Grandes Ligas en el que conectó un jonrón.
1984 — Pete Rose alcanzó la marca de 100 hits por vigésimo segundo año consecutivo, un récord histórico. También igualó el récord de la Liga Nacional de dobles con 725, cuando los Rojos de Cincinnati vencieron a los Bravos de Atlanta por 4-2.
1986 — Joe Crowley, de los Chicago White Sox, lanzó un juego sin hits ni carreras para guiar a su equipo a una victoria de 7-1 sobre los California Angels.
1995 — Ken Caminiti, de San Diego, se convirtió en el primer jugador en la historia de las Grandes Ligas en conectar jonrones desde ambos lados del plato tres veces en una temporada, al lograr 4 de 4 con un récord personal de ocho carreras impulsadas en una victoria de 15-4 sobre Colorado.
1998 — Alex Rodríguez, de Seattle, conectó su cuadragésimo jonrón para convertirse en el tercer jugador en la historia del béisbol en conectar 40 jonrones y robar 40 bases en la misma temporada.
2001 — Roger Clemens se convirtió en el primer lanzador en la historia de las Grandes Ligas en lograr un récord de 20-1, llevando a los Yankees de Nueva York a una victoria de 6-3 sobre los Medias Blancas de Chicago.
2001 — Albert Pujols estableció un récord de carreras impulsadas para un novato de la Liga Nacional cuando St. Louis venció a Milwaukee 8-2. Pujols impulsó tres carreras para alcanzar las 120 carreras impulsadas, rompiendo la marca de 119 establecida por Wally Berger en 1930 para los Boston Braves.
2008 — El sistema de repetición instantánea del béisbol produjo su primera anulación cuando un doble de dos carreras de Carlos Peña, de Tampa Bay, se convirtió en un jonrón de tres carreras durante la cuarta entrada contra Minnesota.
2008 — Greg Maddox lanza su entrada número 5.000 contra los Gigantes de San Francisco.
2011 — Mariano Rivera estableció un récord de las Grandes Ligas con su salvamento número 602, sellando la victoria de los Yankees de Nueva York por 6-4 sobre los Mellizos de Minnesota.
2017 — Se establece un nuevo récord de la MLB de la mayor cantidad de jonrones en una temporada, 5,694, cuando Alex Gordon de los Kansas City Royals conecta un jonrón.
2024 — Shohei Ohtani irrumpe en un club completamente nuevo del que es el único miembro: el club 50-50. Hoy, logra su primer partido de seis hits, tres de ellos jonrones, sumando 51 en la temporada. También roba dos bases, alcanzando (e incluso superando) la marca de 50, mientras impulsa diez carreras en la aplastante victoria de los Dodgers sobre los Marlins por 20-4. Hace menos de un mes, se convirtió en el sexto miembro del club 40-40, pero ahora se encuentra solo en este nuevo nivel de excelencia sobrenatural, y de paso, ha establecido un nuevo récord de jonrones en una sola temporada para los Dodgers (superando la marca de Shawn Green).

title: New York Yankees $70M Infielder Handed Harsh Take Ahead of Playoffs
author: Cole Shelton
body:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising decision on veteran infielder Ryan McMahon before the playoffs.
New York clinched a playoff berth. They will likely be in the Wild Card series again, likely playing the Boston Red Sox for the second year in a row.
The Yankees are 88-64.
New York Yankees Could Bench Ryan McMahon
With the Yankees heading back to the playoffs, New York could have to make a difficult decision on veteran infielder Ryan McMahon.
McMahon is a solid glove-first third baseman, but he has struggled offensively since coming to New York. With that, Yankees analyst Pat Ragazzo of FanSided believes New York could remove McMahon from its playoff roster, or simply have him on the bench.
"Should Rosario's hot streak continue into the end of the regular season, the Yankees find a way to utilize him at third base during the postseason," Ragazzo wrote. "There's even a world where Jose Caballero slides to third, with Anthony Volpe available off the bench. McMahon will probably still get a roster spot, but they cannot play his bat regularly in the biggest games of the year. McMahon's bat creates a black hole in the Yankees' lineup, which they cannot afford to deploy in October.
"If not for his defense, McMahon would've likely been designated for assignment by now. And given his historically poor offensive numbers, it seems like it could be headed that way with McMahon under contract for another year at $16 million. The 31-year-old just has not worked out as a member of the Yankees. His time in pinstripes should come to an end sooner rather than later."
McMahon has one more year on his six-year, $70 million deal. Not having him on the playoff roster would be a tough look. Yet, his bat has struggled, and the Yankees could use Caballero at third, with Volpe as the primary backup infielder in the playoffs.
McMahon is hitting .210 with 10 home runs and 34 RBIs this season.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot and once again have World Series aspirations.
Although New York did clinch a playoff spot, the Yankees know the job is not done.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
The Yankees are set to begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post New York Yankees $70M Infielder Handed Harsh Take Ahead of Playoffs appeared first on HEAVY.

title: #13 Jazz Chisholm Jr's New York Sweet Honeymoon Tune Is Tuning Down After The 2026 Season
author: Natalie Robinson
body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. is one of the most electrifying MLB players around. From his charisma, high energy, confidence, and million-dollar smile, he’s made it clear that being in pinstripes has brought his love for baseball back. His future with the New York Yankees could become one of the biggest questions of the 2026 offseason. The two-time All-Star is scheduled to reach free agency after the season, leaving his future in the Bronx uncertain.
Chisholm has never blended into the background. Since his MLB debut, he has electrified fans with his charismatic personality, bold style, and, most importantly, his explosive play on the field. As the 2026 season draws to a close, all eyes are on this Bahamian superstar —not just for his highlight-reel moments, but for what his future will hold after his 2026 season with the New York Yankees.
Jazz Chisholm Jr.’s Early Career And Rise To MLB Stardom
Chisholm’s journey to the major leagues is a story of perseverance and raw talent. His passion for baseball was evident from an early age. In 2015, he signed with the Arizona Diamondbacks as an international free agent. Showcasing his natural skills, speed, and infectious energy, he caught the attention of the Miami Marlins and made his MLB debut in 2020.
After making his debut, Jazz wasted no time making an impact and electrifying fans. Since his rookie season, he has showcased his potential with his speed and power. His skills did not go unnoticed, earning him an All-Star selection in 2022 and establishing him as one of the game’s most exciting young stars.
The Yankees Era: Highs, Lows, And Star Power
After leaving the Marlins, Chisholm found a renewed sense of happiness when the Yankees acquired him in a blockbuster trade ahead of the 2025 season. They hoped his dynamic skill set would energize their lineup. Once he made it to the Bronx, he immediately brought the fire and flair to the game. His bat speed, base-stealing prowess, and defensive versatility at both second base and center field made him a valuable asset.
Despite the highs, lows, and injuries, Chisholm has made an incredible impact in New York. From his acrobatic plays on the field, clutch home runs in key games, to his swagger and the love from the fans, it is understandable how being in the Bronx gave him back his happiness.
Will Jazz Chisholm Jr. Stay With The Yankees In 2027?
As the 2026 season progressed, rumors began circulating about the Yankees’ roster plans. According to Heavy, recent reports have raised questions about whether the Yankees will bring Chisholm back for 2027. Disappointing to many fans, this development is not entirely surprising. The Yankees are reportedly looking to invest in pitching and have several top prospects ready to debut in the infield and outfield.
If the Yankees ultimately decide not to bring Chisholm back, his time in the Bronx would end after just two seasons. While it marks the end of an era, it also opens the door to new opportunities. His unique skill set, marketability, and ability to energize a franchise make him one of the most sought-after free agents this winter.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. 2026 Yankees Stats
Chisholm may be sidelined at the moment; however, he managed to secure the following stats as a Yankee:
| Stat | 2026 | 
|---|---|
| Batting average | .232 | 
| Home runs | 19 | 
| RBI | 55 | 
| Stolen bases | 40 | 
| OPS | .719 | 
What’s Next For Jazz Chisholm Jr.?
Where will Chisholm go from here? With Chisholm approaching free agency, his future in New York remains uncertain but remains bright. Teams across Major League Baseball value his combination of athleticism, power, and charisma. Whether he lands with a contending team looking for a final piece or a rebuilding franchise seeking a new face, Chisholm’s next chapter promises to be just as exciting as his journey thus far.
End Of My Jazz Chisholm Jr. Rant
Now that the Yankees have punched their way into the postseason, this will be Chisholm’s last chance to make the best of it in New York and try to win a World Series. His career is a testament to rising above expectations and seizing the moment. As the 2026 season concludes, fans and analysts will closely watch his next move, ensuring his star continues to shine brightly in baseball. So I ask the fans: what do you think? Do you think Jazz Chisholm Jr. will remain in New York for 2027, or will the Yankees decide it’s time to move in a different direction?

title: Yankees' Latest Austin Wells Update Won't Shock Anyone
author: Matthew Schmidt
body:
Austin Wells has been a massive liability offensively for the New York Yankees this season, but they have not seemed to care.
The Yankees didn't heavily pursue a catcher at the MLB trade deadline, and it's looking more and more like they will head into 2027 with Wells behind the plate.
Not that that should surprise anyone based on how New York has handled the situation.
Chris Kirschner of The Athletic provided an update on Wells in a recent mailbag, revealing that while the Yankees may try and pursue a platoon bat to pair with Wells this winter, they probably won't make any major changes at catcher.
"Austin Wells is one of the best defenders behind the plate. The Yankees' pitchers fully trust him, and he's a major reason they've had success this season," Kirschner wrote. "Clearly, his offense has nosedived this year. It's frankly shocking. The Yankees will likely be in the market for a platoon partner for Wells for next season. Catching fewer games than he did this year could keep his legs fresher."
Is it really that shocking, though?
Wells slashed .219/.275/.436 last season. Yes, he flashed some pop with 21 home runs, but when he wasn't running into a pitch for a homer, he was barely getting on base.
This year, he is slashing .179/.277/.313. Funny enough, his on-base percentage is actually better than last year thanks to his improved walk rate, but his power (12 home runs and .135 ISO) has declined significantly.
Wells owns a lifetime .212/.289/.392 slash line. He has never been a force offensively. Sure, he calls a good game and he is fine behind the dish, but the idea that Wells is Pudge Rodriguez defensively is pretty ridiculous.
Keeping Wells is fine. He would be a terrific backup. But retaining him as the starter with his .590 OPS this season would be criminal. That's especially considering Ryan Jeffers will be available in free agency.
But as Kirschner noted, the most likely scenario is that the Yankees will try and find a right-handed backstop to alternate with Wells.
The first name that comes to mind in that regard is Tyler Stephenson, who is a far superior hitter to Wells. The problem? Stephenson has actually hit righties (.760 OPS) better than lefties (.701 OPS) throughout his career.
No matter what direction New York proceeds this offseason, it will likely end in Wells remaining the starting catcher.

title: Cody Bellinger Soluciona Un Problema Clave De Los Yankees Que Lastraba Su Alineación Para La Serie Mundial De 2024
author: Esteban Quiñones
body:
NUEVA YORK — La diferencia de tres puntos de Cody Bellinger en el platoon le da a los Yankees una gran ventaja en la alineación para la postemporada de octubre.
Con un balance de 88-64, los Yankees ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada, pero siguen a cinco partidos de los Tampa Bay Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana, cuando quedan 10 partidos de la temporada regular. La clasificación sigue siendo importante. Y también lo es una alineación que tendrá poco margen de error cuando los rivales puedan adaptar sus estrategias de pitcheo para contrarrestarla.
Ahí es donde la postemporada de 2024 sigue siendo un contexto útil. Nueva York llegó a la Serie Mundial antes de caer ante los Dodgers en cinco partidos, pero el jardín izquierdo nunca llegó a ser una fuente fiable de producción tanto ofensiva como defensiva. Alex Verdugo terminó esa temporada regular con un promedio de .233/.291/.356 y un OPS+ de 83, y luego bateó .208/.309/.313 con un OPS de .622 en 14 partidos de postemporada.
El problema duró más de un mes de octubre. Tras la última temporada de Brett Gardner con los Yankees en 2021, el jardín izquierdo pasó a ser una posición rotativa en lugar de un punto fuerte consolidado. Las estadísticas posicionales de FanGraphs sitúan al jardín izquierdo de los Yankees en solo 1,6 fWAR entre 2021 y 2024, lo que lo coloca en el puesto 28 de las Grandes Ligas en ese periodo. Esa trayectoria dejó a Nueva York buscando tanto rendimiento como estabilidad, en lugar de otro parche de una sola temporada en una posición defensiva clave. Por fin, la situación parece haber cambiado.
Bellinger convierte el jardín izquierdo de un compromiso en un punto fuerte
Cody Bellinger es la razón más clara. El miércoles conectó 3 de 5, con una base por bolas, una carrera y una base robada, lo que le ha permitido sumar varios hits en cinco de sus últimos siete partidos. Su racha va más allá de unas cuantas noches de septiembre.
Bellinger ha bateado .340 con cinco jonrones, 18 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 148 en 23 partidos desde que volvió el 23 de agosto tras una distensión de grado 2 en el isquiotibial izquierdo. Al comenzar el viernes, llevaba un promedio de bateo de .276/.351/.444, con 16 jonrones y 71 carreras impulsadas en 125 partidos.
Los Yankees acabaron con un balance de 15-7 en los primeros 22 partidos tras su regreso, batearon .274/.336/.440 como equipo, registraron un diferencial de carreras de +42 y anotaron al menos cinco carreras en 14 ocasiones. Llegaron a las seis carreras en 12 ocasiones y a las siete en nueve. Bellinger ha aportado toda esa potencia ofensiva sin dejar de ser un defensor decisivo.
Sports Info Solutions le atribuye a Bellinger 20 carreras defensivas salvadas en el jardín izquierdo, mientras que Statcast le da seis outs por encima de la media en todo el jardín. Ese valor en ambos aspectos es la diferencia clave con respecto a 2024, y su capacidad para jugar tanto en el jardín central como en primera base aporta a los Yankees una mayor flexibilidad en la plantilla.
Una derrota aplastante dejó claro por qué su bate es tan importante
Los Yankees pudieron comprobar su poder ofensivo durante la derrota por 12-2 ante los Mets el 12 de septiembre en el Yankee Stadium. Bellinger anotó las dos carreras de Nueva York con un sencillo impulsador en la cuarta entrada y un jonrón solitario en la sexta. Era su tercer jonrón en cuatro partidos en ese momento.
Aaron Boone estaba explicando por qué el lanzador titular de los Mets, Zac Thornton, había controlado al resto de la alineación. Ese comentario ponía de manifiesto lo poco que Cody Bellinger había recibido ayuda aquella tarde.
«Está claro que se puso por delante ahí y sus lanzamientos a la zona de strike fueron realmente buenos», dijo Boone.
Desde entonces, el promedio de bateo de Bellinger en septiembre ha subido hasta el 0,390 en 14 partidos, con cuatro jonrones, 12 carreras impulsadas y 14 carreras anotadas. Los Yankees han necesitado esa estabilidad mientras otras partes de la alineación han tenido que adaptarse a las lesiones y a los enfrentamientos.
Una diferencia de tres puntos en el platoon cambia las cuentas de octubre
Quizá la cifra más reveladora sea la que apenas varía. Hasta el miércoles, Bellinger tiene un OPS de 0,797 contra lanzadores zurdos y un OPS de 0,794 contra lanzadores diestros. Esa diferencia de tres puntos le da a los Yankees un bateador en el centro del orden de bateo que no hace falta ocultar cuando los rivales cambian de lanzador.
El panorama del platooning de los Yankees también sitúa a Aaron Judge y Ben Rice entre sus bateadores titulares más equilibrados. Bellinger es otro bateador que puede quedarse en el partido sin que Boone tenga que sacrificar el ataque por la defensa ni la defensa por el ataque, una cualidad muy valiosa cuando, en octubre, los bullpens cambian los enfrentamientos inning tras inning.
El precio original del traspaso solo cuenta la mitad de la historia
Los Yankees ficharon a Bellinger de los Cubs en diciembre de 2024 a cambio del lanzador diestro Cody Poteet, y Chicago también aportó 5 millones de dólares. El precio de ese traspaso sigue siendo impresionante, pero no es el coste total. Después de que Bellinger se convirtiera en agente libre, Nueva York lo volvió a fichar en enero con un contrato de cinco años y 162,5 millones de dólares.
En 2025, sumó 29 jonrones, 98 carreras impulsadas y 4,9 fWAR. El valor que le da FanGraphs para 2026 ronda ahora los cuatro fWAR. Según un cálculo basado en sus estadísticas totales de la MLB durante las dos temporadas con los Yankees , se sitúa en 45 jonrones, 169 carreras impulsadas y un promedio de bateo combinado de aproximadamente .274/.341/.464.
Con la clasificación para la postemporada asegurada y la División Este de la Liga Americana aún en juego, a los Yankees les quedan 10 partidos para pulir su alineación de octubre. El reciente repunte de Bellinger, su rendimiento casi idéntico en el plato y su defensa en el jardín izquierdo aportan a Nueva York algo que su equipo de la Serie Mundial de 2024 nunca tuvo de forma constante en esa posición: un titular que puede seguir formando parte del plan independientemente del rival.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

Bellinger ha bateado .340 con cinco jonrones, 18 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 148 en 23 partidos desde que volvió el 23 de agosto tras una distensión de grado 2 en el isquiotibial izquierdo. Al comenzar el viernes, llevaba un promedio de bateo de .276/.351/.444, con 16 jonrones y 71 carreras impulsadas en 125 partidos.
Los Yankees acabaron con un balance de 15-7 en los primeros 22 partidos tras su regreso, batearon .274/.336/.440 como equipo, registraron un diferencial de carreras de +42 y anotaron al menos cinco carreras en 14 ocasiones. Llegaron a las seis carreras en 12 ocasiones y a las siete en nueve. Bellinger ha aportado toda esa potencia ofensiva sin dejar de ser un defensor decisivo.
Sports Info Solutions le atribuye a Bellinger 20 carreras defensivas salvadas en el jardín izquierdo, mientras que Statcast le da seis outs por encima de la media en todo el jardín. Ese valor en ambos aspectos es la diferencia clave con respecto a 2024, y su capacidad para jugar tanto en el jardín central como en primera base aporta a los Yankees una mayor flexibilidad en la plantilla.
Una derrota aplastante dejó claro por qué su bate es tan importante
Los Yankees pudieron comprobar su poder ofensivo durante la derrota por 12-2 ante los Mets el 12 de septiembre en el Yankee Stadium. Bellinger anotó las dos carreras de Nueva York con un sencillo impulsador en la cuarta entrada y un jonrón solitario en la sexta. Era su tercer jonrón en cuatro partidos en ese momento.
Aaron Boone estaba explicando por qué el lanzador titular de los Mets, Zac Thornton, había controlado al resto de la alineación. Ese comentario ponía de manifiesto lo poco que Cody Bellinger había recibido ayuda aquella tarde.
«Está claro que se puso por delante ahí y sus lanzamientos a la zona de strike fueron realmente buenos», dijo Boone.
Desde entonces, el promedio de bateo de Bellinger en septiembre ha subido hasta el 0,390 en 14 partidos, con cuatro jonrones, 12 carreras impulsadas y 14 carreras anotadas. Los Yankees han necesitado esa estabilidad mientras otras partes de la alineación han tenido que adaptarse a las lesiones y a los enfrentamientos.
Una diferencia de tres puntos en el platoon cambia las cuentas de octubre
Quizá la cifra más reveladora sea la que apenas varía. Hasta el miércoles, Bellinger tiene un OPS de 0,797 contra lanzadores zurdos y un OPS de 0,794 contra lanzadores diestros. Esa diferencia de tres puntos le da a los Yankees un bateador en el centro del orden de bateo que no hace falta ocultar cuando los rivales cambian de lanzador.
El panorama del platooning de los Yankees también sitúa a Aaron Judge y Ben Rice entre sus bateadores titulares más equilibrados. Bellinger es otro bateador que puede quedarse en el partido sin que Boone tenga que sacrificar el ataque por la defensa ni la defensa por el ataque, una cualidad muy valiosa cuando, en octubre, los bullpens cambian los enfrentamientos inning tras inning.
El precio original del traspaso solo cuenta la mitad de la historia
Los Yankees ficharon a Bellinger de los Cubs en diciembre de 2024 a cambio del lanzador diestro Cody Poteet, y Chicago también aportó 5 millones de dólares. El precio de ese traspaso sigue siendo impresionante, pero no es el coste total. Después de que Bellinger se convirtiera en agente libre, Nueva York lo volvió a fichar en enero con un contrato de cinco años y 162,5 millones de dólares.
En 2025, sumó 29 jonrones, 98 carreras impulsadas y 4,9 fWAR. El valor que le da FanGraphs para 2026 ronda ahora los cuatro fWAR. Según un cálculo basado en sus estadísticas totales de la MLB durante las dos temporadas con los Yankees , se sitúa en 45 jonrones, 169 carreras impulsadas y un promedio de bateo combinado de aproximadamente .274/.341/.464.
Con la clasificación para la postemporada asegurada y la División Este de la Liga Americana aún en juego, a los Yankees les quedan 10 partidos para pulir su alineación de octubre. El reciente repunte de Bellinger, su rendimiento casi idéntico en el plato y su defensa en el jardín izquierdo aportan a Nueva York algo que su equipo de la Serie Mundial de 2024 nunca tuvo de forma constante en esa posición: un titular que puede seguir formando parte del plan independientemente del rival.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario más abajo.

title: Ryan McMahon Les Da A Los Yankees Otro Motivo Preocupante Para Replantearse Su Futuro En El Equipo
author: Sara Molnick
body:
PHOENIX — Los Yankees se han pasado todo el mes de septiembre intentando convertir su clasificación para la postemporada en una plantilla más clara de cara a octubre. Una de sus decisiones más difíciles de tomar ahora mismo tiene que ver con la tercera base.
Ryan McMahon llegó como un jugador que aportaba estabilidad sobre todo en defensa, pero cada vez le cuesta más ocultar su bateo. Su último bache se produjo el miércoles en el Target Field, donde se fue de 0 de 6 con cuatro strikeouts en la derrota por 5-4, en 13 entradas, ante los Minnesota Twins.
Los Yankees no dejaron de remontar. Anthony Volpe empató el partido con un doble en la novena entrada. Ali Sánchez puso a Nueva York por delante en la décima, y José Caballero sumó un fly de sacrificio en la undécima. Minnesota respondió en cada ocasión hasta que Víctor Caratini sentenció el partido con un sencillo decisivo en la 13.ª. Tommy Nance se llevó la victoria, John Schreiber la derrota y no hubo salvamento.
McMahon, que bateaba séptimo, terminó la noche con un promedio de .210/.275/.346, 10 jonrones y 34 carreras impulsadas en 118 partidos. Se ha puesto a cero 101 veces, lo que supone un porcentaje del 29,2 %, mientras que su OPS es de .621. Las estadísticas avanzadas actuales que acompañan a las críticas le sitúan en un wRC+ de 77 y un fWAR de 0,5.
Este momento hace que cada turno al bate sin resultado se note más. Los Yankees llegaban al viernes con un balance de 88-64, a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con la clasificación para la postemporada ya asegurada. Jazz Chisholm Jr. sigue en la lista de lesionados de 10 días por un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Volpe ha vuelto de la Triple A y ha jugado como segunda base.
La trayectoria de Volpe en las ligas menores ha ampliado las opciones de los Yankees. Durante su etapa en la Triple A, jugó como shortstop, segunda base y tercera base. Eso no significa que sea la solución definitiva para la tercera base, pero le da a Aaron Boone otra opción de alineación que tener en cuenta cuando vuelva Chisholm.
McMahon también tiene un sueldo garantizado de 16 millones de dólares para 2027. Los Yankees tienen que decidir si su defensa y su contrato siguen justificando que sea titular cuando la diferencia en ataque se ha vuelto tan grande.
McMahon entra en la zona de peligro de LeMahieu
Esa combinación ha hecho que cada vez más gente de los Yankees se plantee una pregunta más dura: si McMahon debería perder su puesto de titular, quedar fuera de la plantilla de la postemporada o, al final, ser designado para cesión.
La comparación que está cobrando fuerza es la de DJ LeMahieu, a quien los Yankees dejaron libre en julio de 2025 cuando aún le quedaban por cobrar unos 22 millones de dólares. Según FanGraphs, en su última temporada con los Yankees, LeMahieu registró un wRC+ de 94, un porcentaje de embasado de 0,338 y una tasa de strikeouts del 24,6 %.
McMahon está por debajo de todos esos indicadores ofensivos. Su porcentaje de llegada a base de 0,275 y su tasa de strikeouts del 29,2 % hacen que los Yankees obtengan menos aportación ofensiva de la que recibían de LeMahieu antes de decidir que ya no encajaba en su plantilla.
Las situaciones no son iguales. LeMahieu tenía 36 años, su papel se había reducido y Nueva York quería a Chisholm en segunda base. McMahon es más joven y sigue aportando valor en tercera base. Pero la decisión sobre LeMahieu dejó claro que el dinero garantizado no siempre protege el puesto de un veterano en la plantilla.
Boone sigue centrándose en el grupo
Los Yankees no han dicho públicamente que McMahon vaya a quedar fuera de la plantilla. Tras asegurarse el título, Boone habló de cómo el vestuario había afrontado una temporada difícil, en lugar de dar a entender que se hubiera tomado ninguna decisión sobre un veterano.
«Pero hay que reconocerles el mérito de haberse mantenido unidos. A pesar de todos los altibajos, han sido un grupo muy unido», dijo Boone.
Ese comentario no aclara cuál será el papel de McMahon en octubre. Lo que sí hace es resaltar la diferencia entre las presiones externas para que lo echen y la decisión que los Yankees hayan tomado realmente.
La defensa ya no es la respuesta definitiva
El argumento más sólido de McMahon sigue siendo su guante. La instantánea que te he pasado muestra un DRS de -1 y un Fielding Run Value de +1, mientras que la página en directo de Statcast muestra un valor defensivo global ligeramente positivo. La cifra exacta varía según la métrica y el momento de la actualización, pero la ventaja defensiva no oculta un OPS de 0,621.
Un tercera base con un OPS de 0,621 puede seguir siendo una opción válida si su defensa es de primera y el resto de la alineación está en forma. Los Yankees tienen menos margen mientras Chisholm esté de baja, y en octubre cada puesto de la alineación cobra más importancia.
Volpe no es un tercera base contrastado en las Grandes Ligas, y los Yankees no han dado a entender que tengan pensado darle esa posición. Aun así, su reciente actuación en esa posición en la Triple A le da a Boone una alternativa real. Su experiencia como campocorto hace que la objeción sobre la potencia de su brazo no sea tan sencilla, pero eso no garantiza que vaya a defender bien la tercera base en octubre.
La comparación de Okamoto hay que ponerla en contexto
Otra comparación que circula entre los aficionados de los Yankees compara a McMahon con el tercera base de Toronto, Kazuma Okamoto. Según la MLB, Okamoto tiene un promedio de bateo de 0,235, con 33 jonrones, 88 carreras impulsadas y un OPS de 0,774. Su contrato de cuatro años y 60 millones de dólares tiene un valor medio anual de 15 millones de dólares.
McMahon gana 16 millones de dólares y lleva 10 jonrones con un OPS de 0,621. A primera vista, el contraste es enorme.
No se trata de una decisión de la directiva en la que se pueda comparar a uno con otro sin más. McMahon ya tenía contrato cuando los Yankees lo ficharon en 2025, mientras que Okamoto llegó a la MLB siguiendo un camino diferente como agente libre. Aun así, la comparación salarial ayuda a entender por qué se han intensificado las críticas y por qué algunas de ellas se han extendido hasta el director general, Brian Cashman.
Octubre obliga a los Yankees a decidirse por un papel
No hay indicios confirmados de que los Yankees hayan decidido designar a McMahon para cesión o sacarlo de la plantilla de la postemporada. Sigue en activo, y la incertidumbre sobre la fecha de regreso de Chisholm hace que la situación en el cuadro siga siendo incierta.
Pero la cuestión ya no es si McMahon está pasando por una mala racha. Es cuánto tiempo de juego pueden permitirse los Yankees darle a un bateador con un wRC+ de 77 cuando empiece octubre.
Nueva York comienza este viernes una serie de tres partidos en el Chase Field contra Arizona. McMahon tiene tiempo para cambiar el rumbo, pero los Yankees ahora tienen menos margen de maniobra y más alternativas en el cuadro que hace un mes.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

Ali Sánchez puso a Nueva York por delante en la décima, y José Caballero sumó un fly de sacrificio en la undécima. Minnesota respondió en cada ocasión hasta que Víctor Caratini sentenció el partido con un sencillo decisivo en la 13.ª. Tommy Nance se llevó la victoria, John Schreiber la derrota y no hubo salvamento.
McMahon, que bateaba séptimo, terminó la noche con un promedio de .210/.275/.346, 10 jonrones y 34 carreras impulsadas en 118 partidos. Se ha puesto a cero 101 veces, lo que supone un porcentaje del 29,2 %, mientras que su OPS es de .621. Las estadísticas avanzadas actuales que acompañan a las críticas le sitúan en un wRC+ de 77 y un fWAR de 0,5.
Este momento hace que cada turno al bate sin resultado se note más. Los Yankees llegaban al viernes con un balance de 88-64, a cinco partidos de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, con la clasificación para la postemporada ya asegurada. Jazz Chisholm Jr. sigue en la lista de lesionados de 10 días por un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Volpe ha vuelto de la Triple A y ha jugado como segunda base.
La trayectoria de Volpe en las ligas menores ha ampliado las opciones de los Yankees. Durante su etapa en la Triple A, jugó como shortstop, segunda base y tercera base. Eso no significa que sea la solución definitiva para la tercera base, pero le da a Aaron Boone otra opción de alineación que tener en cuenta cuando vuelva Chisholm.
McMahon también tiene un sueldo garantizado de 16 millones de dólares para 2027. Los Yankees tienen que decidir si su defensa y su contrato siguen justificando que sea titular cuando la diferencia en ataque se ha vuelto tan grande.
McMahon entra en la zona de peligro de LeMahieu
Esa combinación ha hecho que cada vez más gente de los Yankees se plantee una pregunta más dura: si McMahon debería perder su puesto de titular, quedar fuera de la plantilla de la postemporada o, al final, ser designado para cesión.
La comparación que está cobrando fuerza es la de DJ LeMahieu, a quien los Yankees dejaron libre en julio de 2025 cuando aún le quedaban por cobrar unos 22 millones de dólares. Según FanGraphs, en su última temporada con los Yankees, LeMahieu registró un wRC+ de 94, un porcentaje de embasado de 0,338 y una tasa de strikeouts del 24,6 %.
McMahon está por debajo de todos esos indicadores ofensivos. Su porcentaje de llegada a base de 0,275 y su tasa de strikeouts del 29,2 % hacen que los Yankees obtengan menos aportación ofensiva de la que recibían de LeMahieu antes de decidir que ya no encajaba en su plantilla.
Las situaciones no son iguales. LeMahieu tenía 36 años, su papel se había reducido y Nueva York quería a Chisholm en segunda base. McMahon es más joven y sigue aportando valor en tercera base. Pero la decisión sobre LeMahieu dejó claro que el dinero garantizado no siempre protege el puesto de un veterano en la plantilla.
Boone sigue centrándose en el grupo
Los Yankees no han dicho públicamente que McMahon vaya a quedar fuera de la plantilla. Tras asegurarse el título, Boone habló de cómo el vestuario había afrontado una temporada difícil, en lugar de dar a entender que se hubiera tomado ninguna decisión sobre un veterano.
«Pero hay que reconocerles el mérito de haberse mantenido unidos. A pesar de todos los altibajos, han sido un grupo muy unido», dijo Boone.
Ese comentario no aclara cuál será el papel de McMahon en octubre. Lo que sí hace es resaltar la diferencia entre las presiones externas para que lo echen y la decisión que los Yankees hayan tomado realmente.
La defensa ya no es la respuesta definitiva
El argumento más sólido de McMahon sigue siendo su guante. La instantánea que te he pasado muestra un DRS de -1 y un Fielding Run Value de +1, mientras que la página en directo de Statcast muestra un valor defensivo global ligeramente positivo. La cifra exacta varía según la métrica y el momento de la actualización, pero la ventaja defensiva no oculta un OPS de 0,621.
Un tercera base con un OPS de 0,621 puede seguir siendo una opción válida si su defensa es de primera y el resto de la alineación está en forma. Los Yankees tienen menos margen mientras Chisholm esté de baja, y en octubre cada puesto de la alineación cobra más importancia.
Volpe no es un tercera base contrastado en las Grandes Ligas, y los Yankees no han dado a entender que tengan pensado darle esa posición. Aun así, su reciente actuación en esa posición en la Triple A le da a Boone una alternativa real. Su experiencia como campocorto hace que la objeción sobre la potencia de su brazo no sea tan sencilla, pero eso no garantiza que vaya a defender bien la tercera base en octubre.
La comparación de Okamoto hay que ponerla en contexto
Otra comparación que circula entre los aficionados de los Yankees compara a McMahon con el tercera base de Toronto, Kazuma Okamoto. Según la MLB, Okamoto tiene un promedio de bateo de 0,235, con 33 jonrones, 88 carreras impulsadas y un OPS de 0,774. Su contrato de cuatro años y 60 millones de dólares tiene un valor medio anual de 15 millones de dólares.
McMahon gana 16 millones de dólares y lleva 10 jonrones con un OPS de 0,621. A primera vista, el contraste es enorme.
No se trata de una decisión de la directiva en la que se pueda comparar a uno con otro sin más. McMahon ya tenía contrato cuando los Yankees lo ficharon en 2025, mientras que Okamoto llegó a la MLB siguiendo un camino diferente como agente libre. Aun así, la comparación salarial ayuda a entender por qué se han intensificado las críticas y por qué algunas de ellas se han extendido hasta el director general, Brian Cashman.
Octubre obliga a los Yankees a decidirse por un papel
No hay indicios confirmados de que los Yankees hayan decidido designar a McMahon para cesión o sacarlo de la plantilla de la postemporada. Sigue en activo, y la incertidumbre sobre la fecha de regreso de Chisholm hace que la situación en el cuadro siga siendo incierta.
Pero la cuestión ya no es si McMahon está pasando por una mala racha. Es cuánto tiempo de juego pueden permitirse los Yankees darle a un bateador con un wRC+ de 77 cuando empiece octubre.
Nueva York comienza este viernes una serie de tres partidos en el Chase Field contra Arizona. McMahon tiene tiempo para cambiar el rumbo, pero los Yankees ahora tienen menos margen de maniobra y más alternativas en el cuadro que hace un mes.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

title: Gerrit Cole has a Yankees start that matters more than it looks
author: Alexander Wilson
body:
Friday night in Arizona is not a playoff game. Gerrit Cole does not need to turn it into one.
But the Yankees are 88-64, they have already punched their postseason ticket, and their next start gives them something September rarely offers: a chance to watch their ace work without the standings screaming at every pitch. Cole is listed to face Eduardo Rodriguez in the opener of the Diamondbacks series.
For me, the useful part is not whether he gets the win. I want to see Gerrit Cole work through a settled routine.
The Yankees need the boring version of this start
Cole does not have to rack up 10 strikeouts or carry a no-hitter into the seventh. The Yankees need crisp work, clean recovery between innings, and the kind of outing that makes a manager's postseason decisions less complicated.
That may sound less fun than a big velocity reading or a gaudy line, but this is where the club is. There is no prize for treating every September start like a referendum. The value is getting Cole through a normal workload and having him leave Arizona feeling like he has another ordinary start coming.
Arizona is a better check than it seems
The Diamondbacks are 80-73 and still playing for something. A road game at 9:40 p.m. Eastern against a capable opponent is not a controlled tune-up, either. It will ask for the normal concentration, pitch execution, and in-game adjustment that October will demand.
I would not overreact to one rough inning, especially with the schedule nearly finished. I also would not dismiss a sharp one. The Yankees have enough arms and enough moving parts that every clean Cole outing gives the club one less thing to worry about when the games finally tighten up.

Cole's line will matter. His rhythm will matter more.

title: Don Mattingly Makes Honest Statement on Phillies Unfortunate Injury News
author: Cole Sullivan
body:
The Philadelphia Phillies opened a series with the New York Mets on Thursday night and won the game 3-0 to improve to 85-68 overall.
However, in spite of the victory, the team dealt with a notable injury out of their bullpen to right-handed reliever Jonathan Bowlan, who has been a workhorse for the Phillies this year.
He exited the eighth inning after recording two strikeouts with a reported groin strain.
Don Mattingly Makes Honest Statement on Injury
While it’s still unknown exactly the extent of the injury and how long Bowlan may be out, Phillies interim manager Don Mattingly made an honest statement after losing a key arm out of the pen.
“Paul said right groin tightness, so we’ll reevaluate tomorrow to see where he’s at,” Mattingly said. “We’ll talk about it more tomorrow but at this point you just… I don’t want to be cold hearted but you got to move on and you have to find a way to fill that spot. Which is not necessarily easy to do, but that means other guys got to step up, that’s all.”
“That means other guys got to step up, that’s all.”
Don Mattingly says other arms will need to rise to the occasion if Jonathan Bowlan misses time. pic.twitter.com/5FnoNJ2Mjv
— NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) September 18, 2026
Bowlan’s 2026 Season
In his fourth MLB season, but first with the Phillies after spending the last three years with the Kansas City Royals, Bowlan has been one of the best arms out of Philadelphia’s pen.
He’s appeared in 59 games, and across 56.1 innings pitched, he holds a 2-2 record with a 3.36 ERA, 73 strikeouts, and two saves.
Looking at the Phillies
Philadelphia is still trying to chase the Atlanta Braves in the NL East, trailing them by 4.0 games with nine regular-season games remaining.
The Phillies also want the top Wild Card spot, which would give them home-field advantage in a best-of-three Wild Card Series, but they remain tied with the Chicago Cubs for that spot.

title: Schlittler, Rice more than just most valuable Yanks, they're indispensable
author: Mike Lupica
body:
The two most valuable Yankees this season are a starting pitcher named Cam Schlittler, from Walpole, Mass., and Northeastern University, a school within walking distance of Fenway Park, and Ben Rice, who comes out of Cohasset, Mass., on the state’s South Shore, about 30 miles from Fenway. If the Yankees are hosting a Wild Card Series against the Red Sox in less than two weeks -- at Yankee Stadium and not Fenway -- Schlittler and Rice will be the biggest reasons.
Schlittler ought to win the AL Cy Young Award and ought to be an MVP candidate for the whole league. David Cone, now a Yankees broadcaster for the YES network and once a great Yankee himself, has one word to describe what he’s seen from Schlittler this season:
“Nails.”
Here’s a breakdown of Schlittler’s ERA, month by month after one start in March, when, of course, he threw a shutout (eight strikeouts) into the sixth inning against the Giants:
1.73 in April
1.48 in May
3.38 in June
1.93 in July
2.33 in August
0.86 so far in September
Carlos Rodón got hurt. Max Fried got hurt. Gerrit Cole joined the season late, and he hasn’t looked like his own Cy Young self lately. It is been Schlittler who has been the Yankees' ace, who is their Game 1 guy, who has carried the staff. He is not going to end up with a 25-3 record and an ERA of 1.74 the way Ron Guidry did nearly 50 years ago. But Schlittler is at 14-6 with a 1.95 ERA going into his last few starts of the regular season. He has been the first young power starter out of the Yankees’ system since Guidry to be this good, and this dominant.
But Rice has been just as important to their offense.
In a season when Aaron Judge was gone for more than 80 games because of a fracture to his rib cage. Then, after Judge finally got back into the lineup and even hit his first home run in months, he left a game against the Twins the other day because of pain in his lower leg. It is why you have to believe, if and when Judge is back in the lineup again, he’s going to be a swing and a prayer the rest of the way.
So No. 99 went away. So did Cody Bellinger, the Yankees’ second-most important hitter a year ago, before he finally returned from the IL. But even when the Yankees struggled to score runs, and even in a roller-coaster year that saw Rice hit just .196 in June and .184 in August, it is Rice who has been the Yankees' hitting star, coming into a weekend series against the Diamondbacks with 38 home runs and still with a chance to knock in 100.
Luis García Jr. showed up from the Nationals at the Trade Deadline to give him some backup. Bellinger has been on a heater since coming off the IL, with five homers, 18 RBIs and a .344 average over his last 22 games. But it was Rice around whom the Yankees built what offense they had before all that, while they were staying ahead of the Red Sox and at least maintaining contact with the Rays.
You know how many homegrown Yankees have hit 40 or more home runs in a season in the last 75 years? Two. One was named Mickey Mantle and the other is Judge. There have been other Yankees sluggers who got to 40 and beyond. Alex Rodriguez once made it all the way to 57. But they all came from somewhere else. Rice is the same as Schlittler: He hasn’t just come to this moment from New England, he’s someone the Yankees drafted in the 12th round of the 2021 Draft (Schlittler was out of the seventh round the following year).
Alfonso Soriano made his own run at 40 more than 20 years ago. Did it twice. But Soriano came to the Yankees as a free agent from Japan. So think about the company Rice will be keeping if does get to 40 homers, starting with his chance this weekend against the Diamondbacks:
Mantle. Judge.
Here is something Rice’s manager, Aaron Boone, has said about him:
"I got my first taste of him in Spring Training of '24, and it was like, 'Oh, OK.' But then this year, it's gone to even another level.”
Here is something else:
“I think he's turning into one of the best hitters in the league."
Rice himself has predictably low-keyed what he’s done for the Yankees so far.
"The year is still in progress, you know?” he said. “It's still going on. We've got more games to play and a long road ahead, so I can't really look back and assess it fully yet."
It really has been a roller-coaster ride occasionally. He has struggled occasionally against left-handed pitchers, but his season-long average against them stands at .254 with 10 home runs and 29 RBIs.
We know what Schlittler’s numbers are. Rice’s, though, can get a little lost sometimes. But in a year where he’s batted everywhere from leadoff to cleanup, when Judge was gone for more than half the time, he has been indispensable, too. And still has a shot to be a 40-homer guy for the Yankees.

It is why you have to believe, if and when Judge is back in the lineup again, he’s going to be a swing and a prayer the rest of the way.
So No. 99 went away. So did Cody Bellinger, the Yankees’ second-most important hitter a year ago, before he finally returned from the IL. But even when the Yankees struggled to score runs, and even in a roller-coaster year that saw Rice hit just .196 in June and .184 in August, it is Rice who has been the Yankees' hitting star, coming into a weekend series against the Diamondbacks with 38 home runs and still with a chance to knock in 100.
Luis García Jr. showed up from the Nationals at the Trade Deadline to give him some backup. Bellinger has been on a heater since coming off the IL, with five homers, 18 RBIs and a .344 average over his last 22 games. But it was Rice around whom the Yankees built what offense they had before all that, while they were staying ahead of the Red Sox and at least maintaining contact with the Rays.
You know how many homegrown Yankees have hit 40 or more home runs in a season in the last 75 years? Two. One was named Mickey Mantle and the other is Judge. There have been other Yankees sluggers who got to 40 and beyond. Alex Rodriguez once made it all the way to 57. But they all came from somewhere else. Rice is the same as Schlittler: He hasn’t just come to this moment from New England, he’s someone the Yankees drafted in the 12th round of the 2021 Draft (Schlittler was out of the seventh round the following year).
Alfonso Soriano made his own run at 40 more than 20 years ago. Did it twice. But Soriano came to the Yankees as a free agent from Japan. So think about the company Rice will be keeping if does get to 40 homers, starting with his chance this weekend against the Diamondbacks:
Mantle. Judge.
Here is something Rice’s manager, Aaron Boone, has said about him:
"I got my first taste of him in Spring Training of '24, and it was like, 'Oh, OK.' But then this year, it's gone to even another level.”
Here is something else:
“I think he's turning into one of the best hitters in the league."
Rice himself has predictably low-keyed what he’s done for the Yankees so far.
"The year is still in progress, you know?” he said. “It's still going on. We've got more games to play and a long road ahead, so I can't really look back and assess it fully yet."
It really has been a roller-coaster ride occasionally. He has struggled occasionally against left-handed pitchers, but his season-long average against them stands at .254 with 10 home runs and 29 RBIs.
We know what Schlittler’s numbers are. Rice’s, though, can get a little lost sometimes. But in a year where he’s batted everywhere from leadoff to cleanup, when Judge was gone for more than half the time, he has been indispensable, too. And still has a shot to be a 40-homer guy for the Yankees.

title: Why it's 'hard to argue' against Spencer Jones in Yankees center field battle
author: Conor Liguori
body:
Why it's 'hard to argue' against Spencer Jones in Yankees center field battle originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The New York Yankees appear to be locked in as the AL's first Wild Card seed.
With just a trio of regular season series remaining, the Yankees and their coaching staff/front office should be thinking about how they'll fill out the postseason roster.
One topic of discussion will almost certainly be who is starting in center field.
Bleacher Report's Kerry Miller believes it should be rookie Spencer Jones over the currently injured Trent Grisham.
"Though he hasn't come close to matching the 35 HR, 29 SB, .932 OPS line he posted in the minors in 2025, it's hard to argue with the .802 OPS he's posted since the beginning of June," Miller wrote about Jones. "Even if Grisham is healthy heading into October, Jones might be New York's primary CF in the postseason."
Jones stands out above Grisham for two reasons:
First, he's hitting .362 in 47 at-bats with runners in scoring position. That could be incredibly valuable for the Yankees in October.
Plus, Jones has more than proven that he can handle left-handers, hitting .435 with three home runs and 12 RBIs in 46 at-bats against southpaws.
Grisham's Grade 2 hamstring strain certainly complicates his return, given the Yankees probably want the freshest players on the field.
And Grisham regressed significantly on offense (.211/.308/.395, .703 OPS) after swatting 34 home runs with an .811 OPS in 2025.
Based on recent results and the health of the two players, Jones seems like the clear choice for manager Aaron Boone.

title: Yankees Make Cam Schlittler Announcement on Friday
author: Simeon Kotto
body:
Some New York Yankees fans had been wondering if the team would start to limit Cam Schlittler’s innings or even potentially skip one of his remaining starts with the playoffs in view, but it doesn’t appear that the Yankees are planning on that. At least for now.
The Yankees have locked in their starting pitchers for this weekend’s three-game series in Arizona, and the headline assignment is Schlittler taking the ball Saturday against the Diamondbacks, via MLB.com.
With the club already in the postseason but still chasing both the American League East title and the top Wild Card seed, every start carries extra weight.
Manager Aaron Boone’s staff listed Gerrit Cole for Friday, Schlittler for Saturday, and Will Warren for Sunday, setting up a rotation that showcases the team’s depth heading into the final stretch.
Schlittler’s outing is the one that stands out. The right-hander has been the anchor of New York’s staff all year, posting a 14-6 record with a 1.95 ERA and 228 strikeouts.
Those numbers have made him the clear favorite for the American League Cy Young Award and, in the view of many around the league, the best pitcher in baseball this season … although he has already racked up 184.2 innings. He will face Arizona’s Brandon Pfaadt, who enters with a 7-3 mark and a 3.77 ERA.
The contrast is sharp: a dominant, high-strikeout ace against a solid but far less overwhelming counterpart.
The Yankees’ pitching staff as a whole has been exceptional. Their 3.19 team ERA ranks first in the majors, and they lead the league in fewest earned runs and runs allowed.
They have done it despite injuries that forced constant adjustments. Schlittler’s consistency has allowed Boone to manage the rest of the rotation with an eye toward October.
After this series, the club expects to have Max Fried and Carlos Rodón lined up for Tuesday’s doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays, with Cole and Schlittler available later in that set.
Sunday’s starter, Will Warren, has quietly put together a strong campaign of his own (10-6, 3.89 ERA). How Boone uses him in the postseason—whether as a fifth starter or a high-leverage reliever—will be one of the more interesting decisions of the coming weeks.
For now, the immediate focus is this weekend in the desert. Friday’s matchup pits Cole against Eduardo Rodriguez, Sunday features Warren opposite Corbin Burnes, and Saturday belongs to Schlittler.
The Yankees know the Diamondbacks can be dangerous at home, but they also know they possess one of the strongest rotations in the sport.
Giving the ball to Schlittler on Saturday is both a statement of confidence and a practical move. It also demonstrates that New York is not concerned about his workload.
If he continues to pitch the way he has all season, the Yanks will take another step toward securing home-field advantage and heading into October with its best possible alignment. The series begins Friday night. All eyes will be on Saturday.
